clusters.architecture_notes: parse_with_prelude_enums builds a tree-sitter CST and hands it to one `Lowering<'a>` struct. That struct is a single ~5,700-line impl in ts_parser.rs. It holds the source, the output `declarations`, a RefCell<Vec<ParseError>> error sink, and three pass-1 lookup tables (known_enums, namespace_bindings, entity_bindings), which lower_source_file's first pass fills and nothing writes after that. Pass 2 is a string-keyed `match child.kind()` per container: lower_source_file at top level, lower_member for member kinds, plus separate per-body loops in lower_members, lower_guarded_block, lower_trait_members, lower_purpose_members, lower_specialization_body_members, lower_port_body, lower_connect_body and lower_constraint_def. Lowering an expression takes &self only (lower_expr and what it calls, about lines 4260-5877). There are three fault-handling mechanisms. `check_and_lower!` refuses a subtree before lowering it, via refuse_if_faulty. lower_function_checked runs the inner lowering for its diagnostics, discards the result, and adds a backstop message only if the inner pass said nothing. lower_enum and lower_type_args_from_node report the fault and keep the partial AST. diagnose_error_node, whose CST-walking half lives in the fault_diagnosis.rs satellite, handles direct ERROR children. Member-continuation ambiguity (INV-SF-7 for clean parses) is a separate post-lowering pass: member_continuation.rs walks hand-listed container kinds, and a test-side re-lexer of grammar.js guards that list. Every production consumer (reify-cli, mcp_context, the GUI engine, the LSP's published path, module_dag) returns before compiling when `parsed.errors` is non-empty (documented in reify-compiler compile_builder/pre_pass.rs::forward_parse_errors). So INV-SF-7's safety half reduces to one module-level property: root.has_error() implies errors is non-empty. Nothing enforces that property today. tree-sitter-reify/src/node-types.json, which gives the exact child-kind set of every container, is generated on every build, and no crate reads it.

clusters.architecture_notes: Generic instantiation has one shared Type walker, type_resolution.rs::substitute_type_params, plus its expression twin substitute_expr_result_types. Both are exhaustive, and their duplication with the other Type walkers is already owned by S7 λ #8638. What is NOT shared is the step before the walk: turning (declared type params, supplied args, declared defaults) into an arity verdict and a sigma map. That binding step is re-implemented at about ten sites, each with its own arity policy, message and DiagnosticCode. Sites that build or apply a sigma: expr.rs::instantiate_call_return_type (4 callers since #8232), the empty-collection push-down and match binder_subst inside expr.rs::compile_expr_guarded_with_expected_inner, variant_construct.rs (unify over payloads), compile_builder/entities_phase.rs::check_expr_fn_calls (re-unify), compile_builder/auto_type_param_phase.rs::phase_auto_type_param_resolution (monomorph sigma), type_resolution.rs::normalize_type_guarded (projection), resolve_parameterized_alias and the nested-alias arm of resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst (TypeExpr-level alias sigma), and entity.rs::check_type_param_bounds (positional effective args). Type expressions are resolved by two full TypeExpr resolvers. resolve_type_expr_with_aliases_kinded resolves direct spellings and resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst resolves parametric alias bodies. They share only resolve_entity_name_with_shadowing, and since #6477 that includes the applied-form arms. Monomorphization of generic structures exists only inside the auto: resolution phase. It clones the target TopologyTemplate and substitutes a hand-picked subset of its fields. The resolved user-fn call is lowered to CompiledExprKind::UserFunctionCall { function_name, args }, which carries neither the chosen overload nor its type arguments. So the compile-time post-pass (check_expr_fn_calls) and eval (reify-expr find_matching_compiled_function) each re-resolve the overload and re-derive the binding. Key state: the sigma HashMap<String, Type> is always a transient local, never recorded on the IR. The three ambient thread-local resolution scopes are already owned by #8643, and CompilationScope's 30 pub(crate) fields by #8650.

The subsystems that compensate (eval-side, plus the compiler's own post-pass), and the guarantee the compiler fails to give each:
- reify-expr (eval) re-resolves user-fn overloads in find_matching_compiled_function, keeping its own tie-break policy and a long agreement doc. clusters.architecture_notes: Four entry drivers (build_with_geometry_output, build_snapshot, tessellate_from_values, distance_between_placed) each walk templates and call the receiver-less Engine::execute_realization_ops. That executor short-circuits through probe_realization_cache, or else runs compile_geometry_op → dispatcher::dispatch → an optional conversion recipe → kernel.execute for each op, then terminal VolumeMesh/Voxel conversions. Per-realization results go back to the caller as out-parameters and the small ExecutedRealization struct. Per-op facts about GeometryOp variants have five encodings: the reify-ir GEOMETRY_OP_DESCRIPTORS table (operation, parent_role), exhaustive matches (compiled_geometry_op_to_operation), role-then-inner-OR-match functions with unreachable! tails (parent_handles_for_op, substitute_op_parents), a catch-all match backed by a strum test (classify_op_input_reprs), and per-kind (kind, fn) dispatch tables (`*_COMPILERS`) whose length is locked to a hand-written XKind::ALL in reify-compiler. Engine-scoped state that spans builds: RealizationCache<KernelHandle> (value = bare terminal handle), volume_mesh_sources (meshed-from records, added by #6308 so a cache-served VolumeMesh resolves its egress body), realization_projection_store and morph_source. Per-build state, reset by reset_per_build_state's exhaustive destructure: topology_attribute_table (KernelHandle-keyed), swept_kind_table (bare GeometryHandleId-keyed) and realization_handles (bare id). Within one realization the executor holds lockstep Vec<GeometryHandleId>/Vec<ReprKind> (realization_step_ids/realization_step_reprs). Across realizations it holds named_steps: HashMap<String, KernelHandle> plus a sibling named_step_reprs: HashMap<String, ReprKind>, and module_named_steps snapshots only the handles. After each template, Build and BuildSnapshot run post-processes including redispatch_geometry_consuming_compute_nodes. That function scans every compute node of the graph once per template and uses `realization_inputs.is_empty()` as its 'not yet redispatched' latch. Kernel ownership is carried on KernelHandle through step_handles and named_steps. It is lost at the value boundary (Value::GeometryHandle.kernel_handle: Option<GeometryHandleId>) and in realization_handles/swept_kind_table, and kernel_owner.rs falls back to the default kernel when the owner is not a map key. S10 ι₃–ι₆ (#8992–#8998), S2 ε #9157 and #6366 already own those ownership seams. realization_staleness.rs (new this window) is pure functions over the graph and is healthy apart from the already-filed reverse-index mirror.

clusters.architecture_notes: Three cell-walk drivers share the Engine: Engine::eval (engine_eval.rs, ~2,030 lines), Engine::eval_cached (~1,560 lines plus dispatch_merged_cluster_solve_cached, ~316 lines), and Engine::edit_param / Engine::edit_source (engine_edit.rs). Per-cell writes go through cell_commit.rs::commit_cell_result when a caller opts in. Contexts come from cell_eval_ctx.rs::cell_eval_ctx or the optional eval_ctx_with_meta builder. Answers to the three questions: (1) there is no single cell-evaluation walk parameterised by mode. eval and eval_cached are two drivers held together by 42 mirror/parity comments inside eval_cached and by differential tests. S4 unifies the per-cell step (η elaborate_cell with CellPass), solve write-back (ζ), detectors (κ) and guarded activation (ι), but leaves both drivers in place, and eval_cached still falls back to a cold eval() for any module with guarded groups (#5240, out of S4 scope). (2) Journal-leg attribution is restated per site today. The engine_edit module-doc roster needed three comment-only #6231 fixes. S4 closes this with β (#8859, typed CommitTag), row E6 (Started constructed only in cell_commit.rs) and ζ (#8867, WritebackPolicy replaces the roster). (3) deps.rs's reverse index and trace map are separate builds today. S3 δ (#8691) makes the reverse index DependencyGraph::reverse(), an inversion with no node-kind knowledge of its own, so reverse == transpose holds by construction. Outside deps.rs, though, engine_eval.rs::CellReadIndex keeps its own forward walk (read_closure) and a separately built, memoised reverse map (cells_reaching), and resolve_order.rs and engine_fixpoint.rs keep further walks; none of these is in S3's scope. edit_source is still present with no production caller (engine_edit.rs:3047) and still received window fixes (#6373, #6423, #7114); S4 δ #8862 deletes it. Production reach of eval_cached is narrow: its only caller, reify-lsp diagnostics.rs::compute_diagnostics_with_state, calls it only when content_hash is unchanged, on a solver-free and kernel-free Engine, and never edits params. Under those inputs every cell with a cache entry is re-served.

clusters.architecture_notes:
Each compute target is a free function `fn(&[Value], realization_inputs, prior_warm_state, &CancellationHandle) -> ComputeOutcome`. It is registered by string in compute_targets/mod.rs::register_compute_fns and dispatched by engine_compute.rs::Engine.run_compute_dispatch. That function caches a Completed value into the output cells (and persists it for PERSISTABLE_TARGETS), while a Failed outcome marks the cell failed (engine_eval.rs). Every trampoline decodes its stdlib inputs from `Value` by hand and builds its result `StructureInstance` by hand. Support/boundary-condition realization is done separately in each trampoline.
- modal_ops::build_dirichlet_bcs works on the six box-face names x_min…z_max with a kind-aware FaceCompany rule.
- elastic_static::any_support_targets/SYNTHETIC_CLAMP_FACE handles the "root" string on the dims path, and elastic_static::target_node_set does a kind-blind union clamp over resolved handles on the realized path.
- buckling.rs discards supports and hard-codes a z-axis pin-pin.
- reify_solver_elastic::shell_solve calls build_support_bcs(Fixed, Shell) on a synthesized root.

Failure posture is split by family. elastic_static, shell_extract and multi_case return Failed on an Error. Every modal-family error returns Completed with a degenerate value: modal_ops has 13 Completed constructions, 0 Failed and 12 Diagnostic::error. Result echo fields (ModalResult.boundary_conditions/damping) are copied from options by each builder, independently of what the solve actually applied. The multi-case targets emit `Value::Map{"cases"}` although .ri declares MultiCaseResult/MultiCaseBucklingResult structures, and the GUI recognizes them by sniffing for the key. The planned S15 (#8674/#8679/#8683/#8693), S16 (#9119/#9120/#9121) and coordinate-target (SolveBoundary) work unifies DECODE into one SupportSpec. REALIZATION stays per trampoline, and each of those PRDs extends a different realization site.

clusters.cross_system_notes:
Two upstream gaps drive patching here.
(1) reify-compute-contract::ComputeOutcome does not enforce the property its own docs state ('Completed.diagnostics are non-fatal'). Downstream modal trampolines therefore re-detect upstream failure from the shape of the value: modal_result_missing_outcome, from #4131.

clusters.architecture_notes: Two kernels share one vocabulary. form_find.rs is the anchored force-density (FD) kernel: form_find_anchored, form_find_anchored_surfaces and form_find_anchored_surfaces_aniso each run validate_members and partition_anchors, assemble a dense D (assemble_d or assemble_d_aniso over scatter_line_members), then solve_reduced, which ends in the is_singular_reduced_solve guard. The two surface entries run a line-identical cotangent Picard loop judged by free_equilibrium_residual_relative. form_find_free.rs is the free-standing kernel. It has two specs: Explicit validates and classifies nullity via validate_explicit, and GroupRatios runs a coordinate-descent eigenvalue search. form_find_free_surfaces is a 311-line outer loop on top of both. It bootstraps from the line-only solve, searches q or fixes q, tries a (2b) null-space trial move, takes a (3) FD-gradient eigen-gap descent step, and applies a stall guard. Its own copies of D assembly, spectrum classification, and residual criterion are private to form_find_free.rs. There are three parallel error enums, FormFindError, AnisoFormFindError and FreeFormError, with a map_ff_error bridge. No validated-problem type exists. The reify-eval trampoline (compute_targets/form_find.rs plus tensegrity_crack) range-checks every index before calling the kernel, so the kernel guards added in #7553 and #6563 are a second, independent copy of the same range check. prestress_stability.rs reuses assemble_force_density_matrix from form_find_free and has its own spectrum code. The stdlib tensegrity.rs accessors decode the same Tensegrity topology a second time, with silent-Undef semantics. Churn in assembly/global.rs is feature work (#8373 node-owned parallel assembly), not bug-driven.

clusters.cross_system_notes: Two cross-system seams are involved. (1) Upstream faer 0.24: gevd_real's QZ aggressive-early-deflation step relies on usize wrapping arithmetic. #7602 patched it by setting `overflow-checks = false` for the whole reify-solver-elastic package in dev and test profiles (Cargo.toml `[profile.dev.package.reify-solver-elastic]`). The cost is that overflow detection is off for all of the crate's own code (assembly/global.rs stride arithmetic included) outside release. The exit condition, a leaf crate that alone carries the flag, is owned by #8120. This is a compensation for a missing guarantee in a dependency; I added no finding because the task already exists. (2) The reify-eval trampoline (tensegrity_crack.rs: crack_index_pairs, check_index, crack_anchors) fully range-checks member, anchor and surface indices before the kernel is called. The kernel guards added by #7553 and #6563 are therefore a defensive second copy rather than the only boundary. The kernel's DimensionMismatch variant and the trampoline's `describe` text no longer agree on what the variant means. This is covered by the ForceDensityProblem extension finding (D2 `IndexOutOfRange`).

clusters.architecture_notes: reify-eval builds a `ResolutionProblem` (auto params, constraints, dependent cells, objective). It does so in three builders: `build_auto_param_list`, used by `build_solver_problem` and `build_merged_solver_problem`, plus inline copies in `Engine::edit_param` and `Engine::edit_source`. All three write `AutoParam.bounds: None`. `SolverRegistry::solve_inner` decomposes the problem into components, routes each by `ConstraintDomain` to DimensionalSolver (Nelder-Mead), CpSatSolver or SolveSpace, and folds the components' `unique` flags with `&=`. In DimensionalSolver, a variable's feasible domain lives in a private `DerivedInterval`: `(value, strict)` per side, mined syntactically by `derive_param_intervals` from four linear shapes. Every consumer re-derives it, and the `StrictBound` enum (Kept / Dropped / SteppedInside) projects it into a seed box or a clamp box. `SolveRegime` (RobustnessFloor / TradeoffBlend / FeasibilityWitness) picks which clamp box `solve_core_with_sd_tolerance` uses. That function accepts a point when `max_constraint_residual <= 1e-12`, computed by a hand-rolled residual evaluator (`comparison_residual`) rather than the reify-expr evaluator that `reify check` and CP-SAT use. Determinedness is decided afterwards by `verify_uniqueness`, which returns a `Determinedness` enum. `finalise_uniqueness` then flattens that enum into `SolveResult::Infeasible { ConstraintNonUnique }`, so the verdict crosses the crate boundary as a three-variant `SolveResult` with a `unique: bool` and a `NoProgress { reason: String }`. reify-eval interprets that result separately at six call sites (cold eval, the merged cluster, eval_cached, the cached merged cluster, edit_param, edit_source). The relate/at-auto solve (reify-eval relate_solve.rs over reify-constraints relate_solve.rs) is a separate single-Frame Newton path that returns the same `SolveResult`. The open PRDs that own most of this area are: solver-crates-layering (S14: ξ #8653, ο #8656, π #8658 split solver.rs; ν #8645 gives the predicates one home), solution-set-completeness (P3: a typed `Completeness` carrier, #6706 done, the rest deferred to the E3 coarse tasks #6900/#6901), solver-driver-parity (P1: #6690 builder unification, #6692 one-sided refusal, #6699 entry-point parity), #6653 (equality tolerance, in progress) and #6655 (HC4 interval propagation).

The #6967 and #7050 "GREEN —" commits are TDD feature velocity. The fix(6979), fix(5467), fix(5720) and fix(5711) commits are clippy or review-amendment touch-ups. The six fix(6169) commits are review rounds on one task, already owned by fk-d98e178717e6 and fk-88643a4cc993. solver.rs's +13,489 lines are about half embedded tests. Roughly 11 commits fix landed behaviour, and they are not random: #7883 ×2, #6465 ×2, #5714, #6377, #5415, #5469 and the #5189 esc-5189-5/-7 pair. clusters.cross_system_notes:
Three upstream gaps in reify-eval drive patching here.

(1) The reify-eval problem builders never populate `AutoParam.bounds`: `build_auto_param_list`, plus the inline copies in `edit_param` and `edit_source` (#6690 unifies them). As a result:
- reify-constraints grew a private constraint-derived bound miner (#5618);
- CP-SAT can never enumerate an engine-produced Int auto;
- `decompose::domain_of_auto` carries a long doc explaining the re-route that follows.
The missing guarantee is a populated domain channel.

(2) The engine compensates for the solver's determinedness verdict. `engine_eval.rs::is_strict_connector_instance_auto` / `connector_pin_if_determined` remove strict `__connector_`-prefixed autos from `auto_params` 'to avoid a spurious ConstraintNonUnique' (#4710). That is routing on a string prefix (heuristic 12) to dodge a verdict the solver cannot qualify, because it cannot be told a cell is determined by another pass.

(3) Engine::check's verdict family depends on side tables populated by other surfaces. That is already recorded as fk-c944ff1a913b / fk-88643a4cc993 (#9017) and not re-reported.

In the other direction, reify-eval `detect_underdetermined` (W_UNDERDETERMINED, a syntactic read-closure) is a third determinedness producer, independent of `verify_uniqueness` and `default_bounded_strict_autos`. The #6307 and #7069 false positives sit on that seam; the ParamDomain provenance in finding 1 would give it one source.

clusters.architecture_notes: OcctKernel (lib.rs, 15,275 lines, 4,735 production) is the single-threaded owner of `shapes` and `reprs` (two parallel HashMap<u64,_>), `extracted_{edges,faces,vertices}`, `parent_handle`, `next_id`; the S11 PRD plans to wrap these in a ShapeStore (#8682). OcctKernelHandle (handle.rs, 3,723 lines) is an mpsc/oneshot actor around a dedicated OS thread. Every capability is written out as an OcctRequest variant, an inherent method, a spawn() match arm and a trait forward (planned for collapse by #8672). All handle resolution inside OcctKernel now goes through `OcctKernel::get_shape`, which refuses a missing handle (InvalidReference), a null UniquePtr, and a non-null UniquePtr around IsNull topology. Since #7379 every production caller propagates it with `?`; there are no remaining `map_err(|_| ..InvalidHandle)` sites in lib.rs or handle.rs. The reify-ir `From<GeometryError>` impls for QueryError/ExportError/TessError do the only mapping. The FFI bridge (ffi.rs, 192 fns) is a cxx bridge into one 9,477-line C++ translation unit plus a 1,807-line header. The C++ side wraps every fallible call in `wrap_occt_call`, which catches Standard_Failure, ContractViolation and std::exception and rethrows all three as `std::runtime_error(String)` with a name prefix. Rust flattens each into `GeometryError::OperationFailed(String)` or `QueryError::QueryFailed(String)` at 132 hand-written `e.to_string()` sites in production lib.rs. Process-global OCCT state (Interface_Static, XSAlgo) is serialised by `g_step_export_mutex`, and boolean pass counting and parallelism are thread_local. Defence-in-depth guards are layered Rust-then-C++: the line-wire floor is single-sourced through floor_constants.rs and build.rs, while the other thresholds are free-standing constants in two languages.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partly misleading. Of the 10 fix commits in the last 3 weeks, most are one defect swept entry point by entry point or review amendments. #7379 is 3 commits, which are one task's mechanical sweep of query, export/tessellate and split onto `?`. #7437 is a fix plus an amend. #6344 (about 20 amend/GREEN commits on the STEP angle-unit guard), #6521, #6560 and #7137 are amendment rounds on young features, not landed-defect fixes. The real recurring class is the per-entry-point sweep itself: the same guard or error-mapping decision is re-applied site by site (#5211 added IsNull guards to 4 C++ entry points plus get_shape; #7379 mapped 3 Rust families), because there is no single type or helper to apply it once. The raw 35/369 density overstates how buggy the code is, but the sweeps do show the missing-seam cost.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Two cross-subsystem patches. (1) reify-eval `TopologyCorrespondenceDropTally` (engine_build.rs, around line 1360-1470) builds user-visible Info diagnostics as 'topology correspondence dropped: {op_kind} {counter_name}={count}' keyed by &'static str pairs ('silent_drop_count', 'unsynthesized_profile_edge_count', 'duplicate_parent_subshape_index_count'). That leaks C++/FFI field names into user text and routes on string keys because the kernel history types carry raw u32 counters with no typed 'correspondence lost' notion (upstream reify-ir AttributeHistory / S11 δ #8676 typed history). (2) The eval layer parses kernel replies from strings (parse_xyz_value, kind names), which is the owned S10 η work. In the other direction, reify-ir's GeometryError has no variants for corrupt-handle or contract-violation faults, which is why the OCCT crate encodes fault class in message prefixes and test substring pins ('[rust-guard]', 'OCCT <fn>:'); the first finding's fix lands in reify-ir and needs sequencing after S10 α2 (#8931).

clusters.architecture_notes: scripts/verify.sh is a 4833-line bash program: 2366 lines sit outside any function (arg parsing, scope and narrowing blocks, PLAN emission) and 3275 lines (68%) are comments. build_plan is 733 lines, add_test_passes 331, decide_scope 279. It builds PLAN as an array of shell-text lines, prints it or executes it, and re-reads its own printed plan for --confirm-failed. Scope is decided by decide_scope (path case arms plus two hand lists) and narrowed by affected-crates-lib.sh. After S22 theta (#8662) that lib is a thin bash precedence layer (_routed_record: ALL, SEEDS or NONE) over scripts/reify_path_attribution.py facts. Infra tests are chosen by one data map (verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt, 174 active rows) plus five coded selectors (kloc, ptodo, pdiag, pdoccover, cited-test-paths). Those selectors gate on scope, each takes its own git diff, and one has a path-keyed env prefix in selected_infra_leaf_env. S18 (PRD verify-structured-plan-and-role-table.md, 15 leaves, #9095-#9112) rewrites this as the Python package scripts/reify_verify with a typed Plan and StepKind, a ScopeDecision record, and BashCall/DataFile registries. In that design the Rust-coupled fixture set is derived at plan time (#9097) and the GUI pin set becomes JSON (#9096). The fixture copy lists are derived (#9108) and gate paths come from --print-gates (#9100). Hand lists S18 leaves as lists: RI_CORPUS_CRATES (reify_path_attribution.py, drift test is derived-subset-of-declared); occt-touching-crates.txt and release-sensitive-crates.txt (reached via BashCall); the ptodo, pdiag and pdoccover predicate copies (PRD sections 8 and 9: follow-up candidate, not filed); and the hand-added infra-map rows (D14). The deadline-capable roster (D_ROSTER and G_MEMBERS in tests/infra/test_slot_timeout_marker.sh) is not a verify.sh list at all. S19 owns it (review-all tests-infra-3.1, run-all-runner-infra-harness.md D10), so no S18 leaf covers it. verify.sh is the file S18 zeta (#9112) replaces with an exec shim, so recorded findings on verify.sh internals are effectively scheduled for deletion and the new findings concentrate on what survives the port.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Roughly half of the 41 fix-touching commits on scripts/verify.sh are not defects in landed code. About 10 are fixture-registration commits (5306, 6615, 5305, 5711, 6102, 6093, 5788, 5786, 5481, 6435). Each is the same one-line list edit that S18 beta/pi retire, so it is registry cost rather than a bug class. About 10 are TDD GREEN steps or in-task amendments: 7423 (7 commits, one task), 6393, 6392, 6375, and the 5730 review round (fd18bbce5a, 6f20b77839). The genuinely landed-defect classes are the OCCT LD_LIBRARY_PATH leak (esc-4581-87, #5730), the re-entrancy fork-bomb (#5125), the 7427 inert-class and GUI_PATH_SIGNAL fail-wide fixes, and the 6030/7096/6292 closure fail-wide fixes. clusters.cross_system_notes: Dark-factory is not driving patching in this hotspot beyond what S18 already records. DF_VERIFY_ROLE exports (fix 7630), the exit-code collapse and the sweep ledger record are covered by S18 alpha/epsilon (#9095, #9101). The deadline-capable roster the ask names (D_ROSTER, G_MEMBERS in tests/infra/test_slot_timeout_marker.sh) belongs to S19/tests-infra-3.1, not to S18 or to verify.sh. clusters.architecture_notes: The C1 layout contract turns the test binaries of five crates into 45 hand-written 'harness' compile units. Each unit is a root `crates/<c>/tests/harness_<sub>.rs` that declares every member with a mandatory `#[path = "harness_<sub>/<file>.rs"] mod <file>;` pair (846 `#[path]` attrs across 49 files). It sits next to a module directory of the same name. Cargo is left on auto-discovery: no crate sets `autotests` or `[[test]]`, and no `tests/*/main.rs` exists. So three independent rules sit on top of cargo and are enforced by a 3,308-line bash test: the kLOC cap, the `#[path]` mandate and the no-undeclared-member rule. They are backed by two ratchet data sets, `harness-layout-baseline.manifest` (218 live rows, all in reify-eval) and the in-script `_KLOC_WARN_KNOWN` (empty). The measure and the mod-graph walk live in `harness-layout-lib.sh`, an awk parser of Rust `mod` items. `harness_layout_unit_lines` and `harness_layout_declared_members` consume it, and the diff-scoped gate `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` shares it. S19 theta (#8700) is planned to move the rule functions into a guard lib, move `_KLOC_WARN_KNOWN` to a manifest, and move the contract prose to docs. It keeps the layout, the awk parser and the cap model. Registration is append-only: each new test adds two lines at the end of a shared root, which is why `harness_engine.rs` and `harness_geometry.rs` recur in merge-reconcile commits. Placement is decided by topic plus cap headroom, argued in comments on the root. `run-all-classification.manifest` is the sibling registry for infra tests: 203 rows, 191 of them `pool`, edited 71 times since 2026-08-01. `reify-test-support/src/helpers.rs` is the shared helper bag: about 1,260 lines of code plus a 2,075-line inline test module, grown by 'promote X into reify-test-support' TDD steps.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Mostly misleading as a defect signal. (1) Crate-level test churn in reify-compiler, reify-eval and reify-syntax is dominated by the planned consolidation program (#5282, #5284, #5693-#5696, #7033: 'fold N binaries into harness_X', RED+GREEN pairs). That is mechanical relocation, not bug repair. (2) Of the 20 commits since 2026-08-01 that touch `harness-layout-baseline.manifest`, the ones I inspected only removed rows. Only 4 rows were added after the 2026-07-22 'stop growing the baseline' ruling, all on 07-24 and 07-25, from branches already in flight, and none since. The ratchet is holding socially, and the 12-of-48 fix signal on that file is consolidation progress. (3) The `fix(NNNN): consolidate/re-home/register X under harness_engine|geometry` commits (#5240, #5951, #6756, #7418, #4192, #6001, #5342, #5371, #5752, #6082) are pre-merge review or ratchet reds on the task branch. They are not fixes to landed code, so the 0.39 and 0.62 fix densities on `harness_engine.rs` and `harness_geometry.rs` measure layout friction, not defects. The friction is real and recurring (finding 1) but it is a tax, not a bug stream. (4) `helpers.rs` churn (81 commits since August) is TDD feature velocity: promote a helper, pin it RED, then GREEN and amend. The only genuine defect-shaped history is in the guard's own parsing (finding 2) and the stale prose (finding 3).
clusters.cross_system_notes: Upstream systems patched here. (1) Cargo/rustc: auto-discovery of `tests/*.rs` as binaries, plus silent non-compilation of an undeclared module file, are why the layout contract needs a 3,308-line bash guard (finding 1). Cargo's own `tests/<name>/main.rs` convention and `autotests = false` are the unused native mechanisms. (2) nextest: `binary()` filtersets that match nothing are silent. This is why Section 7 `harness_stale_selector_violations` exists. It greps for `binary(<stem>)` and `--test <stem>` text over scripts and configs, and consolidation changes both halves of a test id. It can go once the consolidation program ends or if the selectors are generated from `cargo nextest list`. (3) Dark-factory: the 'row in the same diff' manifest rules (esc-4914-162) exist partly because the orchestrator's per-task lanes only see their own diff. No dark-factory defect was identified as the driver here.

clusters.architecture_notes: The GUI backend is a Tauri app whose single engine is an Arc<Mutex<EngineSession>> (engine.rs, 9.6k lines) behind pub AppState.engine. Ordered scheduling is owned by eval_queue.rs (EditIdentity coalescing, EditLedger, generation-stamped SnapshotPublisher). Tauri commands (main.rs wrappers over commands.rs *_edit/*_evaluation builders) submit to the queue. debug_server.rs (5.6k lines) is a second front door that reaches the engine through its own run_on_engine and a shared last_state baseline. The FS watcher (watcher.rs, armed by main.rs::watch_file) submits disk_reload_edit. mcp_context.rs::TauriToolContext is a third host that is test-only in production today and locks the mutex raw. Gates live in two places. Real gates sit inside EngineSession methods (export's RepresentationWithin refusal, commit_parameter's refusal ledger); those held after #6190 and #5099. Surface-level gates sit in each front door (the update_source active-file guard, write_confinement, the rejected-buffer save interlock, screenshot save_path rules); those are the ones that keep regressing. S25 (#8937-#8956) unifies scheduling and publication for the debug and AI doors through QueuedEngine, but its own stated guarantee is per-module and ordering-only; it does not move admission policy into the engine. Wire tokens: S25 theta #8944 and S26 mu/chi/iota/lambda (#9070-#9074) make them serde enums with generated TS unions, so a token mismatch becomes a compile or tsc error. No S25 or S26 leaf had landed at 0e60fa138d (no engine/ directory exists). The frontend debug bridge drives Three.js camera and OrbitControls state directly through DebugViewport, which exposes the raw scene, camera, renderer and controls.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Most of the 57 window fix commits are not landed-defect fixes. fix(5099) is a six-commit TDD amendment series on one task branch; fix(5573) is a mechanical migration of eight watcher tests onto a barrier helper; fix(6965) is four GREEN steps of one camera task; fix(6178) restores guards a WIP save reverted; and the fix(5357), fix(6471), fix(6752) and fix(5466) commits are lint, fixture and test-hygiene work. The landed-defect signal is small: #6190 (export bypassed the eta gate), #5097 (non-active path), #6723 and #5098 (verdict wire casing), #6979 (re-check over-adopts), #7375 (scrubbable joints) and #6965 (camera). Several of these are already structurally closed. #6190 was fixed inside EngineSession::export, so the gate cannot be bypassed from any door. The wire-token class is closed by the S25/S26 serde-enum plan. The engine.rs and bridge.ts hotspot counts (13/108, 6/44) mostly reflect file size and breadth, not a defect rate. The findings below concern the surviving class: per-door admission policy and per-door side effects.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Partly upstream: EngineSession::update_source (reify-gui) ignores the caller's path, so the silent-overwrite hazard in findings 1 and 2 is a property of the GUI engine wrapper itself, not of reify-eval. The PRD-level answer to the ask: after S25 xi/omicron/rho the debug and AI doors collapse to QueuedEngine plus a single host. That leaves ordering unified but admission policy still decided separately at (a) the Tauri update_source/re-evaluate door, (b) the watcher door disk_reload_edit, (c) the three open funnels (file-open, argv, debug open) for watcher/identity side effects, (d) save_path and the raw user save/export paths. The wire-token class is closed at build time by S25 theta (serde enums) plus S26 iota/lambda (generated bindings): a token mismatch becomes a Rust or tsc compile error. The class that survives S25/S26 is per-door admission and side effects (findings 1, 2, 5), plus implicit engine sub-state (finding 3, the preview override) and frontend pose duplication (finding 4).

clusters.architecture_notes: reify-lsp has no shared AST visitor. The nearest thing is a private traversal skeleton inside references.rs: for_each_direct_subexpr (wildcard-free ExprKind children), for_each_member_direct_expr (wildcard-free MemberDecl direct expressions), for_each_child_scope (has a `_ => {}` arm; its own comment admits rustc will not flag a missing arm), member_span, collect_bindings_in_scope, collect_decl_name_uses_in_members. That skeleton re-derives, for ExprKind and for MemberDecl child scopes, what reify-ast::walk_members/MemberRecursionSet already declares, and what reify-compiler's entity.rs::for_each_child(_mut), dot_chain_lint::walk_expr_depth and shadow_lint::walk_expr_depth each re-spell. reify reaches the cursor symbol everywhere by text: convert::find_word_at_offset (hover, goto_def, references, rename, highlight), then a name lookup. Only references layers AST-aware refusals on top (cursor_on_member_segment, collect_bindings/resolve_use shadow regions). hover and goto_def use reify-ast's flat find_named_member_span instead. Declaration names carry no spans in the AST (bare Strings), so decl_oracle::name_token_span rescans source text, with 11 production callers. Per-Declaration-kind facts (members, name, span, doc) are answered by about nine separate matches, three of them wildcard-free in decl_oracle and the rest with `_` arms. The per-version compile+check pipeline exists three times: AnalysisContext::from_parsed (rebuilt on every hover and completion request), compute_diagnostics_with_state (per change) and compute_diagnostics (tests only). Only the parse is memoised per document version (DocumentState::parsed_cache). Of the PRD's decomposition, χ #8756 (decl_oracle.rs and symbols.rs split out of analysis.rs) is done; η, θ, ε, ζ, ι, κ, μ, γ, ψ are all still pending. The recurring 'new kind or field must be added to N walkers' fix class comes from the five walker families above. No S27 leaf closes it for expressions and member scopes: η is Declaration::member_scopes only, and #7860 is shadow_lint's member recursion only.
clusters.churn_exoneration: Partly misleading. The #6341 type-alias cluster (nine commits) is RED/GREEN feature velocity across hover, completion, goto-def, symbols and the keyword tables. It is not nine defects, though it does show the cost of touching N per-kind sites. The 6450 and 5579 commits are mostly amend rounds on one task branch (doc and prose repairs). The 8756 and 6388 commits are mechanical moves or TDD. The window's genuine landed-defect fixes are few: 7529 (name-token locator whose empty-span fallback produced a destructive rename edit), the SubDecl index_domain and relate_relations walks in cursor_on_member_segment and collect_uses_in_sub, 6615's derivation arm, and 6162 (unbounded log under lock). They share one root cause, the hand-mirrored walkers. There were no fix commits in the last three weeks, and the structural debt above is real even though it is currently quiet.
clusters.cross_system_notes: Three cross-system patches live in reify-lsp. (1) The eval-readiness containment (eval_guard::skip_reason, wired at AnalysisContext::from_parsed and both diagnostics.rs sites, task #6851) compensates for reify-compiler/reify-eval letting an unsubstituted Type::TypeParam value cell reach engine.check, which panics in debug builds; the missing guarantee is 'compile output handed to Engine is representable'. The PRD's β #8761 moves the predicate into reify-eval but does not remove the need for each surface to call it. (2) references.rs mirrors reify-compiler/scope.rs shadowing precedence by hand ('mirrored, not reused') because the compiler's scope model is not exposed with source regions. (3) The three per-site copies of checker injection mirror reify check's and the GUI's compile entry points, which is what resolution-unification's compile_program #5516/#5520 and γ #8778 are meant to fold. The shared enabling work (an Expr/MemberDecl child enumeration and SpannedIdent names in reify-ast/reify-syntax) belongs to the S9 AST stream, not to reify-lsp, which is why the LSP fix class keeps recurring as 'LSP lags every IR field addition by one fix commit'.

findings.title: language-pipeline/eval-cache-eval-engine-admin-compiler-builtin-signatures-compiler-units.8
findings.statement: cache.rs keeps public peers of the live invalidation path that production never calls. `pub fn dirty_set` has no caller anywhere, takes unused `_graph` and `_values` parameters, and its doc claims it is 're-evaluating and checking for early cutoff', which it does not do. check_early_cutoff and compute_input_hash are called only from cache.rs's own tests. The free function derive_output_freshness has no production caller. DependencyMap::topological_order is called only by dirty_set. Meanwhile two live dirty mechanisms coexist: the one-hop CacheStore.dirty_reasons (invalidate_dependents in engine_edit.rs; is_dirty, clear_dirty and clear_dependents_dirty in eval_cached) and the transitive dirty::compute_dirty_cone (5 production sites in engine_edit.rs). The unwired freshness walk is a third (prior finding).
findings.proposal: Delete dirty_set, check_early_cutoff, compute_input_hash and DependencyMap::topological_order along with their unit tests, and keep the derive_output_freshness truth table only behind the _with_cause variant that production uses.
findings.bug_history_link: carried from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: Commit 2e364f0171 deleted dirty_set, check_early_cutoff, compute_input_hash, the free derive_output_freshness and DependencyMap::topological_order from crates/reify-eval/src/cache.rs. A grep for them in crates/ finds nothing. The with_cause variants and the derive_output_freshness_for_node family remain. The two live dirty mechanisms (CacheStore.dirty_reasons and dirty::compute_dirty_cone) still coexist, but the dead-peer structure the finding describes is gone.

findings.title: analysis/solver-elastic-qoi-stdlib-modal-eval-compute-persist-solver-elastic-mpc.11
findings.statement: The Rust ShellStress container (pub, re-exported at the crate root) has no production consumer. Outside shell_result.rs's own tests and a lib.rs doc example, nothing constructs or reads it; the DSL-side `structure def ShellStress` in solver_elastic.ri is filled through flatten_shell_channels' four Vec<f64> buffers in reify-eval's compute_targets/shell_solve.rs, not through this type. Its file header still tells the next agent the two definitions "must stay shape-aligned" and promises a cross-assertion from "T18-T20" that does not exist.
findings.proposal: Delete ShellStress, its crate-root re-export and its doctest line, and remove the shape-alignment obligation from the shell_result.rs header.
findings.bug_history_link: carried from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: Commit ee76e7e27a (task 8528) deleted the unused Rust ShellStress container. crates/reify-solver-elastic/src/shell_result.rs no longer defines the struct, and its header now just points at the stdlib ShellStress. The misleading 'must stay shape-aligned' / T18-T20 promise is gone.

findings.title: constraints-and-geometry/stdlib-sweep-constraints-relate-solve-constraints-registry-kernel-fidget.9
findings.statement: Within reify-constraints, `collect_value_refs` names two traversals with different rules. dependent_reads::collect_value_refs (via CompiledExpr::walk) collects ValueRef only and descends into Lambda bodies. The IR method CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs() also collects CrossSubGeometryRef and, for Lambda, emits captures without descending. Decomposition connectivity, objective expansion and the dependent-cell analysis use the first. lib.rs's undef classification and solver.rs's bound-derivation MENTIONS test (collect_underivable_in_leaf) use the second. The free fn's doc mentions only the CrossSubGeometryRef difference.
findings.proposal: Rename the free fn to say what it collects (e.g. plain_value_refs), and decide and document whether lambda-body refs count, in one place.
findings.bug_history_link: carried from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: The two same-named traversals still exist. dependent_reads::collect_value_refs (via walk) collects ValueRef only and descends into Lambda bodies. crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs also collects CrossSubGeometryRef and emits Lambda captures without descending. The free function's doc now says 'ValueRef ids ONLY. Not CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs' and names the CrossSubGeometryRef difference, but not the Lambda-body difference. The name collision is unchanged. Partly mitigated by that doc pointer.

findings.title: constraints-and-geometry/kernel-occt-lib-eval-geometry-ops-stdlib-geometry-eval-realization-cache.4
findings.statement: get_shape is documented as the single chokepoint that refuses null/IsNull topology "loudly" (fix 5211): it returns OperationFailed("shape handle .. wraps null/empty topology (IsNull)"). Every query-side caller discards that through `.get_shape(id).map_err(|_| QueryError::InvalidHandle(id))`, so a corrupted but present handle is reported to the user as an invalid handle. export/tessellate do the same into ExportError::InvalidHandle/TessError::InvalidHandle. The guard's test (get_shape_rejects_null_topology_and_queries_return_err) asserts only `is_err()` on the query paths, so the message loss is unpinned.
findings.proposal: Add one `fn shape_for_query(&self, id) -> Result<&OcctShape, QueryError>` mapping InvalidReference(id) to InvalidHandle(id) and OperationFailed(msg) to QueryFailed(msg), with sibling helpers for ExportError and TessError. Replace the 54 sites and assert the message in the existing null-topology test.
findings.bug_history_link: carried from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: Task 7379 commits fixed this. 4095ba9c2e makes query paths propagate get_shape's GeometryError with ?. 668182fd5d does the same for export and tessellate. dea320330f does it for execute_split. A grep for map_err(|_| QueryError::InvalidHandle in crates/reify-kernel-occt finds nothing. RED tests were added, and the cause is now reported rather than collapsed to InvalidHandle.

findings.title: INV-SF-7 has no single enforcement point: "CST fault ⇒ ≥1 ParseError" is re-decided per dispatch arm, and five arms or bodies still fail open
findings.statement: Every production consumer refuses a module whose ParsedModule.errors is non-empty (pre_pass.rs::forward_parse_errors documents all of them). So INV-SF-7's safety half is one O(1) module-level property: `tree.root_node().has_error()` implies `!errors.is_empty()`. That property is not checked anywhere. Instead each arm decides refusal for itself, using one of three different mechanisms. (1) `check_and_lower!` (pre-refusal) covers import, unit, type alias, joint and default at top level, and every lower_member arm except associated_type. (2) lower_function_checked (run, discard, backstop) covers function_definition. (3) Report-and-keep-partial-AST is used in lower_enum and lower_type_args_from_node. The module arm calls refuse_if_faulty by hand. structure, occurrence, trait, field, purpose, constraint_definition, annotation and pragma are lowered unguarded and rely on per-body ERROR arms that some bodies lack. Probed on target/debug/reify (built 2026-10-12; no ts_parser change since). Each of these returns rc 0 with no parse error: `purpose P(x: ) { }`, `purpose P(x: Real) { param y: }` (#8080), `trait T { param a : Length\n port p : out T }` (#7809), `structure S<T: > {...}` (#8275), `@foo(1 +)` (#8081, which only reports 'unknown annotation'), and `field def F : Length -> Real { source = analytical { 1 + } }`, which no task owns. lower_member's `_ => None` and lower_expr's `_ => None // Unknown node kind — skip` are fail-open defaults. A new declaration or expression kind added to grammar.js without a matching arm is therefore dropped with zero diagnostics. That is what reopens the hole: the safety property belongs to each arm's author, not to the parser.
findings.proposal: Enforce the module-level invariant once, at the parse entry, and demote the per-arm machinery to message quality. (a) In parse_with_prelude_enums, after lowering, add a `fault_backstop(root, &errors)` in fault_diagnosis.rs. If `root.has_error()`, then for each faulty top-level child of source_file whose byte range no emitted ParseError intersects, push one located diagnostic at first_error_or_missing_descendant, e.g. `syntax error in <kind>`. Add a `debug_assert!(!root.has_error() || !errors.is_empty())` as the redundant use-site check. (b) Generalise lower_function_checked into one combinator, `Lowering::lower_guarded(node, label, f)`: count errors before, run f, refuse and backstop if the node is faulty. Apply it uniformly in the lower_source_file dispatch so every arm passes through it. Pick one refusal policy for a faulty declaration (run inner for diagnostics, then refuse) and delete lower_enum's ad-hoc has_error block. (c) Pin the property at the public seam with a test. Iterate the tree-sitter corpus entries (tree-sitter-reify/test/corpus/*.txt) whose expected tree contains ERROR or MISSING, and assert `reify_syntax::parse(src).errors` is non-empty for each. What dies or shrinks: lower_function_checked becomes the combinator; lower_enum's inline guard goes; the safety halves of #7809, #8080, #8081 and #8275 are closed by construction (each shrinks to 'improve the message at this site'); and a future declaration kind can no longer fail open. This would have prevented the zero-diagnostic outcomes behind #5392, #6286 (import, unit, joint, alias, default, module), #7809, #8080, #8081, #8275 and the unowned field_definition hole. Relation: not covered as a mechanism. It extends #7809, #8080, #8081 and #8275, which are site fixes. #8742 (S9 μ, ParseErrorKind) could give the backstop its own kind (e.g. UnattributedFault).
findings.bug_history_link: fix(#5392) b7b35c584f 'a fn-body fault must be refused and diagnosed, never dropped'; fix(syntax) 0ce208511f / 0337a7767a / d5d9f38ce8 (#6286: import; unit, joint, type alias, default; module); fix(6156) 11ed96dc84, 9dace85f67; pending #7809, #8080, #8081, #8275 (all agent follow-ups spawned from #6156/#6286 audits)
findings.verdict_notes: parse_with_prelude_enums calls lower_source_file and only adds check_member_continuations. No module-level has_error() => errors non-empty check exists. Refusal is per-arm: check_and_lower!, refuse_if_faulty (module arm only, ~777) and lower_function_checked. The field arm (669) is unguarded. lower_member has `_ => None` at 2729. The exact count of 'five arms' was not checked.

findings.title: field_definition arm lowers nested faults silently: `analytical { 1 + }` checks clean, and `imported { format = }` is misreported as a missing key
findings.statement: The `"field_definition"` arm of lower_source_file calls lower_field directly. Neither lower_field nor lower_field_source checks for a CST fault, and lower_field_source's config-entry loops drop any entry whose value fails lower_expr. Probed on target/debug/reify. `field def F : Length -> Real { source = analytical { 1 + } }` gives rc 0 with 'All constraints satisfied.' and no parse error: binary_expression with a MISSING right operand lowers to None, so lower_field returns None and the declaration vanishes. `... imported { path = "a.vdb" format = }` produces no parse error and only the compiler's 'imported field source is missing required key: format', which blames a key the author actually wrote. #6286's audit listed import, unit, joint, alias, default and module. #8080, #8081 and #8275 cover purpose, annotation/pragma and headers. No task owns field_definition.
findings.proposal: Wrap the field_definition arm in `check_and_lower!(self, child, "field definition", self.lower_field(child))`, matching the #6286 leaf-arm precedent. Add a must-error test in crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax (a field test file) for both probes, asserting a diagnostic located at the fault. If finding 1's backstop lands first, this arm is covered for safety, and this item is only about message quality. Not covered by any task.
findings.bug_history_link: same class as fix(syntax) 0337a7767a (#6286 unit/joint/alias/default); unowned residual of #6286's dispatch-arm audit
findings.verdict_notes: lower_field and lower_field_source have no fault check. lower_field_source uses `?` on lower_expr for analytical/composed. Sampled and imported config loops silently skip entries whose lower_expr returns None, so `format =` leaves format None. The field_definition arm at ~669 does not use check_and_lower!. I did not run the probe.

findings.title: Member-list lowering is re-implemented in seven body loops, each with its own annotation/pragma/ERROR policy, while the grammar has one commonMembers SPOT; pragmas in `where` blocks and sub-specialization bodies are silently dropped
findings.statement: grammar.js::commonMembers (introduced 883155c118, task 3971) is one list feeding both `_member` and `_guard_member`, and it includes annotation and pragma. The lowering has no counterpart. Seven loops each decide their own handling. Annotations attach to Param/Let in lower_members and lower_guarded_block, to Fn in lower_trait_members, and nowhere in lower_specialization_body_members. Pragmas are collected in lower_members, lower_trait_members and lower_purpose_members, but lower_guarded_block and lower_specialization_body_members pass them to lower_member, whose `_ => None` drops them. ERROR children are handled by diagnose_error_node in lower_members and lower_guarded_block, by push_fault_error_with_excerpt in the port, connect and constraint-def loops, and silently drained in lower_trait_members (#7809) and lower_purpose_members (#8080). Probed: `#frobnicate(1)` in a structure body warns 'unknown pragma #frobnicate'. The same line inside `where x > 1mm { ... }`, or inside a `sub a : L { ... }` specialization body (with an `@deprecated("x")` beside it), produces no diagnostic at all. node-types.json confirms that guarded_block and specialization_body both admit `pragma` and `annotation`. lower_member cannot warn on unknown kinds because lower_members passes it every child of the declaration, including `{`, name, type_parameters and trait_bound_list, so `_ => None` is forced. The fix for any one body (#7809, #8080, #8732) leaves its siblings unfixed.
findings.proposal: Introduce one `lower_member_list(container: Node, spec: &MemberListSpec) -> MemberList` in a new ts_parser/member_list.rs. MemberListSpec is a per-container value naming the admitted member kinds, the annotation-attachment rule, and whether pragmas are collected or rejected with a diagnostic. The function iterates only the children between `{` and `}`, reusing member_continuation.rs::members_of's brace logic. It handles annotation, pragma and ERROR in one place, routes admitted kinds through lower_member, and reports any other named kind via warn_unexpected_child. lower_members, lower_guarded_block, lower_trait_members, lower_purpose_members and lower_specialization_body_members each become one call. The `pending_annotations` bookkeeping, repeated five times, dies. lower_member's `_ => None` becomes unreachable and can be replaced by a diagnostic, and the shadowed per-body ERROR arms collapse into one. An unsupported annotation is reported rather than dropped, the same policy lower_source_file already applies to default_declaration. This would have prevented #7809, #8080 and the live where-block/specialization-body pragma drops. Relation: extends #8732 (S9 γ, the compiler-side 'one member-support table; no silent member drops', which touches only lower_purpose_members on the parser side) and subsumes the body halves of #7809 and #8080. The parser-side table itself is not covered.
findings.bug_history_link: 883155c118 (commonMembers SPOT added grammar-side only); fix(6156) 9dace85f67 'convert the shadowed port/connect/guarded-block ERROR arms'; pending #7809 (trait body), #8080 (purpose body), #8732 (S9 γ)
findings.verdict_notes: lower_specialization_body_members passes every child to lower_member and has no annotation or pragma handling, so those kinds fall to `_ => None`. lower_trait_members handles annotation and pragma itself and silently drains non-trait_member children. Per-body policies differ across the loops. I did not verify the guarded_block pragma drop or the probes by running them.

findings.title: Grammar node-kind sets are hand-enumerated in the lowering although node-types.json states them; drift is caught only by a re-lexer of grammar.js for one module
findings.statement: tree-sitter-reify/src/node-types.json is regenerated on every build and gives, per container, the exact child kinds the parser can produce. For example source_file has 16 kinds; guarded_block has 18 including pragma and annotation; specialization_body has 21. No crate reads it (git grep finds only the generate and freshness scripts). The lowering re-lists these kinds as string literals in lower_source_file, lower_member, lower_expr and each body loop, with `_ => None` or warn_unexpected_child defaults. member_continuation.rs keeps a third hand list, MEMBER_LIST_CONTAINERS. Its drift guard re-lexes grammar.js with about 250 lines of ad-hoc JS scanning (#7676), and it caught derived_body only after #6615 had landed (fcf0f01cb3). The grammar declares no `supertypes`, so `_expression` and `_member` have no machine-readable subtype list. Because the catch-all arms cannot be reached through parse(), three inline tests call private lowerers with deliberately wrong node kinds, e.g. a constraint_definition node fed to lower_connect_body, just to reach them. Those tests pin dead branches through internals (Tests stance).
findings.proposal: Make the kind sets derived, not restated. (a) In grammar.js add `supertypes: $ => [$._expression, $._member, $._guard_member, $._declaration]` so node-types.json carries named subtype lists. (b) Turn each dispatch into a static table in its own module, e.g. `const DECLARATION_LOWERERS: &[(&str, DeclLowerer)]`, `EXPR_LOWERERS`, and finding 3's MemberListSpec sets. (c) Add one test module, crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax/grammar_contract_tests.rs, that parses node-types.json with serde_json (the dev-dep #7676 already plans). It asserts that each container's child kinds equal the lowering table's handled set plus a reasoned exclusion list, mirroring MEMBER_LIST_CONTAINER_EXCLUSIONS. The same test can derive MEMBER_LIST_CONTAINERS, replacing #7676's grammar.json walk with the generated file that has stable types. What dies: the grammar.js re-lexer helpers (#7676's scope), the three wrong-node-kind internal tests, and lower_expr's 'Unknown node kind — skip' default, which becomes unreachable. This would have prevented the derived_body miss (#7094 → fcf0f01cb3) and the where-block pragma drop. Relation: extends #7676 (which replaces only the member-continuation guard's lexer). Not covered for the lowering dispatch tables.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(7094) fcf0f01cb3 'cover derived_body, the container the drift guard caught'; fix(5495) 5b19859013 (grammar.js line-cite rot); pending #7676
findings.verdict_notes: No Rust code under crates/ references node-types.json. grammar.js has no supertypes. Kind sets are hand-listed as string literals in lower_expr and the body loops. The test and member_continuation claims were not individually checked.

findings.title: Unit operator is recovered by slicing raw source between operand byte ranges and re-parsing it with a comment stripper, because the grammar hides the scanner's typed mul/div tokens
findings.statement: scanner.c already emits two distinct typed tokens, UNIT_MUL_OP (index 1) and UNIT_DIV_OP (index 2). grammar.js::unit_expr binds them as `field('op', choice($._unit_mul_op, $._unit_div_op))`. The leading underscore makes them hidden, so lower_unit_expr cannot read the field (as #6567 records). It slices `self.source[left.end_byte()..right.start_byte()]` instead, then matches the text exactly in classify_unit_op. When that fails because a comment extra sits in the slice (#6567: `5(m)/*c*/*(s)` dropped the binding), collect_unit_op_comment_spans and strip_unit_op_comments cut the comments out and classify again. This is an ad-hoc parser over source text whose structured form the parser already computed and discarded. It costs about 200 lines of code and prose (about 70 lines of doc comments on these three fns alone, including 'Scope of that claim, stated exactly because the next reader will lean on it'), the UnitOp::Missing/Unrecognized arms, and about 45 references in the inline test module (21 to strip_unit_op_comments, 14 to classify_unit_op, plus unit_expr_from_classified_op 'which exists as that seam').
findings.proposal: Fix it upstream in the grammar. In grammar.js::unit_expr, write `field('op', choice(alias($._unit_mul_op, '*'), alias($._unit_div_op, '/')))`. An anonymous alias keeps corpus S-expressions unchanged; a named alias `$.unit_mul_op` also works but changes the corpus. lower_unit_expr then does `match node.child_by_field_name("op")?.kind() { "*" => Mul, "/" => Div, _ => unreachable_diag }`, and the `·` spelling stays a scanner concern. What dies: UnitOp, classify_unit_op, collect_unit_op_comment_spans, strip_unit_op_comments, unit_expr_from_classified_op's Unrecognized arm and their inline tests. It prevents #6567's comment-in-slice bug class by construction. Regenerate parser.c through scripts/tree-sitter-generate.sh; the freshness gate covers the stale-artefact class (#5629). Relation: not covered. It applies S8-π #8904's principle ('operators parsed at the syntax boundary') to unit_expr, which #8904 does not touch (it covers BinOp/UnOp of binary/unary_expression).
findings.bug_history_link: #5784 (· as unit-multiply; amend commits d0f9bd4214, d1026658d2, 5922588bf4, e54fd19b6c); #6567 'A comment inside a unit expression is rejected as an unrecognized unit operator' (deferred); #6952 (done — fixed by adding the strip pass, not by exposing the token)
findings.verdict_notes: grammar.js:1949 binds field('op', choice($._unit_mul_op, $._unit_div_op)) and the lowering's own comment says child_by_field_name does not expose them. The operator is recovered from the source slice between operands and classified by classify_unit_op (5924), with a comment-stripping fallback. Line and reference counts are approximate.

findings.title: ts_parser.rs is 8,947 lines (4.5× the alarm); expression lowering is a clean &self seam over frozen pass-1 tables but cannot be split without reach-back because those tables live as mutable fields on Lowering
findings.statement: Measurement per heuristic 14. Raw lines: 6,126 of production code (1,847 of its 5,743 non-blank lines are comments, 32%) plus a 2,820-line inline `mod tests` with 91 tests, 14 of which construct `Lowering::new` directly and reach lowering.errors, snippet, lower_port_body and others. Named partition of the top-level symbols. (A) Declarations and imports (lower_source_file … lower_default_decl, about 1,600 lines). (B) Types (lower_type_expr_node … lower_type_args_from_node, about 330). (C) Members and bodies (lower_member … lower_forall_statement, about 1,700). (D) Expressions (lower_expr … lower_member_access, lines 4260-5877, about 1,600). (E) Literal and unit-op free fns (classify_unit_op, strip_unit_op_comments, decode_string_escapes, about 230). h13 check for (D): every method is `&self`, with zero `&mut self` in the range. The only state it reads is self.known_enums, self.namespace_bindings, self.entity_bindings (once each) and self.errors (the sink). All three tables are written only by pass 1 in lower_source_file and collect_import_bindings. A child file `ts_parser/expr.rs` holding `impl super::Lowering` would still reach back into the parent's private fields. That is the stitching the definition rejects, since Rust child modules can see the parent's private items. So the split is blocked by state lifetime (h5/h8), not by the code. (E) has no symptom and could move to its own module today. fault_diagnosis.rs is the existing precedent of a clean downward split.
findings.proposal: Freeze pass 1 into a value. Add `FileScope { known_enums, namespace_bindings, entity_bindings }`, built by `FileScope::collect(root, prelude_enum_names)` in ts_parser/scope.rs and immutable after that. Add `DiagSink` (the RefCell error vec plus push_error, push_fault_error, snippet and refuse_if_faulty) in ts_parser/diag.rs. Then ts_parser/expr.rs defines `ExprLowering<'a> { source: &'a str, scope: &'a FileScope, diag: &'a DiagSink }`. It imports only diag and scope, both downward, and never uses `super::Lowering`. Lowering keeps (A) and (C) and owns an ExprLowering. (E) moves to ts_parser/literals.rs, or mostly dies with finding 4. Move the inline tests out to harness_syntax_lowering, driving parse() and ExprLowering's crate-visible seam instead of Lowering::new. Record the measurement in the commit message. Each resulting file must pass h13, meaning no `use super::*` and no `impl super::Lowering`. Relation: not covered. No review-all stream owns reify-syntax.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (size/seam finding; the per-arm fault churn in findings 1/3 all lands in this one file — ts_parser.rs 14 fix / 68 commits in window)
findings.verdict_notes: ts_parser.rs is 8947 lines. lower_expr is `&self` at line 4260, and the 4260-5877 range has no `&mut self`. The h13 reach-back argument for a child module follows. The 91-test and 14-Lowering::new counts were not checked.

findings.title: Reviewer-answering and stale prose inside the lowering: 13 hard line cites (verified stale), merge-surface notes about task/5392 (done), measurement narratives in doc comments
findings.statement: Production ts_parser.rs carries 13 hard `ts_parser.rs:NNN`, `~line NNN` and `grammar.js:NN` cites. Two checked samples are stale. lower_type_args_from_node says 'Mirrors the "ERROR" => arm in lower_source_file (ts_parser.rs:305-313)', but that arm is at line 817. lower_trait_members says 'Mirrors the "ERROR" arm in lower_members (~line 2134)', but it is at 2754. #5495 (5b19859013) removed this exact class for grammar.js cites in one branch only. parse_with_prelude_enums says its call site 'stays a call site so the merge surface against the pending ts_parser.rs work on task/5392 is one hunk', and member_continuation.rs's module doc repeats the merge-surface rationale. #5392 is done, so both are reviewer and merge-coordination prose that has drifted. diagnose_error_node's 40-line doc and member_continuation.rs's 150-line module doc ('NOTE for anyone reconciling this against #7094's plan text', 'measured', corpus counts) are measurements and rejected-alternative defences. Under the Comments stance those belong in the commit or task record, or in docs/legibility/design-invariants.md for normative rules.
findings.proposal: Replace each line cite with a symbol cite (`lower_members`'s ERROR arm), the convention #5495 established for grammar.js. Delete the task/5392 merge-surface sentences. Rehome member_continuation's normative rule (clauses 1-7) to docs/legibility/design-invariants.md §INV-SF-7 with a one-line pointer, and leave the measurements to the #7094 and #8300 commit messages. Do this when the area is next touched, ideally as part of finding 6's split. Relation: not covered. The docs-truth / prose-rehoming program (prose-rehoming-and-symbol-citations PRD) is the natural owner if it has a reify-syntax leaf.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(5495) 5b19859013 'replace every branch-introduced grammar.js line cite with a rule name' (same class, partial)
findings.verdict_notes: Line 77 still says 'merge surface ... task/5392'. The line-cite comments are stale: line 1574 cites ts_parser.rs:305-313 while the ERROR arm is at 817, and line 2585 cites ~line 2134 while the arm is near 2754 (2093 also matches). My grep found 12 hard-cite lines against the claimed 13, which is negligible. #5392 being done was not checked.

findings.title: Type-argument binding (arity, defaults, sigma) has no home: about ten sites, four mutually inconsistent arity policies
findings.statement:
The same decision is coded separately at each site: given a generic's declared type_params (with optional defaults) and the type args written at a use site, is the arity legal, and what sigma results. The policies disagree.
- range [required, total] with defaults filled, uncoded message 'type alias X expects N type argument(s)': type_resolution.rs::resolve_parameterized_alias.
- the same range but a silent `return None`: the nested-alias arm of resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst.
- strict equality, no defaults, uncoded, degrading to an erased Type::Enum(name): resolve_enum_type_with_args.
- strict equality IGNORING defaults, DiagnosticCode::TypeArgArity: check_applied_type_arg_bounds.
- strict equality, DiagnosticCode::UnresolvedType: the projection arm of normalize_type_guarded.
- 'too many' plus 'missing without default', defaults honoured, uncoded: entity.rs::check_type_param_bounds.
- an explicit-else-default `effective_arg` in phase_auto_type_param_resolution, whose comment says it 'mirrors effective_arg in check_type_param_bounds'.
- an implicit arity 0 that silently drops the args, for builtin, type-param and non-parametric-alias names: resolve_entity_name_with_shadowing's bare-name fallthrough.
- local guards in variant_construct.rs (`args.len() == enum_def.type_params.len()`) and expr.rs's match binder_subst (an unchecked zip).

Probes with target/debug/reify (built 2026-10-12):
- (a) `structure def Holder<U: Rigid, T: Rigid = Steel>`: `sub part = Holder<Bolt>()` checks clean, but `param h : Holder<Bolt>` fails with 'wrong number of type arguments for Holder: expected 2, got 1'.
- (c) `type P<T> = List<T>; type Q<X> = P<X, X>; param q : Q<Int>` reports only 'unresolved type: Q<Int>'. The direct `P<Int, Int>` gets the informative arity message.
- (e) `param a : Int<Real>`, `Length<Int>`, `Bool<Length>` and `String<Int>` all check clean (#7337 is still live).

A new generic position (e.g. generic traits, #5024) would have to pick a policy and a code yet again.
findings.proposal:
Introduce one value type and one function in a lower module, e.g. `type_args.rs`:
- `TypeArity { params: &[reify_ir::TypeParam] }`, built from every type-constructor kind: alias, structure, enum, parameterized builtin (read from S8-ο's PARAMETERIZED_BUILTIN_TYPES table), trait, type param, and non-generic name (arity 0).
- `bind_type_args(arity, args: &[Type], ctor: &str, span) -> Result<Sigma, Diagnostic>`. It applies the one rule (required ≤ got ≤ total, trailing defaults filled), emits the one TypeArgArity diagnostic naming constructor, expected range and actual count (INV-2), and returns a `Sigma` newtype that is complete by construction: every declared param bound to an explicit arg or a default.

Every site above calls it: alias (both arms), enum, Applied structure (construction AND check_applied_type_arg_bounds), projection, check_type_param_bounds, the auto phase seeding, variant_construct, binder_subst. resolve_entity_name_with_shadowing's bare-name fallthrough calls it with arity 0. That closes #7337 and #8229 by construction instead of one kind at a time.

Once Applied args are padded with defaults at construction, `Holder<Bolt>` and `Holder<Bolt, Steel>` become the same Type.

What dies:
- the four hand-written arity checks and their four message shapes;
- the `effective_arg` copies;
- the 'mirrors check_type_param_bounds' comment;
- the per-kind reject arms #7337/#8229 propose.

It would have prevented #6854 round 3 (defaults not seeded), #7337, #8229, #8098 (bare generic enum erasing) and probes (a) and (c).

Coverage: not-covered as a whole. It extends #8903 (S8-ο, whose D13 table carries arity for builtins only) and absorbs #7337 and #8229. Coordinate with #8643 (ResolutionCtx), which supplies the context the binder needs.
