Policies and codes do differ. The probe outputs were not re-run.

findings.title: Generic structure instantiation is owned by the auto: resolver, with partial field coverage and shared ValueCellIds
findings.statement:
The only code that turns a generic TopologyTemplate into a concrete one sits inside the 'resolve auto: type args' phase: it does `mono = target.clone(); mono.type_params.clear()` and substitutes field by field. The phase's purpose therefore needs an 'and' (heuristic 6), and the abstraction does not fit its callers.

(1) Explicit instantiation is never monomorphized. #6854's fixes taught the auto path to seed sigma from explicit args and defaults, but a use site with no auto: clause never enters the phase. The plainest probe, `sub h = Holder<GasketSeal>()`, panics `reify check` in debug: 'unrepresentable cell_type: value cell Holder.seal has cell_type TypeParam("S")' (#6853, #7225).

(2) The substitution is a hand-enumerated subset of TopologyTemplate's Type- and CompiledExpr-bearing fields. Covered: value_cells, constraints, guarded_groups (guard_expr, members, else_members, constraints, else_constraints), ports (members, constraints, frame_expr), sub_components[].type_args. Not covered: realizations, relations, connections, objective, match_arm_groups (arm_type, guard_expr), forall_templates, assoc_fns, assoc_types, sub_components[].args/pose/keyed_member_overrides. There is no exhaustive destructure, so a new field compiles unsubstituted. The postcondition `debug_assert!` checks top-level value_cells only.

(3) Cell ids are not re-keyed, so two monomorphs share ValueCellId("Widget", ...). Probe (k), with `Widget<SealA, auto: Gasket>()` and `Widget<SealB, auto: Gasket>()`, evaluates `Widget.slot_t = SealB {..}`: the generic's own cell is last-write-wins.

The only invariant enforcement is eval's debug-only assert_value_cell_types_representable. Release builds degrade silently to Undef (per #7225).
findings.proposal:
Extract `compile_builder/monomorph.rs` with `instantiate_template(target: &TopologyTemplate, sigma: Sigma /* complete, from bind_type_args */) -> TopologyTemplate`.
- It destructures `let TopologyTemplate { name, type_params, value_cells, ..every field.. } = target` exhaustively, so a new field is a compile error until someone decides how it substitutes.
- It re-keys ValueCellIds under the monomorph name.
- Its postcondition is one predicate, `template_is_concrete(&TopologyTemplate)`, built on S7 λ's Type::any_descendant.

The invariant 'a template reaching the eval graph has empty type_params and no TypeParam/ScalarParam anywhere' is checked at two points:
- construction, in instantiate_template;
- use, in graph hydration. Generic templates are skipped there, which is #7225's option (a), and the check becomes an always-on diagnostic rather than a debug assert.

Both the auto phase and a new explicit-instantiation pass call it. The task #6853's own files list already names monomorph.rs and explicit_generic_phase.rs.

What dies:
- substitute_value_cell_collection and substitute_constraint_collection;
- the 40-line coverage/seeding rationale comments in the auto phase;
- the top-level-only debug_assert;
- the insert-order masking described in #7225.

It would have prevented #6854 rounds 1-3, #6851, #6853 and #7225.

Coverage: extends #6853 (which plans the split but not the exhaustive destructure, re-keying or two-point invariant) and #7225. No review-all PRD covers monomorph.rs.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(6854): GREEN — require full auto-clause coverage before monomorph synthesis (8e2d7aef60); strengthen guard to full target.type_params coverage (cf37a32bec); seed sigma from explicit type-args (e14b5187de); diagnose the residual un-seedable skip path (2491c8d21d); seed sigma from DEFAULTS (92e903095f); live #6851, #6853, #7225
findings.verdict_notes: The monomorph is built with `mono = target.clone(); mono.type_params.clear()` and then substituted field by field. The phase's own comments at ~571-583 admit that realizations, connections, objective, match_arm_groups, forall_templates, assoc_fns and assoc_types are not substituted. The debug-only assert_value_cell_types_representable exists in reify-eval. I did not re-run the panic probe for explicit `Holder<X>()`.

findings.title: UserFunctionCall records no callee or type arguments, so overload choice and sigma are re-derived in the post-pass and in eval
findings.statement:
The compiler decides 'which overload, and with what type arguments' in expr.rs: through resolve_function_overload plus instantiate_call_return_type at four sites, plus a third tier ladder in the TraitMethodCall arm. It then throws the answer away, because CompiledExprKind::UserFunctionCall carries only `function_name: String` and `args`. Two consumers rebuild it.
- compile_builder/entities_phase.rs::check_expr_fn_calls re-runs resolve_function_overload on the args' result types and re-unifies params against args. Its comment says 'same logic as expr.rs:1530', a stale pointer: the helper is at :1337.
- reify-expr's find_matching_compiled_function re-selects the overload at eval under its own policy (first-match-wins versus the compiler's set-size classification). It carries a roughly 90-line doc explaining how it is kept in agreement with the compiler.

Drift has already shipped: esc-4093-152 (trait-object wildcard), #5685 (eval picked the Option overload for a Result subject) and #5686 (missing D4 disjunct). Pending #8586 says a widening rule must be 'implement[ed] in BOTH the compile-side and' eval.

The TraitMethodCall arm builds its result with `resolved[0].return_type.clone()` without going through instantiate_call_return_type. #8232's 'every user-fn-call path' therefore does not hold for the fifth path. It is latent only because generic-trait method signatures cannot yet name T (probe h: 'unresolved type in trait Boxed: T', #5024).
findings.proposal:
Give UserFunctionCall a resolved binding: `callee: FnRef` (a stable index or unique mangled symbol into the merged function table) and `type_args: Vec<Type>` (sigma in declaration order). Both are produced once by a single `bind_user_call(candidates, arg_types, span) -> Result<CallBinding, Diagnostic>` that wraps today's resolve_function_overload plus instantiate_call_return_type. All five lowering sites call it, TraitMethodCall included.

Consumers then read the binding:
- check_expr_fn_calls reads `type_args` for check_type_param_bounds and `callee` for conformance. Its re-resolve and re-unify are deleted.
- eval dispatches on `callee`. find_matching_compiled_function and its tier policy are deleted, and with them the eval-side half of #5686, #5685 and #8586.
- #8897's `intrinsic` stamp becomes a projection of the callee's origin rather than a second stamp.
- #5992's parity test is no longer needed: deduplication replaces pinning, which #5992's own text records as 'the deferred alternative'.

content_hash folds the callee identity.

Coverage: extends #8897 (S8-ζ, which stamps only stdlib intrinsics); supersedes #5992; gives #8233 and #8426 a single place to fix.
findings.bug_history_link: esc-4093-152; #5685 (Option-vs-Result eval mis-resolution, done); #5686 (missing D4 disjunct, done); fix(8232): GREEN — instantiate a generic callee's return type on every user-fn-call path (127a951d37); live #5992, #8897, #8233, #8426, #8586
findings.verdict_notes: UserFunctionCall carries only function_name and args. check_expr_fn_calls in entities_phase.rs re-resolves the overload, and its comment points to the stale `expr.rs:1530`. instantiate_call_return_type is at expr.rs:1337. reify-expr has find_matching_compiled_function, which re-selects the overload at eval. The TraitMethodCall arm uses `resolved[0].return_type.clone()` at expr.rs:6478 without calling instantiate_call_return_type.

findings.title: Parametric alias bodies are resolved by a second full TypeExpr resolver that keeps drifting from the direct-spelling resolver
findings.statement:
#6259 recorded the decision that an alias body 'resolves through the identical path the direct spelling takes'. Yet two resolvers walk TypeExprs:
- resolve_type_expr_with_aliases_kinded;
- resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst, which has its own Arrow, nested-parametric-alias, builtin (_with_subst twin) and depth-guard arms.

They differ on one axis only: whether a type-parameter name resolves to a declared TypeParam leaf or is looked up in a bound sigma. Agreement is restored one arm at a time by moving code into the shared resolve_entity_name_with_shadowing. #6477 moved the applied-form arms there after `type W<U> = Box2<U>` 'dropped its argument at every use site'.

That helper's doc still lists two arms the alias-body path lacks. One is a pinned 'parity GAP' (parametric_alias_deferred_alias_body_known_gap: `type Outer<T> = Option<Inner>` fails while the direct `Option<Inner>` works); the other is the E_BARE_SCALAR guard. Probe (c) shows a third divergence: the nested-alias arity check returns None without a diagnostic.

17 window commits on type_resolution.rs belong to #6477, #6259, #5429 and #6399, i.e. the resolver pair. The recorded finding fk-d402f7243603 and its D13 merge only the builtin and dimension twins. The TypeExpr resolver twin itself survives.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(6477): move the two applied-form arms into the shared name resolver (d9866f9654); fix(6477): forward the use site's entity namespaces into subst-aware alias-body resolution (8b96948be8); fix(6259) GREEN ×4 (c4b4faa1d1, 185a91aa3d, 03b1ee172a, eb176330d1); amend(6477): pin the deferred-alias parity gap (8975577ac1)
findings.verdict_notes: Both resolvers exist, and resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst has its own nested-alias arm. The nested-alias arm's arity failure returns None silently, which is a divergence from the direct path. I did not verify the commit counts or the 'parity GAP' test name.

findings.title: check_applied_type_arg_bounds rejects a default-omitting type annotation that the instantiation path accepts
findings.statement:
check_applied_type_arg_bounds enforces `args.len() != target.type_params.len()` and ignores TypeParam::default. Meanwhile resolve_entity_name_with_shadowing step 1 builds `Type::Applied { name, args }` from the written args without padding defaults.

Probe (a): with `structure def Holder<U: Rigid, T: Rigid = Steel>`, `sub part = Holder<Bolt>()` checks clean, because check_type_param_bounds honours defaults. In the same structure, `param h : Holder<Bolt>` fails with 'error: wrong number of type arguments for Holder: expected 2, got 1'.

The default-type-param feature therefore works in instantiation position and is an error in annotation position. Even where both are accepted, `Holder<Bolt>` and `Holder<Bolt, Steel>` would be distinct Types.
findings.proposal:
Pad Applied args with the declared defaults when the Applied is constructed in resolve_entity_name_with_shadowing step 1, and check the range [required, total] in check_applied_type_arg_bounds. Better, route both through finding 1's bind_type_args. Add the probe (a) pair as a compiler test.

Not covered by any filed task; #4603 (done) introduced strict equality.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (probe-confirmed at target/debug/reify 2026-10-12; introduced with #4603 γ's strict arity)
findings.verdict_notes: The arity check is `args.len() != target.type_params.len()` and takes no account of TypeParam::default. entity.rs::check_type_param_bounds does honour defaults. The two positions are inconsistent, as claimed.

findings.title: An arity mismatch inside a parametric alias body is a silent None, surfacing as a bare 'unresolved type'
findings.statement:
In the nested-parametric-alias arm of resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst, `if got < required_params || got > total_params { return None; }` emits nothing. The direct-use path resolve_parameterized_alias runs the same test and pushes 'type alias X expects N type argument(s), got M'.

Probe (c): `type P<T> = List<T>; type Q<X> = P<X, X>; param q : Q<Int> = [1]` reports only 'unresolved type: Q<Int>' plus a cascade ('list literal cannot satisfy annotation <error>'). Nothing names P or the arity.

The pub-alias def-site guard (validate_pub_parametric_alias_def_site) does not catch it either for a non-pub alias. INV-2 (a violation names the invariant and the values) is broken on this path.
findings.proposal:
Emit the same arity diagnostic in the nested arm, anchored at use_site.span as #6477 established for alias-body diagnostics. Finding 1's bind_type_args makes this automatic. Add probe (c) as a test.

Not covered by any filed task (#7839 is about dropped nested args, not arity).
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (probe-confirmed at target/debug/reify 2026-10-12)
findings.verdict_notes: Lines ~3556-3558 hold `if got < required_params || got > total_params { return None; }` with no diagnostic. resolve_parameterized_alias at line 2530 does report the arity error.

findings.title: Realization cache stores a bare handle; cache-hit parity is emulated by hand, via a parallel cross-build map, or not at all
findings.statement: docs/invariants.md lists INV-BUILD-3 ('a cache-hit short-circuit produces the same observable side-effect set as the path it short-circuits') as enforced(test). The cache value cannot carry that set, because Engine.realization_cache is RealizationCache<KernelHandle>, a bare terminal handle. A cold realization has more facets than that: terminal handle, resolved repr, meshed-from egress body, SweptKind classification, topology-attribute entries and morph source. Each facet the hit path cannot rebuild from the handle got its own ad-hoc remedy. (1) Repr: probe_realization_cache re-derives it with a second BRep fallback lookup and hand-writes step_handles, named_steps, named_step_reprs and produced_repr_out to mirror the miss path. (2) Meshed-from body: #6308's review fix (78df99be6d) added an engine-held VolumeMeshSources map that spans builds, because the hit returns ExecutedRealization::default(). Its lifetime is coupled to the cache only by a paired clear() in clear_realization_cache. RealizationCache.evict_family (engine_edit.rs ×2, engine_build.rs) evicts terminals but never touches it, so two containers describing one realization follow different eviction policies. (3) SweptKind: swept_kind_table.record(last_id, kind) runs only on the miss path inside execute_realization_ops. The table is reset on every surface, so on a cache-served terminal post_process_feature_datum_projections (reached through run_post_processes on build and tessellate surfaces) receives history=None. Its feature_datum_bundle then loses the construction-history Axis/Direction candidate, which can turn a unique datum into FeatureDatumAmbiguous + Undef on the second build only. No test builds the same module twice with a cache hit and reads swept kinds; swept_kind_classifier_e2e's two-build test uses different modules. (4) Topology attributes: these are documented as a 'Known limitation' in execute_realization_ops' rustdoc and pinned by a debug_assert that the table is empty. The S2 PRD's Open question 1 and B-δ4 consider only the MeshedVolume facet, and S1 λ #9050 moves volume_mesh_sources into EngineCaches as a separate field.
findings.proposal: Make the cache value the realization's whole result. Proposed type: `CachedRealization { terminal: KernelHandle, repr: ReprKind, egress_body: KernelHandle, swept_kind: Option<SweptKind>, attribute_entries: AttributeSnapshot }`, built by one constructor from S2's `RealizationStatus::Realized` plus `ExecutedRealization`. Apply it to RealizationOutputs and PerBuildState through a single `apply_realized(&CachedRealization, outputs)`. The miss path calls the same fn after it inserts, so hit and miss share one writer and INV-BUILD-3 holds by construction rather than by a parity test. The invariant's definition lives on the type; the debug_assert becomes a check that apply_realized re-seeded the attribute and swept-kind tables. Deletable: volume_mesh_sources.rs (the map, record/egress_body, the Engine field, its clear pairing and its reset_per_build_state row), the probe's hand-written side effects and its tautological debug_assert_eq, the 'Known limitation' rustdoc paragraph, and the separate morph-source stash on a hit. evict_family then evicts every facet at once. It would have prevented the #3226 empty-table class, #6308's cache-served-egress fix (78df99be6d), and the swept-kind/attribute parity gaps above. Relation: extends S2 δ #9158 (δ moves probe_realization_cache into probe.rs and returns CacheHit{terminal, repr}; widen CacheHit to carry CachedRealization and close Open question 1 in that form) and S1 λ #9050 (drop volume_mesh_sources from EngineCaches instead of moving it). Not covered by either as filed.
findings.bug_history_link: 78df99be6d fix(6308): a cache-served VolumeMesh terminal exports the body it was meshed from; f1cea8b313 fix(6308) (esc-6308-14); #3226 empty topology_attribute_table on cache-served handle; #4349 double-insert / cross-kernel collision; #3437 false hit; prior fk-4696c8f0c6e4
findings.verdict_notes: Verified. RealizationCache.evict_family (realization_cache.rs) drops only terminals and intermediates, and never touches volume_mesh_sources. clear_realization_cache in engine_admin.rs clears volume_mesh_sources only on a full flush. swept_kind_table.record runs only inside execute_realization_ops, at the classify_swept_body site. The cache-hit path in probe_realization_cache has no swept-kind recording, and swept_kind_table is reset on every surface (engine_build.rs ~3446). The rustdoc 'Known limitation' on topology_attribute_table is present. I did not run the two-build scenario, so the FeatureDatumAmbiguous consequence rests on the code reading.

findings.title: Geometry redispatch is a per-template full scan whose 'already done' state is the emptiness of realization_inputs
findings.statement: redispatch_geometry_consuming_compute_nodes is called inside the per-template loop of build and build_snapshot. On every call it clones the whole graph (`graph_snapshot = state.snapshot.graph.clone()`) and scans all compute nodes, not only the current template's. Candidacy is `node_data.realization_inputs.is_empty()`, a one-shot latch encoded as the emptiness of a data field. The #5951 fixes bolted three guards in front of that latch: kernel_handle: Some(_) at the Phase-2 gate (ee5f4737fe), an all-content-None bail (4c6bc86a1a), and RedispatchPassState's failed_pretessellations/contentless_skips sets. emit_contentless_redispatch_warnings then rebuilds 'stranded' at end of build from those sets. The latch is still set before dispatch: node.realization_inputs is written, then run_compute_dispatch runs, and its `Err(_) => {}` arm drops the error with no diagnostic. A dispatch failure after the write therefore strands the node permanently and silently on its degraded first-dispatch value, the same silent-strand symptom #5951 was filed for. The sibling redispatch_as_printed_consuming_compute_nodes selects candidates with a different gate (has_ready_as_printed), so two passes over one graph run two candidacy rules. The root cause is cross-system: BuildStep has only Realize and HydrateCell, so the unified schedule never orders a geometry-consuming compute node after its input realizations, and the build compensates with repeated scans. S2 η keeps 'both redispatches … in today's order' in the walk's post-process set, and S2 §7 puts tessellate-surface redispatch out of scope.
findings.proposal: Give compute redispatch an explicit per-build state machine, scheduled by the DAG. Add `BuildStep::DispatchCompute(ComputeNodeId)`, emitted by the unified pass after the Realize steps of every realization the node's geometry args reference (the edge already exists as realization_read_cells/realization_inputs dependencies). The walk dispatches each node exactly once, when its inputs are realized. Track its outcome in a typed `RedispatchStatus { Pending, Dispatched { inputs_hash }, Failed(ErrorRef), Contentless }` map owned by the walk's per-build state. Transitions are written only by the step handler, and a Failed outcome emits a coded diagnostic instead of `Err(_) => {}`. Never infer status from `realization_inputs.is_empty()`. Deletable: the per-template full scan and graph clone, the kernel_handle-Some and content-None latch guards, RedispatchPassState.failed_pretessellations/contentless_skips, and the end-of-build reconstruction in emit_contentless_redispatch_warnings, which becomes a read of Contentless entries. It would have prevented #5951 (template order emptied a multi-case FEA solve; both fixes) and the residual Err-swallow strand. Relation: not covered. S2 η #9159 keeps today's post-process order, and §7 excludes tessellate redispatch; this lands naturally as a follow-up on η's walk.
findings.bug_history_link: ee5f4737fe fix(#5951): require a kernel-backed handle at the geometry redispatch gate; 4c6bc86a1a fix(#5951): never latch the redispatch gate on content-free inputs; #4726 / esc-3787-23 post-hydration re-dispatch pass
findings.verdict_notes: Candidacy is node_data.realization_inputs.is_empty(). graph_snapshot is cloned per call, though im:: structural sharing likely makes that clone cheap. node.realization_inputs is written before run_compute_dispatch. The Err(_) arm does nothing, with only a comment saying the step-1 assertion still passes. The end-of-build stranded warning reports only nodes whose realization_inputs are still empty, so a node that failed after the latch is silent. redispatch_as_printed_consuming_compute_nodes uses a separate has_ready_as_printed gate.

findings.title: Op-kind dispatch tables are locked to hand-written XKind::ALL arrays; per-variant census literals must be bumped by hand
findings.statement: compile_geometry_op dispatches each op family through a `(Kind, fn)` slice (PRIMITIVE_COMPILERS … PROFILE_COMPILERS) with a linear `lookup_*` returning Option. A miss becomes the runtime string error `no registered compiler for {:?}`. The 'compile-time' safety is lock_dispatch_table!, which asserts `table.len() == Kind::VARIANT_COUNT`. VARIANT_COUNT is `Self::ALL.len()`, and each of the nine `const ALL: [Self; N]` arrays in reify-compiler/src/types.rs is hand-written with no derive or exhaustive match tying it to the enum. Adding a variant to SweepKind without extending ALL leaves every lock green and ships a runtime lookup miss. On top of this sit a runtime uniqueness test file (dispatch_table_uniqueness.rs), test-local hand copies of every family (ALL_PRIMITIVE … ALL_PROFILE in compile_geometry_op_registry_completeness, a second ALL_SWEEP in the seeded meta-test, and ALL_* in compile_geometry_op_characterization.rs) and a registry_completeness helper whose only job is to make its own equality check seedable. There are also literal censuses that test prose rather than behaviour: DOCUMENTED_KIND_FAMILY_CENSUS = 53, `assert_eq!(total, 54)` and `assert_eq!(ALL_MODIFY.len(), 10)`. The window shows the cost. #5754 (868eb6b7b0): ALL_SWEEP silently omitted ExtrudeInfinite. #4192: 19a178b348 reconciled census literals the branch's own ModifyKind bump falsified, and e1ef20ef80 bumped four prose counts. reify-builtins already derives strum EnumIter/EnumCount for exactly this need.
findings.proposal: Replace each `*_COMPILERS` slice and its `lookup_*` with a total exhaustive match, e.g. `fn sweep_compiler(kind: SweepKind) -> SweepCompileFn { match kind { SweepKind::Loft => sweep_loft, … } }`, with no wildcard. A new variant is then a compile error at the one dispatch site, and compile_geometry_op loses its Option and the 'no registered compiler' error. Derive `strum::EnumIter` (and `EnumCount` if a count is still wanted) on the nine kind enums so test iteration uses `SweepKind::iter()`. Deletable: the nine hand ALL arrays and VARIANT_COUNT consts, lock_dispatch_table!, geometry_ops/dispatch_table_uniqueness.rs, registry_completeness and seeded_unregistered_sweep_variant_fails_registry_completeness, the test-local ALL_* copies, DOCUMENTED_KIND_FAMILY_CENSUS and the literal total/ALL_MODIFY asserts. ModifyKind's geometry_modify CASES lock can follow the same rule. It would have prevented #5754 and the #4192 census bumps. Relation: extends S13 δ #8750, which moves each family's table into geometry_ops/compile/<family>.rs but explicitly keeps lock_dispatch_table! and the uniqueness guard 're-pointed' (selector-resolution-factoring D5). Convert the tables to matches in that move instead.
findings.bug_history_link: 868eb6b7b0 fix(5754): ALL_SWEEP omitted SweepKind::ExtrudeInfinite; 19a178b348 fix(4192): reconcile the census literals this branch's own ModifyKind bump falsified; e1ef20ef80 fix(4192): bump the four non-Split GeometryOp censuses
findings.verdict_notes: Each Kind::ALL in reify-compiler/src/types.rs is a hand-written const array, with VARIANT_COUNT = ALL.len() and no derive or exhaustive match tying it to the enum. The size annotation only trips when the array is edited. Adding an enum variant without extending ALL leaves lock_dispatch_table green. The test-local ALL_SWEEP copies, DOCUMENTED_KIND_FAMILY_CENSUS = 53, assert_eq!(total, 54) and ALL_MODIFY.len() == 10 exist as described. The ALL_SWEEP omission of ExtrudeInfinite is documented in the SweepKind::VARIANT_COUNT doc. I did not verify the reify-builtins strum claim, and it is minor.

findings.title: Which fields of a GeometryOp are parents is encoded three times: a descriptor role column plus two duplicated OR-matches with unreachable! tails, and a third re-match per AttributeHistory
findings.statement: parent_handles_for_op and substitute_op_parents each read `descriptor_for(op.into()).expect(..).parent_role`. Each then repeats the same 22-variant SingleTarget OR-pattern, the Surface{grid} arm, the six-variant SingleProfile pattern and the Loft/LoftGuided arm, every one ending in `_ => unreachable!("descriptor role … but op lacks … field")`. The fact 'parents of op' therefore lives in three places: the hand-written ParentRole column in reify-ir and two inner matches that must agree with it. populate_attribute_history re-matches the op a fourth time per AttributeHistory variant, returning QueryFailed on mismatch. Drift is caught only at test time, by three ~50-case 'coverage-completeness' tests in engine_build/tests.rs that call these private fns and compare against GeometryOpDiscriminants::iter(). Yet substitute_op_parents' doc says it 'mirrors parent_handles_for_op's variant coverage exactly so the compiler flags drift', and geometry_op_to_operation's doc says 'Both helpers exhaustively match every GeometryOp variant; the compiler enforces drift'. Both claims are false (heuristic 1). geometry_op_to_operation also still carries `#[allow(dead_code)] // Wired … in step-8` although execute_realization_ops calls it. classify_op_input_reprs adds a fifth mechanism, `#[allow(unreachable_patterns)] _ => None`, so a new Operation silently becomes BRep-only. Adding a variant (task 4999 Surface, task 4192 OffsetSurface, implicit-solids' ImplicitSolid, whose manifest lists descriptor row + compiled_geometry_op_to_operation arm + classify_op_input_reprs arm) is a five-site checklist with mostly runtime enforcement.
findings.proposal: Give reify-ir two total accessors beside the GeometryOp enum: `GeometryOp::parents(&self) -> ParentHandles<'_>` and `GeometryOp::parents_mut(&mut self) -> ParentHandlesMut<'_>`. Each is one exhaustive match with no wildcard, the single home for which fields are parents. A new variant is then a compile error in exactly that pair. Derive ParentRole from `parents()` (or drop the column; reify-compiler's expects_geom_arg cross-check can call a derived `role()`). substitute_op_parents becomes `for h in op.parents_mut() { sub(h) }`. populate_attribute_history takes its parent handles from `op.parents()` and checks the history variant against the op discriminant once. classify_op_input_reprs drops its catch-all so a new Operation is a compile error. Deletable: the two duplicated OR-matches, eight unreachable! arms, the descriptor `.expect` calls, the three private-fn coverage tests (replaced by one behaviour test per role through the executor), and the stale dead_code allow. It would have prevented the Surface arm being added twice (task 4999) and the #4192 per-variant bumps. Relation: extends S2 β₁ #9154 and δ #9158, which move these fns verbatim into geometry_op_lowering.rs / realization_executor/. S23 ε₃ #9140 fixes only the descriptor prose (fk-e2730bcb8111), not the structure.
findings.bug_history_link: e1ef20ef80 fix(4192): bump the four non-Split GeometryOp censuses the new variant moves; task 4999 Surface arm added in both parent_handles_for_op and substitute_op_parents; implicit-solids manifest 'descriptor-row' obligation
findings.verdict_notes: Real: parent_handles_for_op and substitute_op_parents both read descriptor parent_role and both end role arms in unreachable!. substitute_op_parents' doc says it mirrors parent_handles_for_op 'so the compiler flags drift', which is false. The geometry_op_to_operation doc claims the compiler enforces drift, and that function still carries #[allow(dead_code)] with a stale step-8 comment. Overstated: geometry_op_to_operation is now a pure descriptor lookup rather than an exhaustive match, so it is not a third match site. The 'five-site checklist' is therefore somewhat inflated. The core duplication and the false docs hold.

findings.title: A realized step's (handle, repr) is split across parallel containers; seeding writes only the handle half
findings.statement: Inside one realization, execute_realization_ops keeps `realization_step_ids: Vec<GeometryHandleId>` and `realization_step_reprs: Vec<ReprKind>` 'in lockstep'. It finds an op's parent repr by searching the bare parent id's position in the id vector (`realization_step_ids.iter().position(|id| id == pid)`), even though step_handles already holds full KernelHandles. Across realizations, RealizationOutputs carries named_steps: HashMap<String, KernelHandle> and a sibling named_step_reprs: HashMap<String, ReprKind> (task 5033 Gap A). They are written together only at the executor's success insert and in probe_realization_cache. seed_cross_sub_named_steps, seed_cross_let_named_steps and realize_overridden_instance_into insert `named_steps["<sub>.<member>"]` with no repr, and module_named_steps (snapshot_named_steps) stores only handles, so a step's repr is lost at every template boundary. The cross-realization repr resolution therefore falls back to `{BRep}` for any seeded name. That is safe today only because voxel_pipeline_demand_overrides is intra-template, a limitation recorded nowhere near the seeding code. The S2 PRD keeps named_steps and named_step_reprs as separate RealizationOutputs borrows, and its RealizedTerminal {handle, repr} (ε) is applied only to the realization_handles oracle.
findings.proposal: Introduce one value type for a realized step, `RealizedStep { handle: KernelHandle, repr: ReprKind }` (S2 ε's RealizedTerminal can be that type), and use it as the element of the executor's step list, the value of named_steps and the value of module_named_steps. Seeding then copies whole steps, and an op's parent owner and repr are read from the typed step, never located by bare-id position. Deletable: named_step_reprs and its two insert sites, realization_step_reprs, the position-lookup filter_map, and the op_is_voxel_only_input-scoped by-name fallback with its long scoping comment. A cross-template isosurface (or any repr-sensitive cross-sub consumer) then dispatches with the producer's true repr instead of {BRep}. It would have prevented the 5033 Gap A class (repr blind to cross-realization parents) and the #4349-style bare-id matching. Relation: extends S2 ε #9157 (widen RealizedTerminal from the oracle to named_steps) and δ #9158 (RealizationOutputs / RealizationScratch keep the split today).
findings.bug_history_link: task 5033 Gap #2 Gap A (named_step_reprs introduced as a sibling map); #4349 same-integer GeometryHandleId collision across kernels; speculative for the seeded-repr loss
findings.verdict_notes: realization_step_ids and realization_step_reprs are kept in lockstep, and the parent repr is found via position lookup (~7736). named_step_reprs is inserted only at the success path (~9671) and in probe_realization_cache (~7328). seed_cross_sub_named_steps (~653) inserts only the KernelHandle into named_steps, with no repr. module_named_steps is HashMap<String, HashMap<String, KernelHandle>>, so repr is lost at the template boundary. The BRep fallback for seeded names follows. The finding is itself flagged as speculative for the seeded-repr loss.

findings.title: SweptKindTable is keyed by bare GeometryHandleId, breaching INV-GEO-2 that #4351 closed for its sibling table
findings.statement: INV-GEO-2 (docs/invariants.md) states 'Handle identity is (kernel, id)', and #4351 re-keyed TopologyAttributeTable by KernelHandle so a cross-kernel id collision is unrepresentable. SweptKindTable's own doc says it 'mirrors the TopologyAttributeTable shape', yet it is `HashMap<GeometryHandleId, SweptKind>`. execute_realization_ops records `swept_kind_table.record(last_id, kind)` from the bare realization_step_ids, and try_eval_feature_datum_projection looks it up with the bare id taken from Value::GeometryHandle. In a multi-kernel engine, an OCCT revolve terminal and a Manifold/OpenVDB terminal with the same kernel-local id share one entry. The non-revolve body's feature datum then gains a spurious Revolve axis candidate, or loses its own: last write wins. S1 ε #9043 moves the table into PerBuildState unchanged.
findings.proposal: Key SweptKindTable by KernelHandle (record from step_handles.last(), not realization_step_ids.last()), as TopologyAttributeTable already is, and add the same two-kernel same-id test (`topology_attribute_table_distinguishes_same_id_across_kernels` precedent). The lookup site needs the owner. Until #6366 gives Value::GeometryHandle its kernel, try_eval_feature_datum_projection should resolve the receiver through named_steps (which holds KernelHandle) rather than the value's bare id. Relation: not covered (#9043 moves the field as-is; #6366 owns the Value-side owner).
findings.bug_history_link: #4349 cross-kernel GeometryHandleId collision; #4351 re-key TopologyAttributeTable by KernelHandle
findings.verdict_notes: SweptKindTable.entries is HashMap<GeometryHandleId, SweptKind>, and record(last_id, kind) is called with a bare id at engine_build.rs ~9047. The structure matches the claim. The cross-kernel collision consequence is a latent, unobserved possibility. I did not re-check the lookup side in geometry_ops or whether TopologyAttributeTable is KernelHandle-keyed.

findings.title: 'Does this constraint/objective reach this auto?' is decided by six independent walks with six different edge sets
findings.statement:
The same relation, 'constraint or objective term C transitively reads auto A', is derived separately by each consumer, and each consumer uses different edges and different spelling rules.

The six derivations:
- (1) Layer 1, engine_eval.rs::filter_constraints_reading_autos via CellReadIndex::cells_reaching. Follows value-cell edges through @optimized cells. Admits only the OWNING scope's constraints. Bridges spellings additively.
- (2) Layer 4, engine_eval.rs::detect_underdetermined. Takes a GLOBAL forward read_closure over every template's constraints and objectives, then a reverse probe, auto_is_pinned_through_a_reader, gated on a stage-(g) alias oracle and a declaring-template guard. Its own doc says it 'never consults the ResolutionProblem'.
- (3) Cluster formation, resolve_order.rs::union_via_transitive_auto_owners over its own build_non_auto_cell_map (whose doc says it 'Mirrors build_dependent_cells' cell_map construction'). Spelling is as-is first, with a normalised fallback on a miss. The walk STOPS at @optimized cells, which (1) and (2) traverse.
- (4) engine_fixpoint.rs::constraints_reaching_auto, the E_EVAL_UNRESOLVED class and the constraint-decline gate. Follows realization→realization edges ONLY. Its doc records 'Known limitation … does NOT chase value-cell→value-cell read chains'.
- (5) and (6) engine_edit.rs::Engine.edit_param (line 1732) and edit_source (line 4058). Direct reads only: `trace.reads.iter().any(|r| auto_ids.contains(r))`.

The #5467 history is precisely the disagreement between (1) and (2). Commit 02913857af: 'a loud, correct warning had become a silent wrong answer'. f603a9e717: 'Layers 1 and 4 disagreed'. d3b5c320da fixed a member-name collision that unflagged a free auto. 7be73738b1 (esc-5467-18) removed a disjunct that 'converted main's loud TRUE warning into a silent Undef' because layer 1 only filters the owning scope.

The doc on CellReadIndex records the hazard but leaves it to discipline: 'Making only ONE side additive is worse than making neither'. Live tasks are still filed against the seams: #6649 (cross-sub realization-backed constraint escapes the E_EVAL_UNRESOLVED net and gets a WRONG W_UNDERDETERMINED, i.e. (4) vs (2)) and #7069 (a third detect_underdetermined disjunct that no longer exists in the code).
findings.verdict_notes: Opened the sites. resolve_order.rs::union_via_transitive_auto_owners stops at @optimized cells (is_optimized_userfn_cell -> continue) and build_non_auto_cell_map's doc says it mirrors build_dependent_cells. engine_fixpoint.rs::constraints_reaching_auto follows realization_reads edges only; the doc on realizations_reaching_auto records the known limitation about value-cell chains. engine_edit.rs lines 1732 and 4058 test only direct reads (`trace.reads.iter().any(|r| auto_ids.contains(r))`). Sites (5) and (6) are a dirty-cone gate, so they are a looser fit for 'the same relation' than the other four. The divergent edge sets across the walks are real.

findings.title: eval_cached is a 1,900-line parity twin whose production inputs reduce it to replaying the last cold eval
findings.statement:
Engine::eval_cached (engine_eval.rs 8084–9641) and dispatch_merged_cluster_solve_cached (9642–9957) have exactly one production caller: reify-lsp diagnostics.rs::compute_diagnostics_with_state. That caller invokes it only when `last_content_hash == compiled.content_hash` and the engine is initialised. On any change it builds a fresh `Engine::new(checker, None)` and runs eval(). Every reify-lsp construction site passes no kernel and never calls with_solver, and reify-lsp's production code never calls set_param_and_invalidate or edit_param.

The consequences for each part of eval_cached:
- Its re-serve gate is `!param_overrides.contains_key && !cache.is_dirty && cache.get(..)` (≈8257). In production it therefore re-serves every cell that has a cache entry.
- Its cache-miss arms (with their own R3d/R3e copies) run only for cells that eval() committed without a cache leg, which are exactly the INV-EVAL-1 gaps γ #8861 closes.
- Its solver sub-pass is gated on has_active_solver and is unreachable in production until #6695.
- It consults no imported_file_hashes, so it cannot detect external-file staleness either.
- The one-hop dirty_reasons mechanism (invalidate_dependents / is_dirty / clear_dirty / clear_dependents_dirty) is read only by eval_cached.

Yet the window's eval-vs-eval_cached fix class was paid against this twin: #5240 (guarded groups → cold fallback), #5238 (re-serve determinacy), #2259/#2266 (dropped diagnostics, garbage cyclic lets), #8028 and #7038. S4 carries it forward as a third mode in four leaves: CellPass::CachedMiss (η), ServePath::EvalCached (κ), CACHED_SINGLE/CACHED_MERGED policies (ζ), and υ's third differential column. 23 integration test files drive it. This is the same shape the S4 ruling deleted for edit_source (δ: 'dead parity twin'), except that eval_cached has one narrow production caller.
findings.bug_history_link: 534808277d fix(5240) eval_cached falls back to cold eval(); fbaf24c367 fix(5238) Let re-serve determinacy; #2259, #2266 (done); #8028, #7038 (live); b1a9c8e1e0
findings.verdict_notes: The only non-test caller is reify-lsp/src/diagnostics.rs (~line 314), guarded by content_unchanged and engine-initialised. Otherwise it builds Engine::new(checker, None) and runs eval(). with_solver appears in reify-lsp only in a test (~line 2399). The other eval_cached calls are in cache.rs tests. Sizes: eval_cached spans 8084-9641 and the dispatch twin 9642-9957, about 1,870 lines combined. 'Reduces to replaying the last cold eval' is interpretive but follows from these inputs.

findings.title: CellReadIndex keeps forward and reverse read graphs as two hand-synchronised builds; reverse is not transpose(forward) by construction
findings.statement:
Question (3) for the deps.rs maps is answered by S3 δ #8691: DependencyGraph::reverse() is an inversion of the one forward walk. CellReadIndex in engine_eval.rs is outside that scope.

How the two directions are built:
- Its FORWARD direction is a lazy walk, read_closure, over cell_map, re-running extract_value_deps per visit.
- Its REVERSE direction is a separately built, OnceCell-memoised HashMap, cells_reaching's `reverse`, built by its own extract_value_deps sweep.
- Both must apply the same two-namespace bridge (raw plus normalize_cell_id spelling). The rule is restated at three insert sites: read_closure's `push`, the reverse KEYING, and the reverse SEEDING. Layer 4 then compensates with a fourth, the re-projection in auto_is_pinned_through_a_reader.

The doc carries the consistency argument in prose ('It is sound because `push` is the ONLY writer…'; 'the falsehood this comment carried until task #5467 step-19'; 'until amendment round 2'). Two of the four #5467 fixes are this invariant breaking: 02913857af made the keying additive, and the seeding was added by review suggestion 6.

The index is also shared through a caller-owned `OnceCell<CellReadIndex>`. Whichever of build_solver_problem or detect_underdetermined calls get_or_init first fixes the unfold budgets, and a debug_assert_eq! documents that 'the losing caller's budgets are silently discarded'. That is temporal coupling (h7) guarded only in debug builds.

The namespace bridge itself is a meaningful-string parser (h12, normalize_cell_id over strip_collection_indices). S3 ι #8704 types it but keeps both spellings (OQ-2 → c).
findings.proposal:
Fold CellReadIndex onto S3's DependencyGraph rather than keeping a fourth read structure. Add a named projection `DependencyGraph::template_reads()`, the cross-template non-auto default_expr read edges, keyed by the canonical InstancePath::structure_scope id. Each raw instance-path spelling becomes an alias edge to its canonical node, added once at construction. reverse() then transposes it with no spelling knowledge, so 'additive in both directions' becomes a property of the edge set, not of three insert sites.

The unfold budgets become constructor arguments of the one graph built per eval. Pass `&DependencyGraph` (not an OnceCell) to consumers, so no consumer can win get_or_init with different budgets.

Enforce reverse == transpose(forward) at construction with a debug check, and pin it with S3 δ's inversion-law test (B5) extended to template_reads.

What dies: CellReadIndex's `reverse` OnceCell, the additive keying and seeding blocks and their prose, read_closure's dual-insert `push`, the budget debug_assert, and resolve_order::build_non_auto_cell_map.

It would have prevented 02913857af and the seeding half of f603a9e717.

Coverage: extends S3 δ #8691 (DependencyGraph) and ι #8704 (InstancePath). Neither names CellReadIndex, union_via_transitive_auto_owners or build_non_auto_cell_map. S4 ν #8860 only moves CellReadIndex to solver_problem.rs. Pairs with the AutoReach finding, which is its main consumer.
findings.bug_history_link: 02913857af fix(5467) make cells_reaching's reverse map ADDITIVE, like read_closure; f603a9e717; review esc-5467-12 blocking #1; review round 3 suggestion 10 (budget debug_assert)
findings.verdict_notes: read_closure is a lazy forward walk that re-runs extract_value_deps per visit. The reverse map is a separate OnceCell-memoised HashMap built by its own extract_value_deps sweep (~line 2365). Both apply the raw-plus-normalised spelling bridge at separate insert sites. The index is shared through a caller-owned OnceCell<CellReadIndex>, with the budget note at ~line 936. Reverse is not derived from forward by construction.

findings.title: A param edit's persistence is split between edit_param and a caller follow-up; param_overrides conflates user pins with last-solve results
findings.proposal:
Give the edit transaction sole ownership of override state. Split the map into a typed `ParamPins { user: BTreeMap<ValueCellId, Value>, solved_autos: BTreeMap<ValueCellId, Value> }`, or drop solved_autos and let the cold path re-solve, per #6208's decision.

edit_param (ε #8863's EditTransaction) then records the user pin as its FIRST step, before any phase runs. Persistence is a field of the transaction outcome (EditMode::Commit vs EditMode::Preview for edit_check) rather than a second caller call.

What dies:
- set_param_and_invalidate (MCP calls edit_param alone);
- the post-edit cache.invalidate of a freshly committed node;
- invalidate_dependents and dirty_reasons, which die anyway if eval_cached is reduced to replay.

Enforce it by having every phase read pins through `EditTransaction::pin(cell)`, which already contains the new value, and pin it with a B11-shaped test: edit a guarded-group Param member twice and assert the second value survives the guard phase.

Coverage: not covered. S3 explicitly leaves dirty_reasons out of scope (§7). #6208 (pending) covers only whether an auto override stays in auto_params. This extends ε #8863 (EditTransaction) and should land before or with ι #8865's GuardPhase::Edit override honouring.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative for the ι interaction; history: task 2017 (overrides consulted by eval), #6208 (auto override semantics, filed by #5467 amendment), mcp_context comment 'edit_param must succeed before mutating engine state via set_param_and_invalidate'
findings.verdict_notes: edit_param writes param_overrides only for solver-resolved autos (~line 1772). It commits the edited value to the snapshot and records the param's cache entry (~1208-1227). reify-cli mcp_context.rs ~line 612 calls edit_param and then set_param_and_invalidate. That second call inserts the override, invalidates the param's own cache entry (removing the one edit_param just recorded) and marks dependents dirty. The persistence split is real temporal coupling. The S4 iota interaction is speculative, as the finding itself says.

findings.title: Support-to-constraint realization has five independent homes; the in-flight PRDs each extend a different one
findings.statement:
Answer to the brief's ask: after S15/S16/S5 as designed, DECODE is one function (S15 γ #8683 SupportSpec), but REALIZATION (which DOFs of which nodes a declared support constrains) is still decided at five sites. Each has its own target vocabulary, kind semantics and refusal policy.
(1) modal_ops::build_dirichlet_bcs/face_realization: box-face names x_min…z_max via face_bound; kind-aware; a Pinned beam end becomes FaceRealization::PinTransverse (Z on the face plus a Y anchor) when another distinct face is named (FaceCompany); the beam axis is hard-wired to x (per_face_bcs asserts axis == 0).
(2) elastic_static::any_support_targets + SYNTHETIC_CLAMP_FACE (dims path): only the string "root" is recognized; the root is clamped whatever the list says; kind-blind.
(3) elastic_static::target_node_set (realized path): kind-blind union of resolved face handles, clamped on all 3 DOFs.
(4) buckling.rs::solve_buckling_trampoline: `let _ = &value_inputs[5]`, then a hard-coded pin-pin on the z faces (`for k_face in [0, nz]`).
(5) reify_solver_elastic::shell_solve calls build_support_bcs(&root_nodes, SupportKind::Fixed, Shell). The solver crate's own SupportKind×SupportBodyKind policy table is never constructed with Pinned in production.
So the same declaration, [PinnedSupport("x_min"), FixedSupport("x_max")], gives four different boundary problems: a transverse pin (modal), a full clamp (elastic body path, per target_node_set's own doc), a refusal (elastic dims after S16 μ #9119), and pin-pin (buckling today).
The plans keep this split. ξ #9120 extracts `realize_supports(&[SupportSpec], nodes, BeamDims)` for modal only. μ #9119 adds a dims-only FeaDimsSupportNotRealized. #7081 is told to 'port modal's build_dirichlet_bcs', but buckling's column axis is z and realize_supports' PinTransverse is x-only, so the port must be a copy with the axes swapped. coordinate-target-fea C4 adds a sixth representation (SolveBoundary.point_supports/apply_face_clamp) for elastic only, and each consumer separately wires PointSupport (#8256, #7189, #7081 amendment (a), #7143 for modal selectors). #5312 has to find 'any analogous kernel-less read' of a String target by search.
findings.proposal:
Create one support-realization module in reify-solver-elastic, next to S16 ο's BoxFace/StructuredBoxMesh (#9121), so that kind semantics and target resolution each have one home.
(a) `SupportPolicy`: one table `fn constraint_pattern(kind: SupportKind, body: SupportBodyKind, idealization: Idealization) -> ConstraintPattern`, extending shell_boundary::build_support_bcs. Idealization is `Continuum | BeamEnd{axis}`, so modal's simple-support idealization is a declared policy row parameterized by axis rather than a modal-private FaceCompany rule.
(b) `resolve_support_target(&SupportSpec, &BoundaryView) -> Result<NodeSet, SupportRefusal>`, where `BoundaryView = StructuredBox{mesh, axis} | Realized(&BoundaryAssociation) | Points(&[PointTarget])`.
(c) Each trampoline declares a `SupportCapability` (which kinds and target forms it realizes). Every unrealizable support becomes ONE coded `FeaSupportNotRealized` Error naming the support and its span, generalizing μ's dims-only code to all solvers.
What dies: modal DeclaredSupport/support_targets/face_bound/face_company, elastic any_support_targets/SYNTHETIC_CLAMP_FACE, buckling's two hard-coded BC loops, and μ's dims-specific refusal arm. #7081 and #8256/#7143 become calls to the module instead of ports.
Bug classes it would have prevented: #6663 (kind ignored in modal), #6980 (count-based realization), INV-PD-1 A1 (buckling drops supports), and the root/x_min vocabulary split (next finding).
Relation: extends #8683 (decode), #9120 (modal-only seam), #9119 (dims-only refusal), #9121 (BoxFace), #7081 (buckling port) and coordinate-target-fea C4. No leaf owns one cross-solver realization policy.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(6663) honor support KIND per face in modal build_dirichlet_bcs / dedup the modal Dirichlet set / SelectorNoMatch names the offending support type; fix(6980) make PinnedSupport realization face-local, not count-based; trampoline-param-drop-closure A1 (#7081, buckling discards supports); #5312 interim shim touching both elastic_static and modal_ops reads
findings.verdict_notes: Verified the five realization sites exist. modal_ops::face_bound is a box-face-only table and per_face_bcs skips unknown names. elastic_static has SYNTHETIC_CLAMP_FACE ("root"), any_support_targets and target_node_set. buckling.rs::solve_buckling_trampoline does `let _ = &value_inputs[5]` and hard-codes pin-pin on the z faces (its comment says support-driven BCs are deferred with no live task). shell_solve.rs calls build_support_bcs with SupportKind::Fixed only. The 'refusal after S16 mu' part describes planned work, not current code. The rest holds.

findings.title: Modal-family failures are Completed outcomes carrying Error diagnostics and fabricated degenerate values
findings.statement:
The ComputeOutcome contract says `Completed.diagnostics` are 'Non-fatal diagnostics' and `Failed` 'should include at least one Severity::Error'. The only statement of the policy 'Error → ComputeOutcome::Failed' is a comment inside elastic_static (the '2929 severity policy' note at the bc_override block). Nothing enforces it.
modal_ops.rs production code builds ComputeOutcome::Completed 13 times and ComputeOutcome::Failed 0 times, against 12 Diagnostic::error constructions. Every modal-family error (E_ModalNoMassMatrix, E_ModalDampingMaterialNotDamped, E_MechanismModalClosedChain, E_MechanismModalNoMass, E_TransientForcingMissing, E_TransientModalResultMissing) returns Completed with degenerate_modal_result()/degenerate_displacement_history(). Those results contain fabricated fields: mass/stiffness norms Real(0.0), boundary_conditions [], modes [].
run_compute_dispatch's Completed arm writes that value into the output cells via complete_compute_dispatch_atomically. The cell is not marked failed (engine_eval.rs's DispatchError::Failed arm), so downstream .ri code and the next trampoline compute on a well-formed empty result. The downstream compensation is in the code: modal_result_missing_outcome exists to catch an upstream modal failure ('typically indicates the upstream modal analysis … failed'), added by #4131. In the same family the shell_extract/multi_case/elastic trampolines return Failed (shell_extract_compute.rs: 14 Failed, 1 Completed).
findings.proposal:
Enforce the invariant 'an Error-severity diagnostic ⇒ Failed' at the single dispatch boundary and at construction.
(1) Add a constructor `ComputeOutcome::completed(result, diagnostics)` that debug-asserts no Severity::Error, and make the struct-literal form crate-private over time.
(2) Add one check in Engine.invoke_compute_trampoline / OptimizedComputeDispatcher (the same boundary that holds the catch_unwind guard, or analysis-stratum's single `on_completed` site) that turns a Completed-with-Error into Failed and adds a coded `ComputeOutcomeIncoherent` diagnostic, so a release build cannot cache a failure as a value.
(3) Convert modal_ops' 12 error paths to Failed.
What dies: degenerate_modal_result (3 consumers), degenerate_displacement_history, placeholder use on error paths, modal_result_missing_outcome's role as an upstream-failure detector, #7100 β's 'honest-Undef flips on the degenerate builders' (no degenerate builders remain), and one of #8693 ζ's three builder inputs.
Bug classes it would have prevented: #4131 (transient computing on a failed upstream), #6981 (two 'no modes' outcomes at different severities), and the #7012/#7100 fake-norm flips on error paths.
Relation: not covered. S15 #8693/#8702 rebuild these outcomes' value and codes but keep the Completed posture, and PVAC #7100 explicitly keeps 'error-path builder accompanied by its diagnostic'.
findings.bug_history_link: #4131 (transient guard for missing/Undef modal_result), #6981 (reconcile severity of the two 'no modes' outcomes), fix(7012) report mechanism_modal's lumped-undefined fields as honest Undef, #7100 β degenerate-builder honesty flips
findings.verdict_notes: Production modal_ops has about 11 ComputeOutcome::Completed sites and no ComputeOutcome::Failed anywhere in the file, so the count of 13 is slightly high. Error diagnostics are returned inside Completed (no_mass_matrix_outcome around line 1210, degenerate results with Real(0.0) norms and an empty boundary_conditions list). The ComputeOutcome doc in dispatch.rs says Completed carries non-fatal diagnostics and Failed carries an Error diagnostic. shell_extract_compute.rs has 14 Failed sites. The modal behaviour is partly documented as deliberate, but it is real and nothing enforces the policy.

findings.title: Modal support decode has no refusal arm: an unrecognized target or support kind silently constrains nothing, including the elastic 'root' spelling
findings.statement:
support_targets reads only items whose `target` is a `Value::String`, and maps every type_name other than "PinnedSupport" to DeclaredSupport::Fixed (doc: 'FixedSupport (and every unrecognized support type name)'). face_bound then recognizes only x_min…z_max, and per_face_bcs skips (`continue`) any other name.
No diagnostic names a skipped support; the only Info notes are for Pinned end faces. So `FixedSupport(target: "root")`, the spelling every elastic dims example uses and the one SYNTHETIC_CLAMP_FACE recognizes, produces an empty Dirichlet set in modal: a free-free solve that surfaces only as W_ModalRigidBodyMode (small models) or E_ModalNoModesComputed (above DENSE_FALLBACK_MAX_DIM). The same happens to a non-String target (the selector form #5312 introduces) and to any Support kind without a String `target` (PointSupport's `at`).
run_modal_analysis still echoes the raw `options.boundary_conditions` list into ModalResult.boundary_conditions (`field_or(options, "boundary_conditions", …)`), so the result claims supports that were not applied.
S16 decides that "root" parses as BoxFace::XMin 'at the elastic dims entry only' (OQ 2), and μ's FeaDimsSupportNotRealized refuses unrealizable supports on elastic dims only, so modal keeps the silent skip after both PRDs.
findings.proposal:
Make the modal realization total over its input. Every SupportSpec either resolves to a BoxFace or yields a coded `FeaSupportNotRealized` Error naming the support (the same code as the previous finding's generalization). The "root" alias is resolved by BoxFace::parse for every box-mesh consumer, not only the elastic dims entry. S15 γ's SupportSpec decode rejects unknown kinds with UnknownVariant, never a Fixed fallback.
What dies: the `_ => None` silent-skip path in per_face_bcs, the 'every unrecognized support type name' Fixed fallback, and the need for a free-free rigid-body warning to stand in for a support error.
Relation: extends #8683 (kind decode) and #9120 (realize_supports keeps the skip), and is a sibling to #9119 (elastic-only refusal). Not otherwise covered.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(6663) (support KIND was ignored in modal); fix(6980) (a support naming no face used to flip another face's realization); #5312's interim shim had to touch modal_ops' String read
findings.verdict_notes: support_targets accepts only a Value::String target and maps every kind other than PinnedSupport to Fixed. face_bound recognises only x_min through z_max, and per_face_bcs skips the rest with `continue`. modal_ops handles no 'root' target; a test near line 8098 treats it as an ignored static-path name. run_modal_analysis echoes options.boundary_conditions via field_or (line 1671). No refusal diagnostic is emitted for a skipped support.

findings.title: Result echo and unpopulatable fields are chosen per builder as raw Values, not typed and not derived from what the solve applied
findings.statement:
Answer to the brief's other two asks.
First: fields a trampoline cannot populate are not typed as absent. Each builder spells `Value::Undef` or a literal by hand, and the honesty rule (INV-PD-2 C2′) is checked only by value-level tests (V7).
Second: options are echoed into results by hand per builder, with different dispositions for the same declared field. ModalResult.boundary_conditions is the raw options list in run_modal_analysis (field_or), `[]` in degenerate_modal_result, and `Undef` in mechanism_modal_result_value. ModalResult.damping echoes the caller's descriptor even when the plan applied nothing: #6875's W_MechanismModalUnsupportedDamping text says 'ModalResult.damping still echoes … intent … is NOT applied'. Mode.damping_ratio is `Real(0.0)` on that unsupported path.
The echo reads `options` independently of the decision that consumed it (build_dirichlet_bcs / plan_modal_damping), so the echo and the applied BCs or damping can disagree, e.g. a Pinned face realized as a clamp, or a skipped support.
S15 C3 defines build_modal_result(ModalResultParts) but leaves the Parts fields producer-supplied, so the per-builder choice survives the merge into one builder.
findings.proposal:
Type the parts.
(1) `ModalResultParts { boundary_conditions: Applied<Vec<SupportSpec>>, damping: Applied<DampingDescriptor>, mass_matrix_norm: Field<f64>, … }`, where `Field<T> = Populated(T) | Degraded(&'static str)` and `Applied<T>` can only be built from the realization or plan output: DirichletRealization gains `applied: Vec<SupportSpec>`, and ModalDampingPlan gains `applied: Option<DampingDescriptor>`.
(2) build_modal_result maps Degraded to `Undef` at one site, so a fake 0.0 or [] cannot be expressed. PVAC's C1′ dispositions (#7100/#7102) are then read off the Parts type instead of a parallel declaration.
What dies: the per-builder `field_or(options, …)` echoes and the hand-spelled Undef/0.0 literals in three ModalResult and two Mode builders.
Bug classes it would have prevented: #6875 (damping echo added by hand), #7012 (norms flipped to honest Undef by hand), #7100 (degenerate-builder flips).
Relation: extends #8693 (ζ builder) and #7100 (PVAC modal family). Neither specifies typed parts or echo-from-realization.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(6875) echo ModalOptions.damping on the mechanism ModalResult; fix(7012) populate mechanism_modal's matrix norms / report lumped-undefined fields as honest Undef; #7100 degenerate-builder honest-Undef flips
findings.verdict_notes: boundary_conditions is the echoed options list in run_modal_analysis (line 1671), an empty List in degenerate_modal_result (line 1320), and Undef in mechanism_modal_result_value (line 2064). Each builder hand-spells Undef or a literal. The damping echo is taken from options independently of what was applied. Mostly a consistency and SPOT issue; the claim about S15 C3 is plan-level and I did not check it.

findings.title: Multi-case results are emitted as Value::Map{"cases"} despite declared structures, and the GUI identifies them by key-sniffing
findings.statement:
stdlib declares `structure def MultiCaseResult { param cases : Map<String, ElasticResult> }` (fea_multi_case.ri) and `structure def MultiCaseBucklingResult { param cases : Map<String, BucklingResult> }` (solver_buckling.ri). Both trampolines instead return `Value::Map{"cases" -> Map}`. multi_case.rs calls this 'the de-facto runtime MultiCaseResult contract'.
multi_load_dispatch::detect_multi_case_result identifies a multi-case result by 'is a Map whose "cases" value is a non-empty Map'. It carries no type identity, so it returns Some for a buckling multi-case result and for any user Map with a "cases" key. gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs then emits FeaCaseChanged from whichever such cell sorts first.
Because the values are Maps rather than StructureInstances, S15's C4 builder/field_layout parity test and PVAC cannot see these two result types at all.
findings.proposal:
Emit both results through one registry_free builder per structure (S15 C5), as StructureInstances with type_name MultiCaseResult / MultiCaseBucklingResult. Replace detect_multi_case_result with a match on the type identity that returns a typed `MultiCaseKind::{Elastic, Buckling}`, so the GUI routes each kind explicitly.
What dies: the 'de-facto runtime contract' Map shape, the GUI key-sniff, and multi_case_result_value's Map fixture shape.
Relation: not covered. S15 C3/C4 enumerate ElasticResult, ModalResult, Mode and MassProperties only, so this would extend #8690/#8693's builder list to the two multi-case structures.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative
findings.verdict_notes: fea_multi_case.ri declares `structure def MultiCaseResult` with a Map of cases. multi_case.rs and buckling_multi_case.rs emit Value::Map{"cases" -> Map} instead. detect_multi_case_result only checks that the value is a Map whose "cases" key holds a non-empty Map, so it also matches buckling multi-case results and arbitrary user Maps. gui engine.rs calls it at lines 1852, 8969 and 9053. The shape is documented as a deliberate runtime contract, but the stringly-typed detection is real.

findings.title: Combined free-standing solve returns converged=true without ever asserting nullity == 4, and its residual is blind to zero rows
findings.statement: The line-only path rejects any D whose nullity is not exactly 4: validate_explicit returns NullityMismatch. The combined (surfaces) path does not enforce this anywhere. form_find_explicit_combined_relaxed hand-builds a SpectrumClassification with the field `nullity: 4` forged over the observed value. The outer loop gates only on all_node_equilibrium_residual_relative <= 1e-11. After convergence, form_find_free_surfaces runs `result.nullity = classify_spectrum(&d_final, ..).nullity` and returns `converged = true`. The value is stored but never compared with 4, and a code comment merely asserts it will 'reliably report nullity 4'. The residual only proves x lies in null(D). Any D with more than four null directions also satisfies it. Such a D arises from an isolated node, or from two disconnected components that each carry an all-ones mode. In both cases the line-only path would return NullityMismatch. The residual criterion also guards only global d_scale <= 0. The anchored sibling was fixed per row in #6119 and #7046 so a zero row reads as INFINITY. Here a single zero row is vacuously 0 whenever any other row is non-zero. Reached by reading the code, not executed. No free-standing test builds an isolated or disconnected node; the only 'isolated' tests are anchored (surfaces_solve_rejects_isolated_free_node_*).
findings.proposal: Make the 'valid free-standing form has nullity d+1' invariant a single function, `FreeStandingForm::certify(d, x) -> Result<Nullity4, FreeFormError>`. validate_explicit calls it and so does the tail of form_find_free_surfaces. After the fixed point, form_find_free_surfaces returns NullityMismatch (or SearchDidNotConverge, to match the existing contract) when the reclassified nullity != 4. Also reject any zero or NaN row in all_node_equilibrium_residual_relative, as the anchored criterion does. Add two RED tests: an isolated node and a disconnected pair, each through the combined Explicit and GroupRatios entries. Deletable: the comment-only assurance at the end of form_find_free_surfaces, and the `nullity: 4` forged struct literal (SpectrumClassification gets a `forced_nullity` constructor so observed and forced values cannot be confused). This prevents the vacuous-zero class of #6119, fixed only on the anchored side. NOT covered: #8628 and the PRD touch input validation only. #7801 (pending) aligns the normaliser but does not mention the nullity check.
findings.bug_history_link: #6119 (vacuous-zero free-row block, anchored only), #6413 (free-standing twin, normaliser only), #7801 (pending: free criterion per-row alignment)
findings.verdict_notes: form_find_free_surfaces sets result.nullity from classify_spectrum after convergence and returns Ok. Nothing compares it to 4. The only EXPECTED_NULLITY check is in validate_explicit (line path). form_find_explicit_combined_relaxed forges nullity: 4. all_node_equilibrium_residual_relative uses a global d_scale and only guards d_scale <= 0, so a single zero row is not flagged. No other non-test code reads .nullity.

findings.title: ForceDensityProblem (#8628) as specified still leaves the free GroupRatios spec, aniso stress, finiteness and the error text outside the validated boundary
findings.statement: The answer to 'does each entry validate what the last panic taught it' is yes, today. These are the current copies of the member-index range check: validate_members (form_find.rs), validate_explicit, form_find_explicit_combined_relaxed, form_find_group_ratios, form_find_group_ratios_combined, and the in-loop Explicit arm of form_find_free_surfaces. The last one re-runs the length, range and sign checks on every one of up to 200 iterations, after the bootstrap solve has already validated them. #8628's C1 covers the anchored and Explicit shapes. It does not cover four things, so it would leave them as the next 'fourth site'. (1) The GroupRatios spec (group_ids, seed_ratios, reference_group) has its own validation block. The four-check block (length, n_groups==0/reference/group id range, zero seed, member range) is copied verbatim into form_find_group_ratios and form_find_group_ratios_combined, and crack_group_ids repeats part of it in the trampoline. C1's `new(.., q, ..)` has no home for it. (2) AnisotropicSurfaceStress is not an f64, so 'every σ > 0' does not obviously cover sigma_warp, sigma_weft or a finite non-zero warp_dir. (3) Finiteness is checked nowhere. `s <= 0.0` accepts NaN σ (`form_find_anchored_surfaces`, the aniso entry and `form_find_free_surfaces` all spell it that way), `qi > 0.0` accepts +inf for a cable, and NaN coordinates pass the degenerate-area test because `NaN <= eps` is false. Downstream, anchored paths misreport SingularReducedStiffness. The free paths reach `classify_spectrum`'s `.expect("...must succeed")` panic. That panic is plausible but unverified, since it depends on faer's behaviour for non-finite input. (4) DimensionMismatch is one variant for four causes: length mismatch, member endpoint, surface corner and anchor out of range. It carries no offending value, and the trampoline's `describe` text says only 'force_densities length does not match the member count'. That violates the 'informatively' leg of h10. The trampoline already range-checks every index (crack_index_pairs, check_index), so the kernel checks are a second, uncoordinated mechanism rather than redundant enforcement from one definition.
findings.proposal: Extend #8628 rather than add a parallel type. Put the GroupRatios spec in the same boundary: `ForceDensityProblem::free(nodes, members, kinds, FreeSpec)`, where `FreeSpec` is a validated enum (Explicit(q) or GroupRatios) built by `GroupSpec::new(group_ids, seed_ratios, reference_group, members.len())`. That function is the only home of the group checks, and the two search functions drop their guard blocks. Give `MemberKind::admits` and the surface-stress check a finiteness clause: `admits` is `q.is_finite() && match ..`, and σ uses `!(s > 0.0 && s.is_finite())`. Add an `AnisotropicSurfaceStress::new` that validates σ_w, σ_f and warp_dir (finite, non-zero). Nodes are validated finite at construction. D2's `IndexOutOfRange{what,index,len}` plus a `NonFinite{what,index}` variant replaces the lying DimensionMismatch text. Deletable: the five duplicate member checks and four duplicate sign loops in form_find_free.rs, the in-loop Explicit validation in form_find_free_surfaces, the duplicated group guard, and the trampoline's reliance on kernel DimensionMismatch to cover indices. Prevents the whole #7553 and #6563 family, and the NaN/overflow panic class (#6385, #6846, #6940). Relation: extends #8628. Add BT cases for NaN σ, +inf q, a zero warp_dir and a bad group id through the free entry. The PRD's BT2 names NaN q only.
findings.bug_history_link: #7553 (anchor and member guards in three entries, 4 commits), #6563 (surface-corner guard added three times), #6385/#6846/#6940 (NaN guards elsewhere), #8628 (pending)
findings.verdict_notes: The group-spec check (n_groups == 0 || reference_group >= n_groups || group id range) is repeated in form_find_group_ratios_combined and form_find_group_ratios. Member-range checks are spread over validate_members, validate_explicit, the relaxed solver (~line 657) and the loop (~line 320). The sigma checks are written `s <= 0.0` and `sigma_warp <= 0.0`, which accept NaN. DimensionMismatch is returned from many different causes with no payload. The describe text says only that the length does not match. The NaN panic claim is unverified, as the finding itself admits. The count of copies is roughly right.

findings.title: The gauge (scale normalisation) is re-derived per criterion, with absolute floors, not owned by the problem
findings.statement: Answer to the Ask: the gauge is a property of no type. It is re-derived in each criterion, and each was fixed separately after a bug. There are currently six normalisers. (1) form_find.rs: the per-row Σ|D_ij| residual over (1 + coordinate scale), with a per-row zero/NaN guard (#6119, #7046). (2) is_singular_reduced_solve: the same normaliser judged against the anchors' input scale. (3) form_find_free.rs: all_node_equilibrium_residual_relative, which normalises by a global ‖D‖∞ and a global max coordinate. This is exactly the shape #7046 measured as defective (a stiff decoupled subsystem loosens the soft rows' test), and #7801 is pending but unlanded. (4) normalised_eig_gap (divides by max_mag). (5) The un-normalised Σλ² objective in form_find_group_ratios and form_find_group_ratios_combined, deliberately so (task 6413). (6) Absolute thresholds inside those searches: OBJ_TOL = 1e-20, the stall rule `1e-18 * before.max(1.0)`, and four `.max(1e-10)` magnitude floors (warm_group_mag, Phase 1 and Phase 2). The e2e test free_standing_rescaled_seed_ratios_... records the absolute stops as 'search noise' and exercises only λ=7. The 2^±20 gauge suite (tensegrity_free_surface_gauge_covariance) is Explicit-only. The GroupRatios gauge dependence is therefore known but untested at extreme scale: at seed scale ~1e-3 the 1e-10 floor and the 1e-20 stop sit inside the nullity classifier's relative threshold. That is derived by reading, not executed. The same invariant, 'verdicts are invariant under (q,σ) -> λ(q,σ)', has been implemented and fixed in five tasks.
findings.proposal: Introduce a `StiffnessScale` value (crate-private, in a new `fd_criteria.rs` below form_find and form_find_free). It is computed once per assembled D and holds the per-row Σ|D_ij| vector and the coordinate scale. It exposes `relative_equilibrium_residual(&x, rows: RowSet)` and `is_reduced_solve_singular(..)`. The anchored case passes RowSet::Free(&free_indices), the free-standing case RowSet::All. A zero row, NaN row or empty set returns INFINITY in one place. Replace the group-search absolute floors with values relative to the reference group's seed magnitude, and add GroupRatios gauge tests at λ = 2^±20, with both the Explicit and GroupRatios entries in the same parametrised test. Deletable: all_node_equilibrium_residual_relative, the duplicated normaliser inside is_singular_reduced_solve, `1e-10` x4, and the test-local `equilibrium_residual_scaled`. Prevents #6119, #6413, #6983 and #7046 recurring as the 5th and 6th criterion. Relation: #7801 (pending, low) covers only item 3 of the six. #7571 (pending) documents the GroupRatios gauge but does not fix it. Neither the PRD's η nor D3 mentions it. Not covered otherwise.
findings.verdict_notes: all_node_equilibrium_residual_relative normalises by a global d_scale and a global max coordinate, while form_find.rs uses a per-row normaliser. Absolute constants are present: OBJ_TOL = 1e-20, the 1e-18*before.max(1.0) stall rule, and several .max(1e-10) floors. The normaliser count of 'six' is partly a judgement call, but the duplication and the absolute floors are real.

findings.title: form_find_free_surfaces is a 311-line stateful loop with one axis (spec kind) decided inline four times, and review-defence prose in the body
findings.statement: The function spans 311 lines, 129 of them comments (41%), and carries seven mutable loop-lifetime locals: current, converged, last_result, geo_step, prev_resid, stuck_iters and warm_group_mag. It performs six jobs in one body: input guards, bootstrap, per-iteration q source, (2b) trial move, (3) descent, and the stall guard plus finalisation (a reclassify with a second D assembly). The ForceDensitySpec axis is branched inline four times, three of them in this function. These are `match spec` for warm_group_mag at line 282, the per-iteration q source at 317, and `matches!(spec, Explicit)` at 417, which gates (2b). Task #7613 (pending) is open on exactly the asymmetry that gate creates, since GroupRatios gets no (2b). 'D_line + surface_mat' is hand-summed in six loops in this file, and member-force output is built in four copies in the file. Comments include measured results from review rounds: 'left every result unchanged (759 lib + 5 integration tests)' and 'MEASURED on σ=0.05/perturbed×1 ... ~2.66e-5'. Per the Comments stance, that is reviewer-answering prose that belongs in the commit or task record. It is the prose most likely to drift when the loop changes. The next change here (#7613, #7801, anything touching the stall rule) has to reason about state spread across the whole body.
findings.proposal: Split along the real axes, inside form_find_free.rs or a `form_find_free/` module whose children import only downward. Introduce `struct CombinedIterate { nodes, q, d: Mat }` as immutable per-iteration data, built by one `combined_matrix(line_q, surface_mat)` that deletes the six hand-summed loops. Add `trait QSource { fn q_at(&mut self, geom, surface_mat) -> Result<Vec<f64>> }` with `FixedQ` and `SearchedQ` (which owns warm_group_mag). Add `struct StallGuard { prev_resid, stuck }` with `observe(resid, moved) -> bool`, and a `relax(&iterate, ..) -> Vec<[f64;3]>` step. The outer loop shrinks to roughly 40 lines. This also gives #7613 one place to decide whether (2b) applies to both q sources. Move the measured-result prose to the commit message or task #7613's record and leave one-line pointers. Land the member-force dedupe from #8628 D3 first, since it already owns that part. Relation: #8628 D3 covers the anchored loops and the shared member-force and scatter copies only. This split of the free outer loop is not covered by any leaf. #7613 is behaviour work in the same function and should land after the split.
findings.bug_history_link: #6537 (Explicit combined never converges: (2b) added), #6413 (4 commits: gauge-lock inside this loop), #7613 (pending: (2b)/GroupRatios asymmetry)
findings.verdict_notes: The function runs from line 214 to about 525, which is roughly 311 lines. It contains match spec, matches!(Explicit) and the loop-state locals the finding lists. It carries measurement prose and the nullity-4 comment block.

findings.title: build_material_frame accepts a zero warp_dir and emits a NaN frame, misreported as SingularReducedStiffness
findings.statement: The degenerate-frame guard is `if wip_norm_sq < 1e-16 * wd_norm_sq`. For warp_dir = [0,0,0], both sides are 0 and `0 < 0` is false, so the guard does not fire. The next line then computes `e1 = wip / wip_norm` with wip_norm = 0, which gives a NaN frame and a NaN stencil. The field doc says 'any non-zero vector' but nothing enforces non-zero. The only test, aniso_stencil_degenerate_material_frame_guard, uses warp_dir parallel to the normal. A NaN warp_dir passes as well, since NaN < x is false. The NaN D then flows into solve_reduced, where it surfaces as SingularReducedStiffness, a misleading diagnostic for a bad material direction. Found by reading; the zero-vector case is certain, since the comparison is exactly `0 < 0`.
findings.proposal: Change the comparison to `!(wip_norm_sq > 1e-16 * wd_norm_sq)`, which rejects zero and NaN as DegenerateMaterialFrame. Add RED tests for warp_dir = [0,0,0] and a NaN warp_dir through triangle_anisotropic_laplacian and the aniso entry. Also validate warp_dir once at AnisotropicSurfaceStress::new (see the ForceDensityProblem extension finding) so the per-iteration frame check becomes redundant enforcement from one definition. Covered by nothing: #8628's BT list does not include warp_dir.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (same non-finite guard class as #6385/#6846/#6940)
findings.verdict_notes: For warp_dir = 0, wip_norm_sq = 0 and wd_norm_sq = 0, so `0 < 0` is false and the guard does not fire. e1 is then 0/0 = NaN. A NaN warp_dir also passes the guard. No warp_dir check exists in reify-eval. Non-finite output is caught later in is_singular_reduced_solve, which is what produces the SingularReducedStiffness misreport.

findings.title: Dense symmetric-spectrum classification exists three times, each with a panicking .expect, and lives in the wrong module
