findings.statement: Eigendecompose with `self_adjoint_eigen(Side::Lower).expect(..)`, take max|λ|, and threshold at rel_tol*max_mag. That is written in classify_spectrum (private to form_find_free), in prestress_stability::spectral_rank, and in prestress_stability::null_space_basis. Each carries its own `.expect("...real symmetric...must succeed")`. prestress_stability cannot reuse classify_spectrum because it is private. Its docs say 'mirrors' and 'matches the .expect precedent' instead. NULLITY_REL_TOL exists twice with a paragraph explaining that the same value means something different. The D assembly `assemble_force_density_matrix` is pub(crate) inside form_find_free.rs, but prestress_stability, an unrelated analysis, imports it from there, and so does form_find.rs conceptually as scatter_line_members. D assembly therefore has two homes with no module below both of them. Any non-finite D reaches the `.expect`: library code panics where infeasible input is promised a typed error (the module contract in form_find_free.rs).
findings.proposal: Create a `spectrum` module (or `fd_matrix.rs`) below form_find, form_find_free and prestress_stability. It owns `assemble_d(n, members, q)` (merging scatter_line_members and assemble_force_density_matrix) and `SymmetricSpectrum::of(&Mat) -> Result<Self, SpectrumError>` with `nullity(rel_tol)`, `rank(rel_tol)`, `null_basis(rel_tol)` and `max_mag`. Callers map SpectrumError to SingularRecovery or a stability error. It returns Err on non-finite input rather than reaching the faer expect. Three `.expect`s, two NULLITY constants' duplicate sort/threshold code, and the 'mirrors' prose all disappear. Not covered: the PRD streams S14 and S16 do not mention it. Land after #8628, which already touches scatter_line_members.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; adjacent to the NaN-guard history (#6385/#6846/#6940, #7617)
findings.verdict_notes: self_adjoint_eigen(...).expect appears in classify_spectrum (line 1418) and twice in prestress_stability.rs (spectral_rank at line 230, null_space_basis at line 408). NULLITY_REL_TOL is defined in both modules. prestress_stability.rs refers to assemble_force_density_matrix as a layer-2 helper in form_find_free.

findings.title: In-file tests pin private assembly and criterion functions; production is under half of each 2.6-2.9k-line file
findings.statement: Both files exceed the 2,000-line alarm (form_find.rs 2,596, form_find_free.rs 2,866). Measured partition: the `#[cfg(test)]` module is 1,500 lines in form_find.rs (58%) and 1,240 in form_find_free.rs (43%). Production halves are about 1,096 and 1,624 lines. The tests reach private functions through `use super::*`. In form_find.rs these are assemble_d (6 uses), free_equilibrium_residual_relative (7), is_singular_reduced_solve (2) and assemble_d_aniso. In form_find_free.rs they are validate_explicit (7), all_node_equilibrium_residual_relative (5), classify_spectrum, recover_coordinates, combined_geometry_descent_step and combined_eig_gap_objective. The form_find.rs tests also carry a third D assembler (reassemble_d) and a fourth residual (equilibrium_residual_scaled). Per the Tests stance this is an interface smell: the criterion has no public seam of its own, so its behaviour is pinned by private name (it is already covered on the public seam by tests/tensegrity_*_gauge_covariance.rs and the e2e gauge module). Named partition of form_find.rs production: (a) line and isotropic anchored solve and shared validation, L1-600; (b) aniso entry, material frame and principal-stress recovery, L620-1000, which only imports downward from (a) (validate_members, partition_anchors, solve_reduced, MAX_SURFACE_ITERS) and is never imported back, so no h13 symptom; (c) stencils, L1044-1090, which are imported by form_find_free (downward, no cycle). For form_find_free.rs the candidates are the types and entry points, the fixed-point loop, the GroupRatios search, and spectrum/recovery. The last imports nothing from the others, but prestress_stability reaches into its private helpers. A split is legitimate only after the two earlier findings land; moving tests alone into a tests.rs that imports `super::*` is stitching.
findings.proposal: Do not split for size. After the ForceDensityProblem, criterion and spectrum extractions (the findings above and #8628) land, the production files shrink and the aniso section becomes `form_find/aniso.rs` with a downward-only import. Rewrite the in-file private-name tests as behaviour tests at the new modules' pub(crate) seams (StiffnessScale, SymmetricSpectrum, ForceDensityProblem) or delete them where the integration gauge suites already cover the property. Delete reassemble_d and equilibrium_residual_scaled (test-local copies of production algorithms). Covered partly by #8628's BT additions. The test-seam rewrite is not covered.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative
findings.verdict_notes: form_find.rs is 2596 lines and its test module starts at line 1096, so the tests are about 1500 lines. form_find_free.rs is 2866 lines and its test module starts at line 1624, about 1242 lines. Both tests modules use private items through super::*. The finding is a modest design smell, as its own low severity says.

findings.title: Tensegrity topology is decoded twice (reify-stdlib accessors and reify-eval crack), with different failure semantics
findings.statement: Both the viewport accessors (tensegrity_wires, tensegrity_surfaces) and the solver trampoline decode the Tensegrity structure's nodes, struts, cables and surfaces from Value. The stdlib copy has its own list-of-Int-tuple extractor, its own `from < 0 || from as usize >= n_nodes` range check, and the strings "strut"/"cable" as the member kind. The eval copy has check_index, crack_index_pairs and crack_index_triples, and MemberKind is reconstituted purely from list position (struts first, then cables). The same schema is decoded with two failure policies, silent Undef versus a located E_FormFindInfeasible error, and two range-check implementations. A change to the Tensegrity structure def has to be mirrored in both. There is no typed topology value that both sides parse into. The kernel's `kinds`/`members` pair reconstructs what that value would hold.
findings.proposal: Define a `TensegrityTopology { nodes, members: Vec<(usize,usize,MemberKind)>, surfaces }` with one `TensegrityTopology::from_value(&Value) -> Result<_, TopologyError>`. Put it in a crate both reify-stdlib and reify-eval can depend on (the S16 trampoline decoders' home, or reify-ir). The stdlib accessors map the Err to Undef and the trampoline maps it to its located message. Deletable: the stdlib extract_* helpers and range checks, and the sign-by-position convention. The kernel's ForceDensityProblem then accepts `&TensegrityTopology` fields. Not covered: S15/S16 (trampoline-decode-and-result-build.md) mention only the stdlib StructureTypeId(0) minting and tensegrity_crack::scalar_f64. Coordinate with that PRD's owners before filing.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative
findings.verdict_notes: tensegrity.rs has its own extract_index_tuples (returns Option, so failure is silent) and extract_nodes, and hardcodes the strings "strut" and "cable" in build_wire calls. tensegrity_crack.rs has separate check_index, crack_nodes, crack_index_pairs and crack_index_triples that return Err(String). The two decoders are independent.

findings.title: A variable's feasible domain has no single home: a dead input channel, a re-derived private interval, and four pending tasks each adding another bound miner
findings.bug_history_link: fix(7883) 4a38f38b7f 'a strict derived bound wins an exact tie'; fix(7883) 38b7d5fae6 'γ clamp box stops one representable value inside a strict bound'; fix(6465) a31f9fa632 'name the solve regime; give γ a strict-inclusive clamp box'; fix(6465) 5acff8378b 'carry the determinedness evidence out instead of a bool'; #5618 (fixed 0.01 seed ignored derived bounds); #5711 (anchor box); #6755 / #5470 (Int autos have no domain); #6692 (10 m default-corner resolution)
findings.verdict_notes: AutoParam.bounds is None at every production builder (engine_eval.rs 1953, engine_edit.rs 1708 and 4034). It is still read by solver.rs extract_initial_point (line 531) and cpsat.rs domain_spec, whose Int arm is `if let Some(bounds) ... else Err`. derive_param_intervals is called from several consumers (lines 510, 1937, 2984, 4138). The multi-walk and strictness-reread claims are consistent with the code. I did not verify the pending-task claims.

findings.title: The DimensionalSolver accepts a point by a hand-rolled residual that is inclusive at strict bounds, while the checker and CP-SAT use exact Kleene evaluation
findings.statement:
"Is this constraint satisfied at this point?" has three definitions.

(1) The checker. `reify check` uses reify-expr `eval_cmp`, `BinOp::Gt => a > b`: exact and Kleene.

(2) CP-SAT. It accepts a point with `eval_expr(expr) == Value::Bool(true)` (cpsat.rs around line 718), which is the checker's semantics.

(3) DimensionalSolver. It accepts when `max_constraint_residual(..) <= FEASIBILITY_THRESHOLD` (1e-12 absolute, in raw SI units). The residual comes from its own `comparison_residual`:
- For `BinOp::Gt` the else-branch returns `r - l`, which is 0.0 when `l == r`. A point exactly ON a strict bound therefore scores as satisfied, and so does any point in `[r - 1e-12, r]`. The checker rejects both.
- `Eq` uses a 1e-15 absolute tolerance.
- The fold is `fold(0.0, f64::max)`, which drops NaN rows (#9012).
- Non-comparison leaves are scored 0/1/10 by a second copy of the same match.
- A parallel `comparison_violation` / `constraint_violation` pair repeats the operator match for the cost function.

Because the acceptance gate cannot tell inclusive from strict, strictness is enforced upstream by choosing a clamp box instead:
- `StrictBound::Dropped` exists so the general clamp never returns a value the strict comparison rejects (section comment: 'clamping `x > 5mm` to exactly 5mm violates the strict comparison').
- `StrictBound::SteppedInside` (#7883) exists so γ's λ=1 answer satisfies `reify check`.

In other words, two box policies compensate for one acceptance predicate. Neither covers the regimes whose clamp box is `effective_bounds`: RobustnessFloor without a floor, and FeasibilityWitness. There, a Nelder-Mead result within 1e-12 below a strict bound is returned as `Solved` and the checker then reports it violated.

#6653 (in progress) single-sources only the EQUALITY epsilon between the verdict fold and solver acceptance. Its description says 'Inequality comparisons (>=, <=) keep their existing semantics', and #9012 records that its `RowResidual::inequality` spells out the legacy NaN-accepting rule.
findings.proposal:
Make acceptance call the checker's predicate.

**The function.** Add `fn leaf_verdicts(constraints, values, ctx) -> Vec<LeafVerdict>` in the residual layer that solver-crates-layering D16 names (`solver/residual`).
- It evaluates each leaf conjunct with reify-expr's comparison semantics, plus #6653's single-sourced equality tolerance once that lands.
- `LeafVerdict` is `Satisfied`, `Violated { magnitude }` or `Undecidable` (Undef or NaN).
- Acceptance is `all Satisfied`; NaN is `Undecidable` and therefore rejected.
- The magnitude is retained only for the `Infeasible` diagnostic's 'max absolute residual' and for the cost function.

**What dies:**
- `comparison_residual`'s private operator semantics. They collapse into one operator table shared with `comparison_violation`, whose squared penalty stays a cost-shaping choice and not a satisfaction claim.
- The `is_nan()` acceptance arm (#9012).

**What `StrictBound::Dropped` and `SteppedInside` become.** They are still useful search hints, but are no longer the only correctness guard. A boundary landing is caught at acceptance in every regime, rather than only in the two regimes whose clamp box was patched.

**Bug classes prevented:** #7883 (a false Satisfied, then Violated, at a strict bound), #9012 (NaN counted as satisfied), and the #6653 class for inequalities.

**Coverage: extends.** This extends #6653, whose contract (c) — one policy shared by the verdict fold and solver acceptance — explicitly excludes inequalities, and it extends #9012. Neither replaces the evaluator.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(7883) 38b7d5fae6 (γ clamp box steps inside a strict bound because acceptance would not reject the boundary); fix(7883) 4a38f38b7f; #9012 (NaN residuals count as satisfied; found by #6653); #6653 (exact-f64 checker vs 1e-12 solver acceptance, false VIOLATED)
findings.verdict_notes: The BinOp::Gt arm returns 0.0 if l>r, otherwise r-l, so l==r gives residual 0 and is accepted as satisfied. The acceptance threshold is a separate absolute epsilon. The checker uses exact comparison. StrictBound compensation exists. I did not check the Eq tolerance or the NaN fold in detail.

findings.title: The solve outcome is interpreted separately at six engine call sites, and the ranked→plain downgrade is copied three times; the copies have already drifted
findings.proposal:
Introduce one interpreter: `struct SolveOutcomeSink<'a> { values, snapshot_values, cache, journal, solve_failed_autos: Option<&mut ..>, diagnostics }`, with `fn apply(self, problem: &ResolutionProblem, outcome: SolveOutcome)`. It owns, in one place:
- the write-back of solved values;
- the pinned-connector write;
- undef-cause recording;
- the non-unique and no-progress diagnostics.

The six arms each shrink to a single call. The cold-only and warm-only legs (snapshot/version allocation, `param_overrides`) become explicit parameters rather than silent omissions.

Add `RankedSolveResult::into_winner(self) -> (SolveResult, Option<OptimalityStatus>, Option<Vec<RankedCandidate>>)` in reify-ir beside `into_ranked_pass_through`, enforcing I2 once. The three hand-copied downgrades are deleted.

This also gives #6699's entry-point parity (cold uses ranked, warm uses plain) one place to change.

**Bug classes prevented:** warm-path missing provenance; the five-copy warning fan-out that #6707 must otherwise code five times; future honesty codes landing on only the cold path.

**Coverage: extends.**
- #6690 (P1-β) unifies the problem BUILDER, not the outcome consumer.
- #6699 (P1-κ) unifies the entry point.
- #6707/#6901 (P3 β) code the five warning copies in place rather than collapsing them.
- #6711 (P3 ζ) touches 'both `swap_remove(0)` seams', but only to keep alternatives.
No leaf owns the interpreter.
findings.bug_history_link: #5118 / #6226 (warm cluster-solve wiring at three of four sites, the fourth deferred); #6707 (five code-less byte-identical warning sites); #6699 (cold solve_ranked vs warm solve); #4710 (pinned-connector write added per arm)
findings.verdict_notes: Matches on SolveResult exist at engine_eval.rs 6354, 7757, 9171 and engine_edit.rs 1762 and 4088. record_failed_autos is called only in the cold eval arms (6536, 6561) and in dispatch_merged_cluster_solve (7997, 8007), so the warm and edit arms lack it. The ranked-to-plain downgrade appears at engine_eval.rs 6327 and 7726, and in registry.rs around line 697 (`unique: candidates[0].unique`). Several drift details are inferred rather than checked line by line.

findings.title: The relate solve silently discards `at auto(seed = …)` and component-fix `at auto(x = …)` parameters, while its own error message tells the user to use them
findings.statement:
The full chain parses, compiles and carries these parameters, and then drops them:
- The grammar and lowering accept `sub b : B at auto(seed = self.frame)` and `at auto(x = 5mm, orientation = orient_identity())` (tree-sitter-reify fixture gr-03-auto-param.ri; reify-syntax `relate_at_auto_lowering_tests.rs`).
- reify-compiler's `AutoPoseSpec.params` carries them. Its doc states 'ζ's relate-solve consumes these (seed/root selection, partial-fix)'.
- `collect_relate_scope` copies them into `AutoUnknown.seed_params`.
- `solve_relate_scope` never reads `seed_params`. `git grep seed_params` finds only the field, its one writer and a comment. It hard-codes `let seed = Pose::identity();`, with a comment saying evaluating seeds 'is a refinement not exercised by ζ's named e2e set'.

As a result, a component-fix `auto(x = 5mm)`, which is the author pinning one DOF, is ignored without a diagnostic and the solver may move x. That breaches INV-SF-3, honest non-consumption.

The same function's `NoProgress` arm emits 'try an `auto(seed = …)` nearer the intended placement'. That advice cannot have any effect, so the message lies (heuristic 1).

#6676 covers the sibling defect (only `auto_unknowns.first()` is solved) but not the parameters.
findings.proposal:
Immediate fix, low effort:
- In `solve_relate_scope`, when `auto.seed_params` is non-empty, emit a coded Warning naming the sub and each unconsumed parameter. Precedent: the `unconsumable_relation_diagnostic` that task 7050 added for un-consumable members.
- Drop the `auto(seed = …)` advice from the NoProgress message.
- Correct `AutoPoseSpec`'s doc to say the parameters are carried but not yet consumed.
- Add a test that drives `at auto(x = 5mm)` through `solve_scopes` and asserts the warning.

Full fix, when the multi-body pose vector (#6676) reshapes `FrameUnknown`: evaluate `seed` into the seed `Pose`, and lower each component-fix parameter into a pinned DOF of the unknown, so the Jacobian excludes it.

The invariant to hold: every `AutoPoseSpec.params` entry is either consumed or diagnosed, checked where the scope is collected.

**Coverage: not covered.** #6676 owns multi-body only. No task found for seeds or component-fix parameters.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(7050) ef6d415d10 'diagnose an un-consumable relate member instead of dropping it' (the same silent-drop class on a sibling input); #6676 (second at-auto sub silently unsolved); speculative for the seed/component-fix drop itself (no task found)
findings.verdict_notes: seed_params is written at relate_solve.rs line 141 and never read outside a test. The seed is hard-coded as `Pose::identity()`, and a comment says evaluating seed params is a refinement. The NoProgress message at line 882 advises `auto(seed = …)`, which has no effect. I did not independently check whether component-fix params are consumed elsewhere, but seed_params is the only carrier.

findings.title: The solve-failure cause crosses the solver→engine boundary as free text and is re-wrapped as an `UndefCause` string
findings.statement:
The solver computes typed causes and then flattens them to strings:
- `ObjectiveAbstention` (Undefined, NonFiniteTerm, NonFiniteFold) becomes `format!("{} at fallback point", cause.reason())` / `"... at solution point"`.
- Executor failure becomes `format!("solver error: {}", e)`.
- `Determinedness::NotDetermined` and `DefaultBoundsDetermined` become `SolveResult::Infeasible` with a prose message.

All of these reach reify-eval as `SolveResult::NoProgress { reason: String }` or `Infeasible { diagnostics }`. The engine then stores the cause in a `HashMap<ValueCellId, String>` via `record_failed_autos`:
- the literal `"infeasible"` for every Infeasible, the non-uniqueness demotion included;
- `format!("no progress: {reason}")` for NoProgress.

`undef_tracer.rs` and reify-cli `format_undef_cause` render it as `solve failed: {detail}`. That is why a two-root strict model reports 'solve failed: infeasible' (P3 §1 item 2). No consumer can branch on the cause without parsing the prose, and a new cause, such as #5975's 'no optimum exists' or #6692's one-sided refusal, has no typed slot.
findings.bug_history_link: #6707 (two-root strict model labelled 'solve failed: infeasible'); #5975 / #5918 ('no optimum exists' folded into abstention because there is no slot); fix(6377) ff59000003 (non-finite fold made a typed ObjectiveAbstention, then flattened to text at the boundary)
findings.verdict_notes: record_failed_autos takes `detail: &str` and stores it into HashMap<ValueCellId, String>. Callers pass the literal "infeasible" or `format!("no progress: {reason}")`. The solver builds `format!("{} at fallback point")`, `"... at solution point"` and `"solver error: {}"` as NoProgress reason strings (solver.rs lines 3129, 3226, 3280).

findings.title: FFI failures are flattened to strings at the C++ boundary and re-wrapped by 132 hand-written map_err sites, so no typed failure class reaches the user diagnostic
findings.statement: C++ distinguishes four failure classes: Standard_Failure (OCCT algorithm failure), ContractViolation (Reify-authored, user-actionable), std::exception (internal bug) and unknown. wrap_occt_call rethrows all four as std::runtime_error(String) with the FFI function name as prefix, e.g. 'OCCT <ffi_fn>: ...' or '<ffi_fn>: ...'. The class is gone at the boundary. Rust then re-wraps each message at 132 hand-written `.map_err(|e| ..(e.to_string()))` sites in production lib.rs (lines 1-4735), plus 46 `OperationFailed(format!(..))` sites. GeometryError has exactly one variant for every non-handle kernel failure (OperationFailed(String)), so a corrupt handle (get_shape's IsNull refusal), a user-argument contract violation, an OCCT algorithm failure and an internal fault are indistinguishable downstream. The user-facing diagnostic is the FFI message string, with the FFI function name as its prefix (the #5895/#5898 leak class). The codebase already works around the missing type with stringly markers: floor_constants.rs::RUST_GUARD_MARKER '[rust-guard]' exists so tests can tell Rust-origin from C++-origin messages. Tests pin classes by English substring: `msg.contains("fillet") && msg.contains("radius")`, `low.contains("null")`, `lower.contains("zero")` in the lib.rs test module (about lines 6888-7884). The 'Missing/null handle' condition itself has two different OperationFailed texts in get_shape ('is null' vs 'wraps null/empty topology (IsNull)'), so #7379's 'only error' is a prose string, not a variant. Violates heuristic 12 (parse at the boundary into typed values) and 10 (the same fault is spelled at 132+ sites, uniformly only by convention).
findings.proposal: Introduce one typed fault at the bridge, `FfiFault { kind: Contract | Native | Internal, op: &'static str, detail: String }`. wrap_occt_call emits the kind as a fixed machine-parsed envelope (one encoder in C++, ONE decoder in Rust: `impl From<cxx::Exception> for FfiFault`). Add typed variants to reify-ir GeometryError (CorruptHandle(GeometryHandleId) for the IsNull and null-UniquePtr cases, ContractViolation{detail} for user-actionable input faults, KernelFailure{op,detail} for native faults) with From<FfiFault>. The 132 `map_err(|e| ..to_string())` sites become `?`. The diagnostic layer then renders user text from the variant and keeps the op name only in a debug field. Deletable: RUST_GUARD_MARKER, the `contains("null")`/`contains("zero")` substring assertions (replaced by matches! on variants), and the 'OCCT <ffi_fn>:' prefix in user text. Prevents the #5895/#5898 symbol-leak class and the #5211/#7379 message-erasure class. Not covered: S11 (occt-crate-internals.md) moves #7379's mapping into ShapeStore but keeps String payloads, and S10 α2 (#8931) only relocates GeometryError into geometry/error.rs without adding variants. Best sequenced after #8931 so the variants land in error.rs, and before ε (#8682) so ShapeStore::get returns the typed CorruptHandle.
findings.bug_history_link: #5211 (null/empty topology guards), #7379 (3 commits: query/export/tessellate/split propagate get_shape error), pending #5895/#5898 (FFI symbol names leak into user diagnostics)
findings.verdict_notes: wrap_occt_call rethrows all four classes as std::runtime_error with name prefix. About 131 map_err(|e| ..to_string) in lib.rs lines 1-4735 (claim 132). RUST_GUARD_MARKER exists in floor_constants.rs as described.

findings.title: BRepKind is decoded from a C++ type-name string with a silent `_ => Solid` fallback
findings.statement: brep_kind_of_shape calls ffi `shape_type_name` (which returns `rust::String(topabs_name(ShapeType()))`) and matches on the English names 'Solid'/'CompSolid'/'Compound'/'Shell'/..., ending in `_ => BRepKind::Solid`. The enum-to-name table lives in C++ (topabs_name, whose own default arm returns 'Shape') and the name-to-enum table lives in Rust, kept in sync only by spelling. An unrecognised name (including the abstract TopAbs_SHAPE the C++ default arm emits) is silently stamped Solid, which is exactly the wrong-repr failure class S11 documents (a translated profile or wire stamped Solid; fillet over a mis-stamped compound accepted). The classifier is the foundation of the planned ReprPolicy: S11 ζ (#8669) adds 'Classify' to about 14 more arms, and every one depends on this string decode and its silent default. Heuristic 12 (structured data instead of meaningful strings) and heuristic 10 (a silent default instead of an informative refusal).
findings.proposal: Replace `shape_type_name -> String` with a cxx shared enum `FfiShapeKind { Compound, CompSolid, Solid, Shell, Face, Wire, Edge, Vertex }` returned by a `shape_kind(&OcctShape)` FFI fn. The C++ switch is exhaustive and throws a ContractViolation on TopAbs_SHAPE. A Rust `From<FfiShapeKind> for BRepKind` is an exhaustive match with no wildcard arm. Keep topabs_name only for C++ error text. Deletable: the string match, the `_ => Solid` arm, and the doc text describing it. Enforced at the type level, so a new TopAbs kind is a compile error on both sides. It would have prevented the repr-misstamp class (S11 §1 probes). Extends ζ #8669 as a small prerequisite; ζ's 'classify' arms then rest on a total classifier. Not covered by any leaf today (ζ names brep_kind_of_shape as the tool but does not change it).
findings.bug_history_link: #5213 amendment (classification added to fuse), #6652 (repr stamping), S11 f65 (centroid(translate(rectangle)) prints origin); mechanism itself speculative
findings.verdict_notes: Matches on the topabs_name strings with `_ => BRepKind::Solid`; topabs_name default returns "Shape". Reach of the fallback is only the abstract TopAbs_SHAPE, so practical exposure is narrow, but the stringly decode and silent default are as stated.

findings.title: Every stored shape must have a repr, but the two parallel maps keep that by comment, and consumers handle 'repr absent' three different ways
findings.statement: `shapes: HashMap<u64, UniquePtr<OcctShape>>` and `reprs: HashMap<u64, BRepKind>` are inserted together in store_with_repr and cleared together in reset, but are two containers, so 'shape present implies repr present' is maintained by convention. Three consumers reach the 'unreachable' repr-less case differently. fuse_all and apply_transform_to_handle use `repr_of(h).unwrap_or(BRepKind::Solid)`, which silently re-stamps Solid. run_local_feature_with_history matches `None => {}` with a 10-line comment arguing the case is unreachable, then falls through to get_shape. with_warm_state carries a separate sync check ('warm.reprs and warm.shapes are out of sync'), plus a test-only insert_null_shape that breaks the lock-step (lib.rs:4747). The silent-Solid arms are the same wrong-default that S11 f65 measures as user-visible. Heuristic 10 (redundant consumers each re-decide the invariant) and 5/8 (two lifetimes for one fact).
findings.proposal: The ShapeStore from ε (#8682) should store one `Entry { shape: UniquePtr<OcctShape>, repr: BRepKind }` keyed by id, and expose `get(id) -> Result<(&OcctShape, BRepKind), CorruptHandle|InvalidReference>`. Callers needing both (apply_transform_to_handle, fuse_all, run_local_feature_with_history) take the repr from the same lookup, so 'repr absent' cannot be expressed. Deletable: `repr_of`'s Option, both `unwrap_or(Solid)` fallbacks, the `None => {}` arm and its comment, the warm-state reprs/shapes desync check, and the exhaustive-destructure obligation to keep two maps in lock-step. Extends ε #8682: the PRD's D6 interface lists `insert, get, repr_of` as separate operations over fields `shapes` and `reprs`, which would preserve the two-lookup shape inside the new module.
findings.bug_history_link: S11 f65 repr misstamping; esc-2655-26 / task 2821 amendment (comment justifying the unreachable arm); speculative for a desync bug
findings.verdict_notes: Two maps inserted together. repr_of(..).unwrap_or(Solid) at lines 1203 and 1318. run_local_feature_with_history has `None => {}` with a justifying comment. with_warm_state only debug_asserts sync and falls back to Solid. insert_null_shape is test-only. All as described.

findings.title: The C++ null-topology guard is 9 hand-copied checks with 2 exception types, and about 35 sibling shape-taking entry points have none
findings.statement: Answering the brief's question: the Rust side resolves every handle through ONE get_shape and propagates its error unchanged. The C++ IsNull guard, however, is copies, not a helper. 14 lines say 'null/empty topology'; compute_volume_arm throws ContractViolation('shape has null/empty topology') (no op prefix), while query_area, query_edge_length, query_centroid, query_face_centroid, query_bbox and query_inertia_tensor each inline `if (shape.shape.IsNull()) throw std::runtime_error("<fn>: shape has null/empty topology")` under an identical 'DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH ... see compute_volume_arm' comment. Different exception types produce different prefixes after wrap_occt_call. A scan of the 104 top-level functions that take an OcctShape shows that, of the query and conformance family, query_face_normal, surface_angle, shape_local_tolerance, surface_normal_at, query_distance, min_clearance, vertex_point, query_moment_of_inertia, is_watertight, is_manifold, is_orientable, is_closed, is_connected, is_bounded, get_edges/get_faces/get_vertices and measure_mesh_deviation deref `shape.shape` with no check. Two further notions of 'empty' also exist: shape_has_no_topology (empty compound) and the Rust `shape_is_null`. #5211 patched four entry points and the next query added will not know to add a fifth. The guard is correct today only because Rust get_shape runs first; the C++ copies are redundant enforcement without a single definition (heuristic 10 uniformly; heuristic 11).
findings.proposal: Add one C++ accessor in the anonymous namespace beside reject_empty_input_shape: `const TopoDS_Shape& live_topology(const OcctShape&)` that throws a ContractViolation and is the ONLY way query code reads `shape.shape`. Use it from compute_volume_arm and the 6 inlined copies, and from every unguarded query entry point (mechanical: replace `shape.shape` by `live_topology(shape)`). The Rust side already has the primary guard; also expose `shape_is_null` through the ShapeStore::get chokepoint (ε), so the C++ helper is the single redundant layer. Deletable: the 7 inline guards and their 7 identical 'DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH' comments (comments stance). Add one behavioural test that injects a null shape via make_null_shape_for_test into every query FFI fn (table-driven). Prevents the #5211 SIGSEGV class. Not covered: S11 ε moves the Rust chokepoint; the C++ side is untouched by any leaf.
findings.bug_history_link: #5211 (defence-in-depth IsNull guards at four C++ query entry points)
findings.verdict_notes: The duplicated inline guards are real: compute_volume_arm throws ContractViolation, and six sibling query functions throw runtime_error with copied comments. The claim that about 35 siblings deref unguarded is overstated. They run inside wrap_occt_call, which converts OCCT null-object exceptions into errors, and Rust get_shape runs first. query_distance and is_watertight have no explicit IsNull check, but that is not an unguarded crash path.

findings.title: Death of the OCCT actor thread is an unmodelled, permanent state: no panic capture, no cause, 35 copies of a literal message
findings.statement: OcctKernelHandle is Running or (implicitly) Dead. Dead is reached when the kernel thread unwinds: spawn()'s loop has no catch_unwind (`grep catch_unwind` over the crate is empty), so any panic inside kernel.execute/query, including a Rust `debug_assert`, `unwrap` or FFI decode panic, ends the worker. From then on every call returns the literal string 'kernel thread died', hard-coded as `|| X::Y("kernel thread died".into())` at 35 sites in handle.rs (one per method, though send_recv already takes the mapper). The panic payload is lost: Drop does `let _ = thread.join()`, and in an async context never joins. The thread's OcctKernel (all shapes, repr map and caches) is gone with no way to rebuild, so every later realization in the GUI session fails identically, and the cause the user sees is the same string whether it was a panic, a C++ std::terminate-adjacent fault or a shutdown. This is the 'no crash-reporting boundary' of live #7385 seen from the structure side: there is no state variable for it. Heuristic 10 (missing state, missing informative violation message) and 12 (literal message routed as meaning).
findings.proposal: Give the handle an explicit liveness cell: `Arc<Mutex<ActorState>>` with `Running | Panicked{payload: String} | Shutdown`. spawn() wraps each request body in `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))`, records the payload in the cell, then replies with `GeometryError::KernelFailure{op:"actor", detail: payload}` (a typed variant from the finding above) instead of dropping the reply sender. On `ChannelDied` the shared `call<R>` primitive reads the cell and reports 'OCCT kernel panicked in <op>: <payload>' or 'kernel shut down'. Deletable: the 35 literal closures (one `chan_died` function), the discarded join. Optionally the handle could respawn a fresh OcctKernel, since the engine already supports reset and rebuild. Extends θ #8672, whose D7 keeps 'GeometryError::OperationFailed("kernel thread died") and siblings, as today', so it freezes the lossy mapping into the new primitive. Relation to live #7385 (crash-reporting boundary): this would be its in-crate half. This finding supplies the structure; coordinate rather than duplicate.
findings.bug_history_link: #7385 (no crash-reporting boundary for OCCT actor thread), #7383 (SIGSEGV on printer.ri); speculative for the panic path itself
findings.verdict_notes: 'kernel thread died' appears 35 times in handle.rs. grep catch_unwind over src returns nothing.

findings.title: occt_wrapper.cpp is a 9,477-line translation unit that no leaf measures or partitions; it also ships test-only constructors and test observability in the production library
findings.statement: The review-all h14 table measured lib.rs, handle.rs and ffi.rs but not the C++ TU (the PRD only names it as 'accessor set' edited by δ). It is over the 2,000-line alarm at 9,477 lines plus a 1,807-line header, and its purpose needs 'and' (primitives, booleans, four history families, transforms, wire/curve builders, queries, test fixtures, STEP export, STEP import, tessellation, serialisation). Measured partition and h13 symptom, by scripted reference scan of top-level definitions: (1) STEP export+import, lines 7088-9162 (about 2,075 lines, with g_step_export_mutex, InterfaceStaticOverride and the XDE reader). Symptom: none upward. The range calls exactly two outside definitions, wrap_occt_call (line 260) and reject_empty_input_shape (line 500), and no definition in the range is referenced from outside it. (2) Test fixtures, lines 6075-6771 (about 700 lines, 12 `*_for_test` constructors) compiled into the production library and declared ungated in ffi.rs. Symptom: none, no production caller. (3) boolean/history (747-2860), (4) wire and curve builders (3764-4670), (5) queries (4710-6075), (6) tessellation (9189-9477). All of them import only the shared prelude at lines 225-512 (wrap_occt_call, ContractViolation, topabs_name, reject_empty_input_shape, validation constants). The prelude would become `occt_common.h`, a downward import, so no cycle and no stitching. Other smells in the TU: three `static thread_local` test-observability counters (t_boolean_pass_count, t_parallel_bop_build_count, t_boolean_run_parallel) live in the production file with 20+ lines of rationale each; g_step_export_mutex is named 'export' but its comment says it serialises STEP import as well (heuristic 1). The first of the 14 mined 'native failure mode' fixes in this window (#7437, #7439) all landed by editing this single TU, so a reader must load all 9.5k lines to find the one Build() site.
findings.proposal: Split along the measured partitions into `step_io.cpp` (export+import, owning the mutex, renamed g_xstep_mutex), `occt_fixtures.cpp` (compiled only with the `test-fixtures` feature; gate the 12 ffi declarations with cfg), `occt_history.cpp`, `occt_query.cpp`, `occt_tessellate.cpp`, over a private `occt_common.h`/`.cpp` that defines wrap_occt_call, ContractViolation, topabs_name, live_topology (from the IsNull finding) and the validation constants. Move the thread_local boolean counters behind a small `boolean_policy.cpp` that also hosts build_bop_algorithm. Layering is strictly downward (leaf .cpp -> occt_common.h). No Rust symbol changes; build.rs lists the sources. Per heuristic 14 this is only legitimate because each resulting file passes h13 per the measurement above. Do the step_io and fixtures extractions first (zero cross references). Not covered: S11 γ/δ/ι partition only the Rust files and edit the C++ accessor set in place.
findings.bug_history_link: #7437/#7439/#5213 (boolean pass counting and BOP mode edits concentrated in this one TU), #6344 (STEP unit-guard, about 20 amend commits in the STEP region)
findings.verdict_notes: The file is 9477 lines. g_step_export_mutex is at line 7096. 27 for_test references. ffi.rs exposes them ungated, with a comment saying they are deliberately not cfg(test).

findings.title: Layered Rust/C++ degeneracy thresholds are single-sourced and compile-time ordered for one guard, but free-floating constants with different values for the rest
findings.statement: The line-wire floor shows the intended pattern: `floor_constants.rs` is the canonical source of both RUST_ and CPP_ values, build.rs writes the C++ one into a generated header, and lib.rs asserts the layering with `const _: () = assert!(RUST < CPP)`. The other layered guards follow no such mechanism. Rust AXIS_MAG_SQ_MIN = 1e-12 (squared, used at about 8 production sites) and ANGLE_ABS_MIN = 1e-30 sit in lib.rs; CPP_AXIS_MAG_SQ_MIN = 1e-30, CPP_ANGLE_ABS_MIN = 1e-30 and CPP_DIR_MAG_MIN = 1e-10 sit in the C++; the eval layer has its own DEGENERATE_ANGLE_RAD and GEOMETRY_EPSILON = 1e-12 (geometry_ops.rs). The relationship is described in prose ('Matches the C++ ANGLE_ABS_MIN threshold (1e-30)', 'Rust validates first with stricter thresholds') and checked by nothing, and the 'stricter' relation is not even uniform: ANGLE_ABS_MIN is equal in both layers and CPP_DIR_MAG_MIN (1e-10, linear) is looser than Rust's 1e-12 squared (1e-6 linear), not stricter. Changing one value silently flips which layer produces the error message; the Rust and C++ messages differ, which the tests then pin by substring. S11 γ1 (#8652) moves the Rust constants into op_args.rs but does not touch the cross-language relation. Heuristic 10 (invariant defined in one place, enforced uniformly) and 11.
findings.proposal: Extend the existing floor_constants.rs mechanism: add AXIS_MAG_SQ_MIN, DIR_MAG_MIN and ANGLE_ABS_MIN pairs (RUST_* and CPP_*) to it, generate all CPP_* into the same build.rs header, delete the C++ literal constants in occt_wrapper.cpp, and put one `const _: () = assert!(..)` per pair in op_args.rs (after γ1). Write the true relation (strictly looser, or equal where intended) once in the module doc. Deletable: the three C++ constexpr literals and the 'DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH' prose blocks at occt_wrapper.cpp lines 526-531 and 4584-4585. Extends γ1 #8652 (op_args.rs home for the Rust half). The eval-side constants are the S10 θ territory and are out of scope here.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; same shape as the layered line-wire floor that needed floor_constants.rs after the guard layers diverged
findings.verdict_notes: Rust AXIS_MAG_SQ_MIN 1e-12 against C++ 1e-30, and ANGLE_ABS_MIN equal at 1e-30 in both layers, are real and relied on only by prose. floor_constants plus a compile-time assert exists only for the line wire. But CPP_DIR_MAG_MIN guards a surface-normal cross product, a different quantity from the axis magnitude, so calling it 'looser than Rust' is an apples-to-oranges comparison.

findings.title: Per-crate scope-class declarations live in five homes and four forms, with only detective drift tests
findings.statement: One fact family, "crate X belongs to scope class C", is declared in different forms. The corpus-reader set is a Python frozenset (RI_CORPUS_CRATES, 6 crates). The OCCT set is a txt file that is also derivable from cargo metadata (occt_touching_set), and it is copied a third time into dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml -p/--exclude flags. The release-sensitive set is a second txt file. The harness-consolidatable set is a 5-crate literal in select_harness_kloc_guard, a copy in test_harness_kloc_cap.sh CONSOLIDATABLE_CRATES, and a third in harness-layout-lib.sh. The engine-hash closure is a fifth manifest in reify-eval. Each has its own drift test (RI-CORPUS-DRIFT is derived-subset-of-declared by regex over crates' .rs sources), and those tests run only when a verify-pipeline artifact changes, per verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt rows 275-276. A task that adds an examples/ read in a crate therefore first reds at the merge-tier pool. S18 beta (#9097) derives only the kloc set (via harness_layout_consolidatable_crates). It treats occt/release as BashCalls and does not mention RI_CORPUS_CRATES. S22 theta moved RI_CORPUS_CRATES into Python and left it hand-declared. The regex derivation is also brittle: fix(6932) had to move a fixture out of .rs because the grep read it as a corpus reader.
findings.proposal: Make the crate the single declaration site. Add a [package.metadata.reify-scope] table per Cargo.toml with boolean keys corpus_reader, release_sensitive and harness_consolidatable. Add one function in reify_path_attribution.py, crate_scope_classes(cargo_metadata) -> Mapping[crate, frozenset[ScopeClass]], that reads them from the same cargo metadata call affected_crates already makes. attribute()/RI_CORPUS_CRATES, release_declared_set and the kloc literal then read from it. Delete RI_CORPUS_CRATES, release-sensitive-crates.txt and the 3 kloc copies. Derive the OCCT set from the closure instead of the txt plus yaml copy, or generate the yaml flags from it. Enforce at use (a crate's Cargo.toml edit is already a manifest touch that selects the DAG-gate crate) and with one structural test that every declared key names a workspace member. Prevents the fix(6509), fix(5721), fix(5751) and fix(6001) classes, where the declaration was added only after a gate went red. Not covered: extends #9097 (kloc half only) and #8662's module; no leaf owns the corpus-reader or release/occt declarations.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(6509) declare reify-test-support an examples/ corpus reader; fix(5721) declare reify-constraints release-sensitive; fix(5751) declare the two kernel crates release-sensitive; fix(6001) add reify-builtins to the engine-hash closure manifest; fix(6932) move fixture out of .rs so it is not read as a corpus reader; fix(7427) map examples/**/*.ri to corpus reader crates
findings.verdict_notes: Multiple homes for scope-class sets are real (RI_CORPUS_CRATES frozenset, occt/release txt files, kloc literal in select_harness_kloc_guard). But test_harness_kloc_cap.sh CONSOLIDATABLE_CRATES is not a literal copy: it is derived from harness_layout_consolidatable_crates in harness-layout-lib.sh, and test_verify_scope.sh also derives from it. Only verify.sh keeps a hand literal for kloc (the case ' reify-cli reify-syntax reify-kernel-occt reify-eval reify-compiler ' line), so the kloc copy count is overstated.

findings.title: decide_scope's staged primary diff is fail-open while its three sibling diffs fail wide
findings.statement: For --scope staged the primary file list is `_files="$(git ... diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRD | grep -v '^\.task/' || true)"`. Under `set -euo pipefail` the `|| true` that is there to absorb grep's no-match exit also absorbs a failing git diff. Verified by experiment: a failing git leaves _files empty with rc 0. An empty list classifies as docs-only (RUN_RUST=0, RUN_GUI=0, no gate). The branch-scope primary diff and both rename-source diffs check git's status explicitly and fail WIDE per contract C5, so one guard exists at three entry points and not at its sibling. The staged path is the hook-gated commit-to-main route, which has no later gate. S18 D5 states the staged primary-diff failure is "still fail-open", preserving it by decision.
findings.proposal: Split the pipeline: capture git's status in an `if ! _diff_out=$(...)` exactly like the branch arm, fail wide on non-zero, then filter .task/ in a separate step. In the S18 port this is gather_changed(scope) returning Result[ChangedSet]. One error policy, enforced at all four git calls by construction. Add a test_verify_scope.sh scenario that injects a failing git for the primary staged diff and asserts RUN_RUST=1. Not covered: D5 deliberately keeps the behaviour, so this needs an explicit amendment to #9097.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; sibling hardening is the branch-arm explicit status check (contract C5) and fix(6030)/fix(7096) fail-wide closure fixes
findings.verdict_notes: The staged arm is `git diff --cached --name-only ... | grep -v '^\.task/' || true`. The `|| true` absorbs a git failure, and the pipeline has no pipefail-visible check of git alone. The branch arm and both rename-source diffs check status and fail wide. The in-code comment openly says the staged path keeps || true.
findings.dedup_step: step 1 key lookup: none; step 2 search_tasks >=0.6: nearest #5140 (0.70, done, deletion-blind filter) and #9061 (0.64, lock-charter selection), different defects; step 3 curator: created #9170 depending on #9097 (S18 D5 amendment)

findings.title: Artifact-to-guard registries are hand-edited per new test and S18 adds more rows by rule
findings.statement: Whether an edit selects a guard test is declared in verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt (174 active rows, 29 artifacts with multiple rows). The sweep guard (verify-pipeline-guard.sh is-registered), verify-pipeline-paths.txt (full-gate paths) and doc-sync-paths.txt answer overlapping questions. 70 of the window's non-merge commits touch the infra map. The row's key is an artifact path and its value is a glob in a different file. The two are tied only by the author remembering to add a row, and drift is caught by an ANTI-DRIFT sweep that is itself a hand-maintained predicate. S18 kappa derives only gate paths from emitters. D14 and the infra-map note require each new Python module and member to add rows by hand ("Python member = stdlib unittest + .sh wrapper + manifest row + infra-map rows"). This is the 'register X with its gates' class (fix 6102, 7630, 6393 "re-home the infra-map rows") that S18 does not close.
findings.proposal: Let the test declare its subjects: a single `# guards: <path-or-glob> ...` header line (or an `GUARDS = [...]` constant in a .py member) read at plan time by one parser in reify_verify.selection. The map file, the is-registered sweep and the infra-map rows in D14 collapse into one test that every tests/infra member either has a guards header or an explicit `guards: none` marker. Locality: the declaration lives in the file the author is already creating. Dies: verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt rows and the ANTI-DRIFT sweep; fixtures that copy the map. Covered by no leaf; extends #9097/#9100 (selection and print-gates) and touches S19's run-all-classification.manifest, which should adopt the same declaration.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(6102) register the new test + fixture with their gates; fix(7630) re-anchor 8 infra guards; fix(6393) re-home the infra-map rows; 70 commits touching the map in the window
findings.verdict_notes: The infra-tests map has 174 active non-comment rows, consistent with the claim. The artifact-to-guard mapping is hand-maintained across the separate registry files. I did not independently verify the 70-commit figure or the 29-artifact figure.

findings.title: Three audit-predicate copies in selection remain hand-synced lists with no owning leaf
findings.statement: pdiag_swept_path re-implements crates/reify-audit pdiag.rs::is_swept_path. pdoccover_input_path re-implements pdoccover.rs is_chunk_path/in_oracle_scope (its case arms carry trailing comments naming the Rust function to keep in sync). select_cheap_ptodo_gate re-implements ptodo.rs::is_swept_ext as `*.rs|*.ri|*.sh|*.py|*.ts|*.tsx|*.js`. Each is guarded only by a drift test (PT-DRIFT, PDIAG-DRIFT, PDOCCOVER-DRIFT). Adding a swept extension or path in reify-audit therefore forces an unrelated verify-pipeline edit, which pays the full gate. S18 PRD sections 2.3, 8 and 9 keep "the three guarded copies" and record the single reify-audit --print-scope-predicates export as a follow-up candidate, not filed, because the hook path has no built binary.
findings.proposal: Skip the binary dependency: put the swept extensions and path globs in one data file under crates/reify-audit (for example scope-predicates.toml). The Rust predicates read it via include_str! and reify_verify.selection reads it as a DataFile (D15), so --print-gates lists it. Delete the 3 bash predicate bodies and their 3 drift tests; the file becomes the one home and a Rust test pins that the file and predicates agree. File the PRD-section-9 candidate with this cheaper form. Not covered by any leaf.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; drift guards PT-DRIFT/PDIAG-DRIFT/PDOCCOVER-DRIFT exist because of the copies
findings.verdict_notes: select_cheap_ptodo_gate comments call its extension list a DERIVED COPY of ptodo.rs is_swept_ext, guarded by PT-DRIFT. pdiag_swept_path (~2436) and pdoccover_input_path (~2485) exist as hand-synced predicates in the same way.

findings.title: The port deletes 3.2k lines of verify.sh rationale with no leaf that rehomes it
findings.statement: 3275 of verify.sh's 4833 lines (68%) are comments; 224 comment lines cite task or esc ids. add_tool is a one-line function under a ~60-line essay that records a review round and a rejected interim draft. The PG-DRIFT and GUI-coupled blocks above the two fixture lists run ~150 lines for two string literals. Under the Comments stance, review-answering prose belongs in commit messages and persistent rationale in docs/. Heuristic 14's measurement protocol (prose in its right home first) was recorded for the package partition in D1 but not for the prose. S18 zeta (#9112) deletes the bash body, alpha puts knob meanings in docs/notes/verify-pipeline-knobs.md, and S23 (#8540) retargets line cites. None of them decides which of the SCOPE CONTRACT, ambient-LD, role-matrix and C5 rationales survive into the Python modules or docs. A byte-stable behaviour port (D8) copies code and silently drops or silently ports prose.
findings.proposal: Add one step to gamma1/gamma2/zeta: for each verify.sh comment block longer than ~10 lines, classify it as (a) invariant now enforced by a type or table (delete), (b) persistent rationale (move to docs/notes/verify-pipeline-design.md with a symbol pointer from the module docstring), or (c) reviewer-answering history (drop; already in the commit log). Record the classification in each leaf's commit message. Dies: the essays on add_tool/_LD_SCRUB, the narrowing and coupled-list blocks. Extends #9098, #9099 and #9112; S23 does not cover prose that is not a line cite.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative; adjacent: fix(5986) stale cross-file citation, fix(6372) de-rot line pins
findings.verdict_notes: verify.sh is 4833 lines, and about 3275 lines start with '#' (matches the claim). add_tool is a one-line function at ~2970, preceded by a long rationale essay that cites a review round and a rejected interim draft. The forward-looking part, that no leaf rehomes the prose, is a plan claim I did not check.

findings.title: lib_main_checkout.sh scrubs a 4-variable git env subset, while lib_git_env_scrub.sh owns the 8-variable list
findings.statement: _reify_main_checkout_git hard-codes `env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE -u GIT_COMMON_DIR -u GIT_INDEX_FILE`. lib_git_env_scrub.sh declares itself the one home of the enumerated scrub set (GIT_DIR GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES GIT_COMMON_DIR GIT_NAMESPACE GIT_PREFIX; grep finds no other inline -u GIT_ scrub in scripts/ or hooks/). The resolver is the only reader of the main-checkout path for the setup scripts, verify's background ledger and review-readme.sh. The two lists already differ, and a variable added to the canonical list (the #7106 class) will not reach it. The lib's own header gives the `env -u` rationale (empty GIT_DIR hard-fails on git 2.43), which is exactly what reify_git_env_scrub already implements.
findings.proposal: Have _reify_main_checkout_git call reify_git_env_scrub git "$@" after sourcing lib_git_env_scrub.sh (with its own missing-file error naming the lib, as verify.sh does). Add lib_git_env_scrub.sh to the fixture copy set that ι's copy_verify_sandbox derives, so no new hand cp line is needed. Add the one behavioural test asserting reify_main_checkout answers correctly under each scrub variable set to a bogus value. Not covered by S18 (D15 lists reify_git_env_scrub_prefix and reify_main_checkout as separate BashCalls but does not connect them).
findings.bug_history_link: fix(7423) add lib_main_checkout.sh to 6 fixture copy lists; #7106 hook-env leak; speculative for a missed variable
findings.verdict_notes: The function hard-codes `env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE -u GIT_COMMON_DIR -u GIT_INDEX_FILE`. lib_git_env_scrub.sh REIFY_GIT_ENV_SCRUB_VARS holds the 8-variable list (adds GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_NAMESPACE, GIT_PREFIX). The two lists differ.

findings.title: The harness layout is policed by a bash scan on top of cargo's auto-discovery instead of being made unrepresentable
findings.statement: Upstream system: Cargo's integration-test auto-discovery plus rustc module resolution. Cargo compiles every top-level `tests/*.rs` as its own binary, which is the link-count cost C1 exists to cap. A harness is placed as `tests/harness_x.rs` with its members in `tests/harness_x/`, and rustc resolves a bare `mod` in that crate root against `tests/`, not `tests/harness_x/`. That forces a mandatory `#[path]` on each of the 846 member declarations. The test header says the failure modes are SILENT: a bare `mod x;` 'silently binds the WRONG file', and an undeclared member file 'is never compiled' so its tests vanish. All of these guards (Section 6 `harness_path_attr_violations`, rule (d) `harness_undeclared_member_violations`, rule (b), the diff gate) compensate for that. No crate sets `autotests` or `[[test]]`, and no `tests/*/main.rs` exists. The PRD `merge-gate-compile-cost.md` §5 C1 never considers cargo's native `tests/<name>/main.rs` form. Cost to the next change: each new test needs a hand-appended `#[path]`+`mod` pair on a shared root. Concurrent tasks append to the same tail, so `harness_engine.rs` and `harness_geometry.rs` recur in reconcile commits (e.g. 'merge(5392): keep both harness_engine mod declarations', 'merge(7418): reconcile with main (693 commits)'). A new test in the wrong place reds only after the full gate. Placement is also argued in 26 comment blocks.
findings.proposal: Make the contract structural, in three independently landable steps, and delete the guards each step makes redundant. STEP A (mechanical, per crate): move each `tests/harness_x.rs` to `tests/harness_x/main.rs`. Cargo auto-discovers `tests/*/main.rs` as a target named `harness_x`, so the nextest binary id and every `binary(harness_x)` selector are unchanged. A bare `mod foo;` then resolves to `tests/harness_x/foo.rs` exactly as rustc does, so the `#[path]` mandate and the 'silently binds the wrong sibling' mode cannot exist. Only genuinely external includes (`../common/mod.rs`) keep an explicit `#[path]`. The unit's own size becomes a `find` of the directory. STEP B (kills the registration step and the conflict hotspot): make membership directory-driven, via a directory-expanding macro (`automod`-style `dir!`), an in-workspace proc macro, or a 20-line build.rs that writes the `mod` list to OUT_DIR. Every `.rs` under `tests/harness_x/` is then a member by construction, and files deliberately not compiled move out of the module dir. Rule (d) becomes unrepresentable, and concurrent tasks stop editing the same root lines. STEP C: set `autotests = false` in the five crates and list the harness roots, override binaries and grandfathered standalones as `[[test]]` entries. Cargo then validates path existence (an orphan row is a build error), and the whole baseline manifest becomes the Cargo.toml `[[test]]` list. A stray `tests/*.rs` is no longer compiled, so keep a ~20-line check that `git ls-files 'crates/*/tests/*.rs'` is a subset of `cargo metadata` test src_paths, to stop silent non-compilation. DIES: `harness_path_attr_violations`, `harness_undeclared_member_violations`, `_bare_mod_decls`, `_harness_layout_mod_decls`, `_harness_layout_walk_unit`, `harness_layout_declared_members`, `harness_layout_orphan_rows`, `harness_layout_malformed_rows` and `_harness_layout_norm_path`/`_row_crate`. Also the baseline manifest, `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` as a diff-scoped heuristic, and roughly 40% of the 3,300-line test (their hermetic fixtures). PREVENTS: the re-home commits #5240, #5951, #6756, #7418, #4192, #6001, #5342, #5371, #5752, #6082, 'repair the stale --test invocation' (#5282), and the merge reconciles. RELATION: #8700 (S19 theta) only relocates the guard engine into libs and keeps the layout, the parser and the baseline; it does not close the registration tax. Not covered by any S19 leaf. If this lands, theta's guard-lib extraction should be re-scoped to the residual rules: kLOC measure and external includes.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(5240) 'layout ratchet'; fix(5951) 'land the regression under harness_engine'; fix(4192) 're-home both new tests'; fix(5342/5371/5752/6082/7418/6001) consolidate/register under harness_*; fix(5282) 'repair the stale --test invocation the consolidation broke'; merge(5392) 'keep both harness_engine mod declarations'; mined theme [70x] test placement churn
findings.verdict_notes: No autotests/[[test]] in crate Cargo.tomls and no tests/*/main.rs. harness_engine.rs relies on #[path] per member and the bash guards compensate. The 846 count and merge-reconcile history were not individually checked.

findings.title: The Rust mod-graph resolver is an awk parser with demonstrated wrong answers, duplicating a better Rust lexer already in the repo
findings.statement: `_harness_layout_mod_decls` re-implements, line by line in awk, which files rustc compiles from a root. Every harness-layout decision rests on it: the cap measure, the `#[path]` mandate, the undeclared-member rule and the external-include attribution. I ran it on a scratch file. (1) `#[path="h/a.rs"]` followed by `#[cfg(test)]` before `mod a;` reports `a` as `bare`, because 'any other line clears' the pending path. That is a false Section-6 FAIL, and the unit measure then drops the file. (2) A `mod ghost;` inside a `/* */` block comment is reported as a declaration, so a real orphan file named ghost.rs would be treated as declared, which hides the silent-non-compilation case rule (d) exists for. (3) `mod nested;` inside an inline `mod inl { }` is reported as a top-level bare decl. (4) `pub(crate) mod d;` is not matched at all (regex allows only `pub `), so d.rs is invisible to the measure and flagged as undeclared. None of these shapes is in the live roots today, so the live gate is green, but the next author who writes any of them gets a wrong red or, for (2), a wrong green. Meanwhile `scripts/assert-module-scc.py` already contains a more complete resolver (visibility, cfg, `#[path]`, inline-mod depth, string/comment-blind lexing via `RUST_LEXER_AWK` in `lib_rust_production_view.sh`), and `harness-layout-lib.sh` imports neither. Two parsers answer the same question and can disagree.
findings.proposal: One module-graph authority, not two. Preferred: if finding 1 lands, the parser shrinks to 'external includes of a unit', which is `rustc`'s own dep-info (`target/<profile>/deps/harness_x-*.d` lists exactly the files compiled into the unit) or `cargo metadata`'s test src_path. Measure from that or from the directory, and delete `_harness_layout_mod_decls`. If finding 1 is deferred: route the lib through the shared lexer (`RUST_LEXER_AWK` / a function exported by `assert-module-scc.py`'s resolver) so strings, block comments, `pub(...)` and attribute stacks are handled once, and add the four shapes above as must-fire/must-not-fire fixtures. ENFORCED: one parser consumed by both harness guards (the lib already is the single consumer inside the layout guards). DIES: the awk block and its attribute-binding prose (~60 lines of comment justifying line-based binding). PREVENTS the 'literal-blind brace/cfg parsing' class in the mined themes (#6421, #6424, #6430, #8369 are the same class in sibling scanners). RELATION: #8700 theta renames the helpers public and moves them to a guard lib but keeps the awk parser, so it does not cover this; extends #8700.
findings.bug_history_link: mined theme [12x] literal-blind brace/cfg parsing (#6421, #6424, #6430, #8369); fix(5620) transitive measure; speculative for the four specific shapes (not on live roots)
findings.verdict_notes: The awk resolver only matches `(pub )?mod x;` and clears a pending path on other lines. It has no block-comment, inline-mod or pub(crate) handling, so the described wrong answers follow from the regexes. The claim that scripts/assert-module-scc.py has a fuller resolver was not checked.

findings.title: Harness roots route placement through accreting prose that has gone false or points at escalations
findings.statement: `harness_engine.rs` is 158 lines, of which 114 are comments. Each member added since #5196 carries a block of the form 'Task #N lands here for the same anti-re-accretion reason as #5196's and #5360's above'. `git grep` finds 26 mentions of 're-accretion' across 10 harness files. This is escalating comment volume that signals the registration step is not self-explanatory (Comments stance), and each block is a drift site. Measured drift: `harness_geometry.rs` tells authors NOT to use `harness_fea_solver_e2e` because it is 'within ~700 lines of the 20 kLOC cap', but that unit measures 17,009 (about 3,000 lines of headroom). `harness-layout-lib.sh` and `test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` state '348 grandfathered baseline rows' and 'all 355 non-harness units', but the live baseline has 218 rows. The baseline header says 'deliberately not restated' while the other two files restate it. A Rust header cites 'Leo 2026-07-22, esc-5056-11', a pointer into an escalation record that no dispatched role can read (the Comments stance says that does not count). An agent choosing where to put a test reads these roots, so a false headroom claim steers placement wrongly.
findings.proposal: Delete the per-module rationale blocks from the roots and keep one pointer line to `docs/contributor/harness-layout-contract.md` (the file #8700 creates). Re-state the 'which harness' decision as a rule in that doc: topic first, then measure headroom with the guard's own output instead of a number in prose. Remove every restated count (348, 355, ~700, 585, 31 roots) and replace each with the command that derives it. Replace the esc-5056-11 / Leo-date citation with the ruling's one-sentence text in the doc. If finding 1 step B lands, the blocks have nothing left to explain and the roots become a bare macro call. RELATION: #8700 theta repoints the 35 `crates/**` headers that cite `test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` and moves the contract prose to docs, so the pointer half is covered. The per-module accretion blocks, the stale counts and the escalation citations are not, and S23 (prose burn-down, wave 4) is told not to retouch those headers. Extends #8700 and needs an explicit hand-off to S23.
findings.bug_history_link: amend(7654) 'correct the falsified cap claim, narrow the 0 0 enforcement claim'; docs(5282) 'delete the false rule-(a) claim from the four EVAL-3 harness roots'; amend 'drop post-split counts from the #6121 split-rationale header'
findings.verdict_notes: The baseline manifest has 218 data rows, but harness-layout-lib.sh:146-156 and test_harness_kloc_cap.sh:115 still say 348 and 355. harness_geometry.rs:24 says '~700 lines' of the 20 kLOC cap. harness_engine.rs is 158 lines. The 17,009 measurement and the 114 comment-line count were not re-run.

findings.title: The kLOC cap measures raw lines (17-28% of them comments) and its WARN ratchet machinery guards an empty set
findings.statement: The cap exists to bound merge-gate compile cost, but it is enforced on `wc -l` of every file in the unit, comments included. I measured the comment-line share of the three largest units: 17% (harness_syntax, 3,007 of 17,924 lines), 26% (harness_topology_selector) and 28% (harness_fea_solver_e2e). Of the 45 units, 8 are at or above 16,000 lines (80% of the cap) and 17 are above 12,000; harness_syntax measures 17,994, six lines under the 18,000 WARN trigger. A unit that ARRIVES in the WARN band is red until its row is added to the in-script `_KLOC_WARN_KNOWN` array in the same diff, so the next small test added to harness_syntax reds the gate for a squeeze the author did not cause. History: 'fix(5318): merge main to pick up the harness_occt kLOC warn-ratchet row', 'test(7543): re-measure the harness_compilation_surface _KLOC_WARN_KNOWN row', 'test(7709): empty _KLOC_WARN_KNOWN to red the squeeze'. The array is now empty (declared 'the healthy end state'), yet the ratchet machinery (`harness_warn_ratchet_violations`, `_warn_ratchet_rows`, PRUNE notes, hermetic Section 4c and live 5d) is still maintained. #8700 D11 moves it to a new manifest, entrenching it. Two independent axes are also conflated: a unit's name is its TOPIC, but its size forces a split along a prose seam (#5282 auto-resolution, #7654 milestone corpus, #7466 occt), so each split is a design decision with selector fallout.
findings.proposal: (1) Measure what the cap is a proxy for. Count non-comment, non-blank lines of the files in the unit's dep-info (finding 1/2), or gate on a measured per-binary compile cost if one is available from `cargo build --timings`; keep the 20k figure only as a code-line ceiling. (2) Make the WARN tier purely advisory output, with no gating row and no per-unit ratchet. Delete `_KLOC_WARN_KNOWN`, `harness_warn_ratchet_violations`, `_warn_ratchet_rows`, Section 4c/5d, and cancel the planned `harness-layout-warn.manifest`. The hard cap alone remains the gate, and it already bites on the commit that crosses it. (3) For size-driven splits, allow a numbered shard of the same topic (`harness_syntax_2`), so a split does not need a new topical name or a header argument. PREVENTS: the arrival-red churn above. RELATION: contradicts #8700 D11's plan to carry the ratchet forward as a manifest, so #8700 should drop that part. Not covered otherwise.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(5318) 'pick up the harness_occt kLOC warn-ratchet row'; test(7543) re-measure harness_compilation_surface row; test(7709) empty _KLOC_WARN_KNOWN; fix(5282) 'split the auto-resolution cluster out of harness_engine (kLOC cap)'; fix(6095) 'fold the gauge module into tensegrity_t0a to clear the kLOC cap'; fix(6162) 'acknowledge harness_cli in the kLOC WARN ratchet'
findings.verdict_notes: _KLOC_WARN_KNOWN=() is empty at line 372, and the ratchet machinery and its notes are still present. The comment-share percentages and the harness_syntax 17,994 figure were not re-measured.

findings.title: The run-all classification manifest is a 203-row central registry, 94% one value, edited 71 times in 2.5 months
findings.statement: Every `tests/infra/test_*.sh` needs a row `<name> <bucket>` in one shared file, enforced in both directions by the drift guard, so every new infra test must edit the same file. `git log --since=2026-08-01` shows 71 commits touching it. 191 of the 203 rows are `pool`, 7 `intra-run-serial` and 5 `host-exclusive`. The bucket is a property of the test (does it burn CPU, mutate lane-shared target/), but lives away from the test, so the file does not make sense in isolation (heuristic 13) and the fact is stored in two places (the test's behaviour and the row; heuristic 11). The mined history shows the row being forgotten or wrong: 'chore(5964): register test_reify_audit_pdiag_budget_skip.sh in run-all manifest', 'chore(7538): register test_pre_commit_ts_guard.sh', 'fix(5938): delete the orphan ... row', 'amend: drop the drifting row count from the manifest's pool banner (task 6582)', and live #6483 (bucket counts drift silently). The file also carries long per-row prose, and the S19 PRD (D8) keeps the 'row in the same diff' rule as is.
findings.proposal: Move the bucket into the test file as a fixed-grammar one-line pragma in its first 20 lines (`# run-all-bucket: pool|intra-run-serial|host-exclusive`). The pragma is required, so omitting it is red and explicitness is preserved. Make `classification_discovered_set` (the single discovery predicate S19 D2 already introduces) read it, and keep the manifest only as a generated, checked-in snapshot or delete it. The rationale for the 12 non-pool rows moves into those tests' headers, next to the behaviour that justifies it. ENFORCED at discovery: unknown bucket or missing pragma fails closed. DIES: ~190 rows, the two-direction orphan/missing-row checks, and the same-diff manifest edit that unrelated tasks conflict on. Before adopting, check every other reader of the manifest (verify.sh, `run_all.sh` H9, dark-factory). RELATION: S19 alpha/D2 (single discovery predicate) is the natural seam, but D8 explicitly keeps per-diff manifest rows, so this is not covered.
findings.bug_history_link: chore(5964)/chore(7538) 'register ... in run-all manifest'; fix(5938) orphan row; amend(6582) drifting row count; live #6483; 71 commits touching the file since 2026-08-01
findings.verdict_notes: 203 data rows: 191 pool, 7 intra-run-serial, 5 host-exclusive. The 71-commits figure was not re-run.

findings.title: reify-test-support/helpers.rs is a 3,335-line bag of five strata, 62% of it an inline test module
findings.statement: One-sentence purpose fails ('shared test helpers' = engine factories AND compile wrappers AND diagnostic assertions AND template/function lookup AND eval-result readers AND mesh aabb). Measured: about 1,260 lines of code, then `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` from line 1260 to 3335 (2,075 lines, 110 `#[test]`s). That is over the 2,000-line alarm, and a reader of any one helper loads the other 3,000 lines. Partition of the top-level symbols with the heuristic-13 check: (a) `collect_errors`, `error_diags`, `errors_only`, `warnings_only`, `underdetermined_diags`, `assert_*diagnostic*`, `assert_error_code_*`, `assert_no_type_cascade` need only `reify_core`; (b) `compile_source*`, `parse_and_compile*`, `compile_template`, `compile_first_template` import (a); (c) the `eval-helpers`-gated `make_engine*`, `eval_source`, `check_source*`, `run_modify_pipeline`, `build_against_mock_kernel`, `assert_no_eval_errors`, `cell_value`, `members_of` import (a) and (b); (d) `get_value_cell_in`, `get_let_expr*`, `get_function_in`, `lookup_value_cell`, `resolve_member_collision` need only `reify_compiler`/`reify_ir`. The imports run strictly downward (a, then b, then c) with no cycle or reach-back, so a split passes heuristic 13. Only 6 call sites use the `helpers::` path (2 files); everyone else reaches these through the crate-root glob `pub use helpers::*`, so no re-export shim is needed. The file grew by promotion (81 commits since August, e.g. 'feat(6524): promote underdetermined_diags', 'feat(7299): add make_engine_with_mock_kernel', 'feat(7253): add get_function_in'), so the next promotion makes it larger. Also, `collect_errors` and `error_diags` have identical bodies (docs: 'semantically equivalent') with `errors_only` a third wrapper, used 260, 182 and 1,389 times.
findings.proposal: Split into `diagnostics` (a), `compile` (b), `eval_helpers` (c, feature-gated as a whole module rather than per-fn `#[cfg]`) and `module_lookup` (d). Each module takes its own tests with it; the `panic_message`/`eval_result` fixtures go to the one module that uses them. The lib.rs glob re-exports keep the consumer paths, and the 6 `helpers::` users are repointed. Collapse `error_diags` into `collect_errors` (keep `errors_only` as the module-typed wrapper), as a mechanical rename across the roughly 18 files that use `error_diags`. Make `eval-helpers` a module-level gate so the 15 per-item `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` attrs die. This stays a split only if each new file passes heuristic 13, which the downward-only import structure above shows. PREVENTS: growth by promotion into an already-over-alarm file. RELATION: no review-all leaf covers reify-test-support.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (feature-velocity growth: feat(6524), feat(7299), feat(7253), fix(7341) 'resolve a member collision to the template's own cell')
findings.verdict_notes: The file is 3335 lines, `mod tests` starts at line 1261, and there are 110 #[test]s. collect_errors and error_diags have identical bodies, and errors_only wraps collect_errors. The five-strata partition and the downward-import claim were not traced.

findings.title: The 'baseline never grows' invariant is prose-only, and the diff gate fails open
findings.statement: The ratchet's whole contract is 'a ratchet only shrinks; growing is SUPERSEDED (Leo 2026-07-22)'. Nothing mechanical checks it. Rule (b) and `_check_candidates` accept an added standalone iff `harness_layout_baseline_contains` finds it, and that reads the working-tree baseline, which the same diff can edit. After the ruling, four rows were added anyway: fix(5347), fix(5364), fix(5302), amend(5214), dated 07-24 and 07-25 (none since, so the social rule is holding but is untested by the machine). The diff gate also fails open: a failed `_derive_added_from_git` falls through to `_check_candidates` with no args, which prints PASS with `added=0`; a missing lib exits 0; and no-arg stdin is a documented vacuous-green/hang trap (#7313). This is the 'check that cannot express its own failure' class.
findings.proposal: Add one monotonicity check in the diff-scoped gate: rows(HEAD baseline) must be a subset of rows(merge-base baseline); any added row is red naming the file and the ruling. Make derive-failure and missing-lib exit non-zero with an explicit `reason=cannot-derive-diff` instead of PASS. If finding 1 step C lands, the baseline becomes the `[[test]]` list and this check becomes 'no new `[[test]]` entry outside harness roots', but the fail-closed requirement stays. RELATION: not covered by #8700.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(5347)/fix(5364)/fix(5302)/amend(5214) grandfather rows added 2026-07-24..25 after the 07-22 ruling; docs #7313 vacuous-green trap; mined theme [16x] silent-green gates
findings.verdict_notes: The fail-open is real: --from-git exits 0 and prints PASS with added=0 when the base is underivable, and the script header documents this. It is a deliberate, acknowledged design choice, not a missed guard. The claim that nothing mechanical enforces baseline growth rests on the working-tree baseline check, which I did not fully trace. The four post-ruling grandfather rows were not verified.

findings.title: update_source's active-file guard exists on one of four doors; the engine method silently ignores its path argument
findings.statement: EngineSession::update_source(path, content) takes a path and deliberately ignores it whenever core.file_path() is set (module_name and entry come from the session). #5097 found that this lets reify_update_source(file_path=lib.ri) overwrite the active entry module, and fixed it only in debug_server.rs (update_source_target_matches_active, refusing a mismatch). The same call is reached unguarded from three other doors. (1) The Tauri update_source command, via commands::editor_source_edit -> reload_for_watch_impl -> update_source_impl. Its payload path is the editor's activeFile tab in Editor.tsx's updateListener, and in App.tsx handleReEvaluate. Tabs can be an import: navigateToDiagnostic and go-to-definition open cross-file tabs and setActiveFile them. build_gui_state's files holds only the entry, since source_map stores only the entry. Typing in an imported file's tab therefore recompiles the import's text as the entry module. (2) disk_reload_edit(path) reads the given file and calls the same path-ignoring update_source. (3) TauriToolContext::update_source has no guard today. The debug_server.rs doc says the path-ignoring behaviour is 'right for the editor, which only ever edits the active buffer', but the editor's active tab is not the engine's entry. The sibling duty 'consult holds_rejected_source before persisting files[].content' is likewise a consumer obligation, enforced at one consumer. The S25 plan (section 2.8 row 3, leaf xi) re-implements the guard in mcp_context.rs only; QueuedEngine unifies ordering and publication, not admission, and the contract says the guarantee is per module.
findings.proposal: Make admission a property of the engine API (heuristic 10, uniformly enforced at the one choke point, as export already does for #6190). Introduce a typed EntryDocument (or SourceTarget) newtype built by EngineSession::resolve_target(path) -> Result<EntryDocument, NotActiveEntry>, which absorbs update_source_target_matches_active, source_key_matches_path and the canonicalize arms. Change update_source to take EntryDocument, so the ignored string parameter disappears. NotActiveEntry names the requested and active paths (informative violation). commands::editor_source_edit, disk_reload_edit and the host update_source all go through it; the editor and watcher paths map a refusal to a diagnostic or toast (a tab for a non-entry file is not engine-backed). Also make EngineSession expose persistable_source() -> Result<&str, RejectedBuffer>, so holds_rejected_source stops being a convention. Deletable: the debug_server.rs guard and its pure-function tests (S25 omicron already deletes them), the xi copy in mcp_context.rs, and the 'right for the editor' caveat prose. It would have prevented #5097 and the editor-path twin of it. Relation: extends xi #8950 and omicron #8951 (they place the guard in the AI host only); not covered for the Tauri editor and watcher doors. Add a regression test: open a design with an import, call editor_source_edit with the import's path, and assert refusal with the entry unchanged.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(5097): reify_update_source refuses a non-active file_path (b421eeca90); fix(5097) gate holds_rejected_source to its consumers (7c52d02791); fix(5193)/#5359 open-funnel family; same class as #6190 (closed by putting the gate in the engine)
findings.verdict_notes: EngineSession.update_source derives module_name and entry from core.file_path() and uses path only for the no-file fallback. The only mismatch guard is debug_server.rs::update_source_target_matches_active. commands.rs::editor_source_edit and disk_reload_edit reach the same path-ignoring call unguarded, and mcp_context.rs::TauriToolContext.update_source has no guard.
