I did not trace the editor active-tab payload in depth.

findings.title: Which file the watcher follows is decided by each open funnel; the debug funnel never re-arms it, and the stale watcher can clobber the new design
findings.statement: The invariant 'the FS watcher watches the engine's loaded design' has no owner. watch_file is called from exactly two places in main.rs: the open_file_engine Tauri command and the argv-launch completion handler. The third open funnel, debug open_file/load_fixture (open_source_into_engine_and_refresh_baseline), calls load_file_into_engine and pushes the frontend, but DebugServerState holds no watcher or AppHandle slot, so it cannot re-arm. After a debug-driven open, the watcher still targets the previous file. Edits to the new file never hot-reload, which contradicts the contract's and sidecar prompt's advice that 'Claude edits natively and the FS-watcher reloads'. Worse, a later change to the OLD file fires disk_reload_edit(old_path), which reads the old file and calls the path-ignoring update_source (previous finding), replacing the newly opened design with the old file's source. Argv-launch additionally sets state.initial_file (the sidecar workspace) while File-Open does not, so identity side effects diverge per funnel. #6257 (open-funnel gaps) covers only files[].path canonicalization, not watcher or identity side effects. The S25 plan keeps the open funnel as a snapshot job over commands::load_initial_file_impl, and DebugServerState becomes {engine, selection, frontend, registry}, which has no watcher either.
findings.proposal: Give the watch target one owner and derive it from engine truth. Add a DesignWatch component (main.rs or a new watch_follow.rs) whose reconcile(engine_canonical_path) re-arms when the path differs. Call it from a SessionEvents 'design_loaded' event (S25 lambda's sink) or from the queue after any snapshot/evaluation ticket whose job loaded a file, so all three funnels, and any future one, get it for free. Disk reloads then also take the EntryDocument check from the previous finding, so a stale watcher event is refused rather than applied. Deletable: both explicit watch_file calls in main.rs and the funnel-specific initial_file bookkeeping, which can become a derived accessor. Prevents the #5194/#5338/#5359 'GUI path lags the CLI/engine seam' class. Relation: extends lambda #8947 (event sink) and rho #8954 (open funnel); not covered by any leaf today, and not covered by #6257.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(5193)/#5359 debug-bridge open_file duplicates; #6257 open-funnel gaps (pending); #5194/#5338 reload and argv-launch path divergence; fix(gui-watcher) trailing-edge debounce e81d9377ef
findings.verdict_notes: watch_file is called only at main.rs:484 (open_file_engine) and main.rs:1041 (argv-launch handler). The debug open funnel has no watcher handle: debug_server.rs mentions the watcher only in comments. initial_file is set only on the argv path. The stale-watcher clobber follows from disk_reload_edit calling the path-ignoring update_source.

findings.title: Preview-override liveness is an implicit state: every refused commit recompiles unconditionally, and 'a preview must be followed by a commit' is an unenforced cross-IPC protocol
findings.statement: preview_parameter writes its override only into last_check, with no flag, cell id or generation. The engine then has two legal states (committed, or committed plus transient override) that are distinguished nowhere. commit_parameter's own comment admits 'this method cannot know whether a preview is live', so on every refusal it does an unconditional full recompile through update_source (discard_parameter_preview), then hand-restores a (compile_failure, last_reload_error) snapshot. Six fix(5099) commits (discard on refusal, ledger discipline, tell the frontend what replaced the preview, path resolution of the discard, fileless cadence, boxing the restored state) all patch consequences of the missing state. The rule that a preview must be followed by a commit is carried by MechanismPanel.tsx's RAF/coalesce/flush choreography and EditOrder ordering, across IPC, with nothing in the engine detecting an abandoned preview. Export, save and the debug engine_state read all happily proceed while an override is live; export builds from declared defaults, which is the esc-7281-4 defect class the doc names. reload_would_be_a_no_op will also skip a same-text echo while an override is live.
findings.proposal: Add an explicit PreviewState to the engine session (a private field of the CoreState neighbourhood, with one transition table). PreviewState is None or Live{cell, generation}. preview_parameter sets it; commit_parameter, update_source, load_file and discard clear it through commit_state (one place); every state-publishing method reads it. Then commit_parameter discards only when Live{cell} matches (no recompile on an unrelated refusal), export and save_file return a typed 'preview live' refusal or flag instead of silently building without the override, and GuiState (or its delta) can carry preview_live so the frontend can show it and tests can assert it. Deletable: the unconditional-discard commentary, the failure-surface snapshot dance, and the esc-7281-4 caveat prose. Would have prevented the #5099 series and esc-7281-4. Relation: not covered by S25 (its D6 touches build_preview_gui_state only). It composes with the S25 eta builder (#8943) if PreviewState is added to the shared assemble_gui_state inputs.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(5099) x6: a refused commit discards the preview it refused (6776b97823), keeps the ledger discipline (1558e0bbfd), tells the frontend what replaced the preview (5be3872526), boxes the GuiState (4b626aa091); esc-7281-4
findings.verdict_notes: The comment 'This method cannot know whether a preview is live' is present in commit_parameter. I did not count the six fix(5099) commits.

findings.title: Camera pose is applied and read in three places; the debug bridge reaches into OrbitControls internals through a raw DebugViewport
findings.statement: The operation 'apply a CameraState to camera + controls' exists in bridge.ts set_camera (position, up, syncOrbitUpAxis, target, zoom, updateProjectionMatrix, controls.update, updateMatrixWorld, render) and, separately, in Viewport.tsx's saved-camera restore (position.set, up.set, target.set, zoom, updateProjectionMatrix, controls.update). The read side is also duplicated (set_camera's 'applied' vs Viewport's snapshotCamera, with a comment saying 'same reads as'). The #6965 fixes (stale matrixWorld before raycast, orbit frame not re-derived when up changes, 'applied' built from request not live state) each patched the debug copy. The restore copy still omits syncOrbitUpAxis, so a persisted camera whose up differs from the constructor's Z orbits about the stale axis, which is the #6497 defect. The root cause is that DebugViewport exposes the raw scene, camera, renderer and controls, so the bridge, a test harness surface, owns camera semantics, and controls.ts holds the only three-private-field poke. S26 tau (#9081) moves the camera handlers into handlers/camera.ts, move-only, and does not unify the pose operations.
findings.proposal: Add gui/src/viewport/cameraPose.ts exporting applyCameraState(camera, controls | undefined, state) -> CameraState (the live post-constraint pose, with syncOrbitUpAxis and the matrix refresh inside) and readCameraState(camera, controls). Expose them on DebugViewport as setCameraPose and pickEntityAt hooks that Viewport.tsx implements, and narrow DebugViewport so that scene, camera and renderer are no longer public to the bridge. Viewport restore, persistCamera, set_camera and the pick/project handlers call the same functions. Deletable: the duplicated sequences and the 'same reads as snapshotCamera' comments; the bridge stops importing three's Raycaster path. Would have prevented the four #6965 fixes and the restore-path twin. Relation: not covered by S26 tau (#9081, move-only); it should be an added leaf there or a follow-up.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(6965) x4: raycast through the live camera pose (5763bad326), re-derive orbit frame when set_camera changes up (9fd2e8052a), build applied from live state (c36f33272b); #6497
findings.verdict_notes: bridge.ts calls syncOrbitUpAxis at line 1461. The Viewport.tsx saved-camera restore sets position, up, target and zoom, then calls controls.update, and never calls syncOrbitUpAxis. The pose-apply logic is duplicated and the restore copy lacks the sync.

findings.title: Path-write policy is stated four times with different strength; screenshot save_path escapes the confinement that #7816 added
findings.statement: Whether a caller-named path may be written is decided independently by (1) write_confinement::confine_to_design_dir for reify_save_file/reify_export (design directory, symlink-aware); (2) screenshot_save::take_save_path for the three image tools (absolute, .png suffix, parent exists, nothing else, so any directory the GUI process can write, overwriting existing .png files); (3) save_file_impl (raw std::fs::write, Tauri user door, unconfined by intent); and (4) export_impl (raw path). #7817's rationale (the GUI process is not under the sidecar's landlock bound, so debug tools must not be a write-escape) applies equally to save_path, which the same assistant can call (the sidecar ALLOWED_TOOLS globs mcp__reify-debug__*). #7817 was cancelled as landed by #7816, which covered only the two reify_* tools. Neither S25 (xi moves confine_to_design_dir into the host for the reify_* tools only) nor S26 mentions save_path, and docs/debug-mcp-contract.md describes save_path without a confinement rule.
findings.proposal: Introduce one WriteTarget admission type in write_confinement.rs: WriteTarget::admit(origin: WriteOrigin{User, Assistant}, requested, design) -> Result<WriteTarget, WriteTargetRefusal>, where Assistant origins require confinement (design dir plus an explicit screenshot dir such as REIFY_WORKSPACE or the tmp dir the sandbox already allows) and User origins pass through. save_image_result and the host save/export take a WriteTarget, never a raw path, so an unadmitted write does not type-check. Deletable: take_save_path's ad-hoc rules and the duplicated absolute-path checks. Relation: extends xi #8950 (placement row 6); the image-tool half is not covered by any leaf, so add it to omicron/rho or file a follow-up.
findings.bug_history_link: #7817 (cancelled, delivered by #7816 for two tools only); fix(6752) save_path tests
findings.verdict_notes: take_save_path checks only that the path is absolute and ends in .png. It does no call to write_confinement::confine_to_design_dir. Only the reify_save_file and reify_export paths in debug_server.rs use confined_write_target.

findings.title: Sidecar 'must be Ready' precondition is re-decided per command and left as a caller duty on the handle
findings.statement: The same four-arm match on SidecarState (Ready -> proceed; Crashed(msg) -> 'sidecar crashed: ...'; NotStarted -> 'sidecar not started'; Starting -> 'sidecar not ready (still starting)') is copy-pasted in claude_send_message_impl and claude_permission_decision_impl, with a third variant in wait_ready (which returns a 'not ready after notification: {:?}' message). SidecarHandle::send_message documents 'the caller is responsible for ensuring the sidecar is in the Ready state', abort is tolerant by design, and clear_session writes unconditionally. So the state machine's legal-operation table lives in the callers, and a new command must remember to copy it. S26 alpha (#9062) fixes the permission-decision wire defect but not this structure.
findings.proposal: Add SidecarState::require_ready(&self) -> Result<(), String> as the single owner of the refusal text, and have SidecarHandle::send_message and permission_decision call it internally (checked at the handle, the use site, redundantly with the impl-level lookup only for None). The *_impl functions reduce to 'lock slot, get handle, call'. Deletable: both duplicated matches and the 'caller is responsible' note. Relation: not covered; fold into S26 alpha #9062 if touched there.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative
findings.verdict_notes: The same four-arm match on SidecarState (Ready, Crashed, NotStarted, Starting) with identical error strings appears in claude_send_message_impl (lines 648-651) and claude_permission_decision_impl (lines 694-697). wait_ready has a separate variant at lines 504-505.

findings.title: TauriToolContext locks the engine mutex raw at 12 sites while every other door uses the panic-catching, poison-recovering with_engine_lock
findings.statement: engine_lock::with_engine_lock is documented as the one lock policy (recover from poison via into_inner, catch_unwind, drop the guard before returning so no new poison is created). commands.rs uses it 21 times and debug_server's run_on_engine uses it. mcp_context.rs instead calls self.engine.lock().map_err(Lock error) at 12 sites with no catch_unwind. A panic inside build_gui_state, export or the OCCT kernels under that host poisons the mutex. All other doors would recover from the poison, while this host and its next call would return 'Lock error: poisoned' forever. S25 xi will re-host this context as TauriToolContext<'e> inside queued jobs, and nothing in the plan says the host adopts with_engine_lock.
findings.proposal: In xi #8950, make the host reach the engine only through one private helper, TauriToolContext::with_session(|s| ...) that wraps with_engine_lock and maps its Err to ToolError::InternalError. Ratchet the 12 raw .lock() sites in mcp_context.rs to 0 via an adoption-ratchet row. Deletable: the 12 map_err(Lock error) closures. Relation: extends xi #8950, which does not state this.
findings.bug_history_link: speculative
findings.verdict_notes: The structure is real: mcp_context.rs locks the engine raw with a Lock error map_err and never calls with_engine_lock or catch_unwind. The site count is 11, not 12. I did not verify the 21 uses of with_engine_lock in commands.rs.

findings.title: Expression and member traversal is re-spelled in 5+ places; references.rs holds a third in-file copy that already drifted
findings.statement: Heuristic 11 (SPOT) and 3 (one mechanism per axis of change). references.rs already defines for_each_member_direct_expr and for_each_direct_subexpr, and collect_uses and collect_decl_name_uses_in_members use them. cursor_on_member_segment (about 130 lines) and expr_member_segment_hit (about 100 lines) do NOT use them. They hand-mirror both: a 20-arm ExprKind match and a MemberDecl-kind match with the where-clause, forall and connect sub-cases spelled out again. Their doc comments mirror 'collect_uses (470-566)' and 'for_each_child_scope (335-357)', line cites that are now stale. That is how the window's fix commits 'walk SubDecl::index_domain in collect_uses_in_sub', 'walk index_domain in cursor_on_member_segment's Sub arm' and 'walk relate_relations in the same arm' each needed a separate commit. for_each_child_scope ends in `_ => {}` and its comment says rustc does not flag a missing arm; the sketch arm was added by hand (task 5506). It re-declares the child-body set that reify-ast::walk_members declares as data in MemberRecursionSet (Sub overrides, Port, Sketch, GuardedGroup, MatchArmDeclGroup). Outside the LSP, reify-compiler holds independent exhaustive ExprKind child enumerations in entity.rs (for_each_child and for_each_child_mut, whose doc says 'modelled on dot_chain_lint::walk_expr_depth, the authoritative current AST-child enumeration', i.e. copies of copies), dot_chain_lint.rs and shadow_lint.rs. reify-ast offers member walkers but no Expr child enumeration at all.
findings.proposal: In reify-ast, beside walk_members, add three wildcard-free primitives: `Expr::for_each_child(&self, &mut dyn FnMut(&Expr))` with a `_mut` twin, `MemberDecl::for_each_direct_expr(&self, ...)` (the current for_each_member_direct_expr, including sub_direct_exprs and the keyed-entry overrides), and `MemberDecl::child_scopes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item=&[MemberDecl]>`, defined once on top of sub_override_bodies and MemberRecursionSet. walk_members becomes a client of child_scopes, so the recursion-set table is the only place the child-body set is declared. reify-lsp then deletes for_each_direct_subexpr, for_each_member_direct_expr, sub_direct_exprs, keyed_entry_param_override_exprs and for_each_child_scope. cursor_on_member_segment shrinks to a short `any`-style fold over for_each_direct_expr + child_scopes (about 15 lines); expr_member_segment_hit shrinks to the MemberAccess arm plus for_each_child. reify-compiler deletes the entity.rs, dot_chain_lint and shadow_lint child enumerations. The step with no external dependency is to rewrite cursor_on_member_segment onto the existing local helpers now, which removes about 200 lines and the stale line cites. A new ExprKind or MemberDecl field becomes one compile error in reify-ast instead of a fix commit per walker; this would have prevented the three index_domain/relate_relations fixes and the sketch-arm gap. Relation to existing leaves: not covered. η #8772 adds only Declaration::member_scopes. #7860 is a scope-aware member walker for shadow_lint, whose option (b), 'source the child-body set from reify-ast', is the natural overlap, so extend #7860 or file a sibling under S9. #7588 concerns CompiledExprKind, a different tree.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(reify-lsp) walk SubDecl::index_domain in collect_uses_in_sub; walk index_domain in cursor_on_member_segment's Sub arm; walk relate_relations in the same arm; fix(6615) account for derivation in reify-lsp's exhaustive SubDecl pattern; task 5506 sketch arm in for_each_child_scope; #7860; #7588
findings.verdict_notes: expr_member_segment_hit hand-matches ExprKind arms and cursor_on_member_segment hand-matches MemberDecl arms with where-clause cases. Separate shared helpers for_each_member_direct_expr and for_each_direct_subexpr exist and are used by other walkers. for_each_child_scope ends in `_ => {}` and has the sketch arm added by hand. I did not open every compiler copy (entity.rs, dot_chain_lint.rs, shadow_lint.rs). shadow_lint.rs does have its own walk_expr_depth.

findings.title: Declaration and member name tokens are recovered by rescanning source text because the AST stores bare String names
findings.statement: Heuristic 12 (structured data, no ad-hoc parsers of source) and 11. ParamDecl, LetDecl, SubDecl, PortDecl and every Declaration carry `name: String` plus the whole-statement span. SubDecl.structure_name, PortDecl.type_name and ConstraintInstDecl.name carry no span at all. name_token_span therefore takes the first whole-word occurrence of the name inside the statement span (is_ident_byte scan plus UTF-8 snapping). It has 11 production call sites: bindings (4), type and constraint uses, sub-construction uses, port trait uses, symbols and goto_def. The rescan is wrong whenever the wanted token is not the first occurrence. #7541 (live, pending, still present at collect_decl_name_uses_in_members' Sub arm) is `sub Hole = Hole()`: the binding token is returned instead of the construction-site token, so cross-file rename rewrites the binding and leaves `sub Bore = Hole()`. That buffer re-parses clean, so rename's parse-cleanliness invariant does not catch it. The fix(7529) pair shows the failure mode: the earlier bare-substring locator matched the `s` of `structure s`, and its fallback emitted a name.len()-wide span over the leading keyword, 'a destructive edit' on the rename write path. The fallback is still an empty span that each consumer interprets differently (goto_def maps it to None, name_selection_range degrades to the statement start, references propagates it into the edit set). The AST is already moving the other way: SubDerivation.prototype, param_resets, SubParamOverride.name and disposition paths are SpannedIdent, 'so a diagnostic can underline the token ALONE'. Decl names, structure_name, type_name and ConstraintInst name are not.
findings.proposal: In reify-ast, give every declared or referenced name a `SpannedIdent` (name + name_span) and populate it at the single lowering site in reify-syntax (ts_parser lower_*). The tree-sitter node for the name field already has the byte range. Consumers read `x.name_span` and name_token_span, is_ident_byte's use here, the three empty-span conventions and `decl_name_span_in`'s refusal logic all die; the decl_oracle 'name_token' contract tests become lowering tests in reify-syntax. This fixes #7541 by construction (the construction-site ident has its own span) and removes the need for a bounded-search helper variant. A migration can proceed field by field: structure_name, type_name and ConstraintInst name first (the three no-span cases, where the rescan is only correct by luck), then decl names. Relation: not covered. χ #8756 only moved name_token_span into decl_oracle.rs, #7541 point-fixes one call site, and no PRD under docs/prds adds AST name spans.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(7529): locate declaration name tokens with analysis::name_token_span; fix(7529): refuse when a decl span excludes its own name token (destructive keyword edit); #7541 (live)
findings.verdict_notes: name_token_span rescans source text inside a statement span. Non-test callers are in references.rs (about 11 sites), symbols.rs and goto_def.rs. collect_decl_name_uses_in_members pushes name_token_span(source, s.span, name) for a Sub whose structure_name matches, so `sub Hole = Hole()` would pick the first occurrence, as claimed. I did not check #7541's task status.

findings.title: The compile + guard + check pipeline for one document version is spelled three times and re-executed per hover and completion request
findings.statement: Heuristics 11, 7 and 13. The sequence `compile_with_stdlib_checked(&parsed, &SimpleConstraintChecker)` -> `eval_guard::skip_reason(&compiled)` -> `Engine::new(Box::new(SimpleConstraintChecker), None)` -> check appears in AnalysisContext::from_parsed, compute_diagnostics_with_state and compute_diagnostics. The window's fix commits wired the real checker 'at the two diagnostics.rs compile sites' and then 'at AnalysisContext::from_parsed' as separate GREEN steps, and the containment guard 'at both diagnostics.rs sites' and 'at AnalysisContext::from_parsed' as two more. A fourth consumer would be a fifth site with no compile error if it were forgotten. Only the parse is memoised per document version (DocumentState::parsed_cache, a Mutex<Option<Arc<ParsedModule>>>). The server's hover and completion handlers call AnalysisContext::from_parsed(doc.parsed_module()), which runs a full compile and Engine::check, inline on the async worker, for every request, although didChange has already compiled and checked that same version inside compute_diagnostics_with_state with its own CompiledModule and Engine. AnalysisContext's own doc points to 'server.rs:268-284' for its Send-safety rationale, and the reason from_parsed constructs a throwaway Engine is only to keep the undef-cause trace. The two pipelines also differ silently (undef-cause capture on in one, off in the other).
findings.proposal: Introduce one constructor, e.g. `analysis::analyse(parsed: &Arc<ParsedModule>, mode: EngineMode) -> Analysis { compiled: CompiledModule, skipped: Option<SkippedEval>, check: Option<CheckResult>, engine: Engine }`, which is the only place that names SimpleConstraintChecker, calls compile_with_stdlib_checked, applies eval_guard and builds the engine. Memoise the result on DocumentState beside parsed_cache (OnceLock per version), so hover, completion, symbols and the diagnostics pass of the same version share one compile+check. EvalState keeps only the incremental engine and hash for eval_cached. AnalysisContext becomes a view over Analysis. Deletable: the three copies of checker injection and guard wiring, the per-request compile+check on hover and completion, and the fk-1a772 placement problem's cost half (hover and completion stop being the expensive handlers, so ι #8774 shrinks to moving only cache misses). Relation: extends ε #8759 (which adds check_result to DiagnosticsResult but keeps separate pipelines), γ #8778 (moves the compile call onto compile_program but still at three sites) and ι #8774 (moves the cost to the blocking pool instead of removing it); no leaf shares the result across requests.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(reify-lsp) GREEN — inject real constraint checker at the two diagnostics.rs compile sites / at AnalysisContext::from_parsed; GREEN — wire the containment guard at both diagnostics.rs sites / at AnalysisContext::from_parsed; #6851, #6798
findings.verdict_notes: compile_with_stdlib_checked appears in from_parsed and in both compute_diagnostics_with_state and compute_diagnostics. skip_reason appears at the same sites. server.rs calls from_parsed(doc.parsed_module()) at lines 580 and 670 (hover and completion handlers), so the compile and check run per request. from_parsed builds its own Engine with undef-cause capture on.

findings.title: Cursor-to-symbol resolution has no shared seam: every feature starts from a text word, and only references adds AST-aware refusals
findings.statement: Heuristics 9 and 11. hover (hover.rs:32), goto_def (goto_def.rs:38 and :263), references (references.rs:120 and :1288 for prepare_rename) all call convert::find_word_at_offset(source, offset), a byte-level identifier scan, and then look the word up by name. Context that a symbol resolver should decide is then bolted on per feature. (a) The `.member` segment guard (cursor_on_member_segment) exists only in collect_references_at, so hover and goto_def on the `diameter` in `h.diameter` resolve to a same-named param of the enclosing structure. hover calls find_member_decl(word, enclosing) and goto_def's phases A-C do the same, with no member-segment check. (b) hover and goto_def use reify-ast's flat find_named_member_span (first match, no shadowing), while references has a second, region-based shadowing model (Binding, resolve_use, depth tie-breaks) that it says is 'mirrored, not reused' from reify-compiler/scope.rs. That is three scope models for the same question. (c) reify-ast's own MemberRecursionSet doc admits hover/goto-def on a sketch-local name 'unresolved' (NAMED_MEMBER_LOOKUP excludes sketches) although references and outline treat the sketch as a scope. (d) goto_def's Phase C is lexical: a comment, a string or a shadowing lambda param resolves to the top-level declaration (#7607, documented as KNOWN IMPRECISION and pinned by a test that asserts the wrong answer). #7607 owns only that one case.
findings.proposal: Add `cursor.rs`: `fn resolve_cursor(parsed: &ParsedModule, source: &str, offset: usize) -> CursorTarget`, where `CursorTarget = DeclName{decl} | ValueUse{binding: Binding} | MemberSegment{base: &Expr} | TypeUse{name} | Keyword | Trivia(Comment|String) | None`. It is computed once from AST spans (expressions already carry spans) plus a comment/string oracle from reify-syntax (per #7607), and takes ownership of references.rs's Binding/collect_bindings/resolve_use/cursor_on_member_segment. hover, goto_def, references, rename, highlight and completion's DotAccess become `match resolve_cursor(..)` with a wildcard-free match, so a new target kind is one compile error across all features. Deletable: find_word_at_offset call sites, goto_def Phase C's lexical fallback and its wrong-answer pin, hover's and goto_def's flat lookups for member names, and the 'mirror collect_uses' discipline between two scanners. The binding model should be reconciled with reify-compiler/scope.rs, either by sharing a precedence function through reify-ast or by a cross-check test. Relation: not covered. #7607 covers one phase, η and θ cover declaration-kind dispatch, and ψ #8757 only moves code. Best sequenced after finding 1 so the resolver is built on the shared traversal.
findings.bug_history_link: #7607 (Phase C scope-unaware, filed from 6388 review); task-4346 member-segment guard added only to references; reify-ast MemberRecursionSet sketch-local note; fix(7529)/#7541 token selection
findings.verdict_notes: The function starts at line 212 and the next top-level item is at about 873, so its length is consistent with the claim. It mixes compile, the skip_reason early return and EvalState mutation. I did not verify the exact string-literal counts or the server.rs count of 21.

findings.title: compute_diagnostics_with_state is a 485-line function that interleaves eight stages, EvalState mutation ordering, and string diagnostic codes
findings.statement: Heuristics 4, 2, 6 and 10 (and 12 for the codes). The function (lines 212-697) runs: parse, parse-error early return, compile, containment skip, EvalState version/hash/cold-vs-warm eval, check_snapshot fallback, violated-message filtering, eval-diagnostic merge, span-aware violation errors, the FEA hint (about 100 lines, including two nested maps and a long perf rationale), and freshness diagnostics. The invariants between stages live in prose. 'Placement before the state mutations is LOAD-BEARING' (state.version_counter and last_content_hash must stay unadvanced on the skip path, else the stale-cache bug); last_content_hash is written only at the very end; a debug-only WARNING covers 'hash matched but engine uninitialised'. Nothing in the types stops a new early return between the version_counter increment and the final hash write from leaving EvalState half-advanced. LSP-level diagnostic codes are bare strings: "computation-failed" and "computation-pending" appear as literals here and in 8+ test sites, FEA_NOT_EVALUATED_CODE is a private const, and `lsp_types::Diagnostic { source: Some("reify".to_string()), ..Default::default() }` is hand-built about 8 times in this file (21 more times in server.rs). Neither ε #8759 (result type, tests) nor ω #8770 (test-module move) touches the function body.
findings.proposal: Split into stage functions with explicit data flow: `parse_stage`, `compile_stage` (finding 3's `analyse`), `eval_stage(&mut EvalState, &CompiledModule) -> EvalOutcome` as the ONLY writer of version_counter/last_content_hash/engine (commit on success only, so the ordering rule becomes a type-level property of one function), then pure `violation_diagnostics(&CheckResult, &spans)`, `fea_hint_diagnostics(&CheckResult, &CompiledModule, &Engine)`, `freshness_diagnostics(&Engine, &CompiledModule)`. Add `enum LspDiagnosticCode { ComputationFailed, ComputationPending, FeaNotEvaluated }` with `as_str()` and a single `lsp_diagnostic(severity, code, range, message)` constructor used by diagnostics.rs and server.rs. Deletable: the prose ordering warnings, the repeated Diagnostic literals, and the test string literals. Relation: extends ε #8759 (it ports tests to check_result but leaves the body) and ζ #8771 (edits two loops inside this function). Do it after finding 3 so the compile stage already lives elsewhere. This is a decomposition for a stateful pipeline, not a line-count target.
findings.bug_history_link: fix(5240) keep the eval_cached guard-bypass note out of the editor stream / re-home eval_cached_guarded_groups; GREEN — wire the containment guard at both diagnostics.rs sites; fix(6162) bound the unknown-URI log and hoist it out of the state write lock
findings.verdict_notes: determine_context reads the text of the current line only. It checks ends_with('.') for DotAccess. For TypePosition it requires starts_with_decl_keyword, an rfind(':') and no '=' in the text after that colon. For `sub bolt = Bolt(length: ` this returns TypePosition because it is checked before the Expression branch. The determine_context tests cover only `param x:` and `let x:`, not named arguments.

findings.title: Completion context is classified by line-text heuristics; a named constructor argument is treated as a type position
findings.statement: Heuristic 12 (ad-hoc parser of source text) and 2. determine_context decides DotAccess, TypePosition and Expression from the current line's text before the cursor: `trim_end().ends_with('.')`, and for TypePosition 'line starts with param/let/sub AND rfind(':') AND no `=` after that colon'. For `    sub bolt = Bolt(length: ` (a common form; examples/auto_binding_sites.ri:94 has `sub bolt = Bolt(length: auto)`, examples/anisotropic_bar.ri has `let tip_load = PointLoad(point: ...)`) the line starts with `sub`, rfind(':') finds the argument colon, and the text after it contains no `=`, so the context is TypePosition and the user is offered only type and structure names instead of members, builtins and expression keywords. Only the text after the LAST colon is checked for `=`, so the earlier `=` is ignored. No determine_context test covers a named argument (the tests cover only `param x:` and `let x:`). Other consequences of the same approach: a `.` inside a string or comment gives DotAccess, comparison operators (`<=`, `==`) count as the Expression `=`, and the `cursor_in_line > eq_pos` check is always true. Multi-line expressions lose context because only the cursor line is read. [Merged same-key finding lsp-walkers.7: Heuristic 11 and 10 (a completeness invariant over walkers that is enforced by a bound-to-underscore pattern, not by a check). sub_direct_exprs destructures SubDecl exhaustively and deliberately binds `derivation: _` ('A-beta must wire both together rather than inherit either silently'). SubDerivation carries expressions and references the grammar already produces today: `prototype: SpannedIdent` (the sibling sub `a` in `mirror of a`), `kind: Mirror{plane: Expr} | Image{transform: Expr}`, `param_overrides[*].value` and `.guard`, `dispositions[*].using_plane`, and `members: Vec<MemberDecl>` (let and constraint members). None are visited by collect_uses, cursor_on_member_segment, collect_bindings_in_scope, for_each_child_scope or the type-name collector, and reify-ast's own member walkers also skip `derivation.members` (documented). Consequence: find-references and rename on sub `a` or on the let used as the `across`/`under` operand omit the derived sub's use, so rename leaves `sub b = mirror of a2 across P` pointing at a name that no longer exists, and that buffer re-parses clean. The deferral is tied to #6616 (compile semantics, pending), but reference collection does not depend on elaboration. The explicit `_` is a good tripwire for the compiler error but is not a reminder to anyone who edits the LSP later.]
findings.proposal: Immediate fix (effort low): compute TypePosition only when the colon is the declaration's name/type separator, i.e. the first top-level ':' after the declared name and before any '=' or '(' on the line; add RED tests for `sub s = Foo(a: |`, `let x = f(a: |`, and `constraint c(x: |`. Systemic fix: take the context from the parse tree (the enclosing member's AST node and the cursor's position relative to its `type_expr`, `default`/`value` expression spans, and MemberAccess object span), the same CursorTarget as finding 4, so completion, hover and goto agree about 'type position' and 'dot access'. DotAccess would then derive from a MemberAccess whose member segment holds the cursor, and string/comment cursors return no completions. Relation: not covered by tooling-front-end.md (no leaf names completion's context); fk-419ebb996480/#6012 covers only the builtin signature table. [Also from lsp-walkers.7: Make the derived clause part of the shared direct-expression enumeration (finding 1): `MemberDecl::for_each_direct_expr` yields `kind`'s operand expression, each override value and guard, and `using_plane`; `child_scopes` yields `derivation.members`. In the LSP add the prototype SpannedIdent as a Sub-name use in collect_uses and collect_bindings_in_scope. Add RED tests (rename of sub `a` and of the plane let must touch the `mirror of a across P` text). Relation: not covered. #6616 owns compile semantics only, and S9's walker work (reify-ast) would absorb the traversal half.]
findings.bug_history_link: speculative (no fix history; coverage gap in tests)
findings.verdict_notes: sub_direct_exprs destructures SubDecl exhaustively and binds `derivation: _`. Its comment defers derivation expressions and members to #6616. Derivation expressions and members are therefore not visited by this iterator, which collect_uses uses. I did not check every walker, nor that the grammar already produces these forms.

findings.title: language-pipeline/test-support-eval-engine-eval-compiler-geometry-modify-spec-conformance.1
findings.statement: Handling of a per-scope solve outcome has six hand-maintained arms, and they implement different step sets. The arms are: Engine::eval single-scope, Engine::dispatch_merged_cluster_solve, Engine::eval_cached single-scope, Engine::dispatch_merged_cluster_solve_cached, and engine_edit.rs's edit_param and edit_source solver blocks. Only the two cold arms do these steps: call solve_ranked_with_dispatch and emit W_SOLVER_OPTIMALITY_UNPROVEN, record objective_provenance, run materialize_dependent_cells (the joint-drive write-back its doc calls the PRD section 6.3 PRIMARY INVARIANT), emit E_OBJECTIVE_UNCONSUMED, record undef-cause solve failures, and stamp SnapshotProvenance::Resolution. All four warm/edit arms omit every one of these. The auto(free) non-uniqueness warning has a shared helper (push_merged_cluster_nonunique_warnings) used by 2 arms, while the other 4 inline the identical format string. Solver-value write-back is Started/Completed-journaled on the cold arms and a bare cache record with no journal on eval_cached. governing_objective's doc nevertheless asserts eval and eval_cached build a 'byte-identical solver invariant'. The arms are not copies of one another (code similarity 0.23 to 0.36), so the divergence is in what each arm does, not in its spelling.
findings.bug_history_link: re-observed from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes:
[recovered from the anchor-shape drop; re-verified in phase 4] Opened crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs (eval single-scope 6250-6620, dispatch_merged_cluster_solve 7603-8083, eval_cached 8084+ and 9130-9375, dispatch_merged_cluster_solve_cached 9642-9957, governing_objective 3825-3860) and engine_edit.rs (module doc 1-140, solver blocks near 1802 and 4156). Ran git grep for each step function, a difflib re-measurement of the similarity figures, and greps for documentation of the warm/cold divergence. — The structure is real. Both cold arms call solve_ranked_with_dispatch, optimality_unproven_finding, objective_unconsumed_finding, materialize_dependent_cells, record_failed_autos and stamp SnapshotProvenance::Resolution, and no warm or edit arm does. The two cold-only callers of materialize_dependent_cells and objective_unconsumed_finding match the repo-wide grep. The nonunique helper is used by 2 arms, and the format string is inline in 4 (engine_eval.rs 6430 and 9267, engine_edit.rs 1847 and 4196). The three try_fast_path / is_dirty copies in eval_cached are at the cited lines. The weight of the next_change scenario is overstated, and the single-scope similarity figure is not reproduced.

(1) 'Neither file records whether the absence is intentional, except a journal-only census' is materially wrong. engine_edit.rs's module doc lists eight legs, not journal legs only, and calls legs 6-7 (resolved_params, objective_provenance) 'a deliberate, documented divergence, not drift'. engine_eval.rs ~8050 says 'NOT MIRRORED ONTO THE WARM PATHS, deliberately' for E_OBJECTIVE_UNCONSUMED. engine_eval.rs 9724-9750 and ~9002 call the solve()-versus-solve_ranked split and the cold-only W_SOLVER_OPTIMALITY_UNPROVEN a 'Documented, PERMITTED cold/warm divergence'. A pinning test exists: merged_cluster_solve.rs:2141 eval_vs_eval_cached_merged_cluster_objective_cluster_may_diverge_by_solve_entrypoint. The record_failed_autos / undef-cause step belongs to the capture_undef_causes feature, which is eval()-only. So 4 of the 6 listed steps already have recorded intent and a pin. Only the materialize_dependent_cells warm gap and the Resolution-provenance gap are not clearly recorded.

(2) The 'byte-identical solver invariant' quote concerns solver INPUT. governing_objective's doc says both paths 'build identical ResolutionProblem inputs', and the warm merged dispatch builds the same problem via the same build_merged_solver_problem. The statement presents it as an output-parity claim that contradicts the arms.

(3) The similarity measure is half-reproduced. Merged matches exactly (266/158, 76 matched, 0.358). Single-scope gives 0.355 over the stated ranges (221 cold lines, 151 warm lines, 66 matched), not 0.234 (104 warm lines). The conclusion that the arms are not copies still holds.

(4) The edit_param and edit_source arms are compared with eval's Resolution provenance, but edit entry points carry their own provenance semantics. That makes the 'drift' reading weaker for those two.

The duplication and coordination cost (H11/H3) stands, but the 'agent cannot tell intent from drift' cost is largely already paid down by in-code notes and a pinning test.

findings.title: tooling.11
findings.statement: Completion advertises 96 builtin functions from a hand-written table of signature and doc strings, with no parity link to the compiler. reify-lsp does not depend on reify-builtins, and only 3 of the 96 names appear in the registry's seeded rows today. The builtin-signature-registry PRD measured 35 LSP signatures that the type checker contradicts and owns the fix (its success table, row 12). findings.title: stateless.1
findings.statement:
Engine::check's verdicts for three constraint families depend on which other public Engine calls ran before it, not on its arguments.

Three check-time passes read Engine side tables that only other public surfaces populate:
- dispatch_constraints reads achieved_repr_tol. That table is written only by tessellate_realizations or tessellate_snapshot, and only after set_capture_repr_tol(true). An empty table turns every RepresentationWithin into Indeterminate.
- measure_dfm_rules and measure_gdt_conformance inject kernel handles from realization_handles. That table is written only by the Build/BuildSnapshot surfaces and cleared only at the next Build entry.

check's rustdoc states the required sequence: callers 'must call set_capture_repr_tol(true) followed by tessellate_realizations(&compiled) before calling check()', and DFM needs a subject 'realized by a prior build() call'. The sequence is spelled at exactly 1 of the 6 non-test check() call sites: reify-cli cmd_check's no-purpose arm (main.rs 907-918). The other five silently get Indeterminate or no DFM/GD&T measurement: the CLI --purpose arm, reify-lsp analysis.rs and diagnostics.rs, GUI EngineSession::check_with_solve_slot, and GUI preview.

In the GUI, check runs before that reload's tessellate_snapshot. It also runs right after reset_geometry_for_reload, which resets the kernels and the realization cache but not realization_handles. So check-time DFM/GD&T can only see handles left by an earlier export build, which now dangle (InvalidReference → Indeterminate, thanks to OCCT's monotonic ids). reset_geometry_for_reload's own contract ('exactly once per whole-file reload … never on a slider edit') is kept only by its single GUI call placement (engine.rs 1556).
findings.bug_history_link: re-observed from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: Read engine_constraints.rs check() rustdoc (2325-2390), dispatch_constraints, unmeasured_reason (880-922), representation_within_indeterminate_reason (925-935), measure_dfm_rules (1805-1850); engine_admin.rs reset_geometry_for_reload/clear_realization_cache; cli main.rs 890-1005; lsp analysis.rs 116/183, diagnostics.rs Engine::new sites; gui engine.rs 343 (cfg(test)), 1536-1556, 4780-4803, 5336+; git grep set_capture_repr_tol. — The coupling is real. check()'s DFM and GD&T passes read realization_handles, and RepresentationWithin reads achieved_repr_tol. Both are filled only by other public calls. reset_geometry_for_reload does not touch realization_handles. The weight is overstated in three ways. (1) The '1 of 6 call sites does the protocol' count is wrong. The LSP (analysis.rs:116, diagnostics.rs:337/909) and the GUI preview engine (engine.rs:4797) are built with Engine::new(checker, None), deliberately kernel-less. The CLI main.rs:1001 arm is the lightweight path, taken only when the module has no repr/DFM/GD&T/geometry. The GUI engine.rs:343 call is #[cfg(test)]. None of those can be wrong-order callers, because there is nothing to measure. (2) 'Silently Indeterminate' and 'nothing catches it' overstate the case. The RepresentationWithin Indeterminate carries an explicit MeasurementUnavailable reason from unmeasured_reason(). It separates three cases: no kernel; surface does not measure ('run reify check'); no tessellation ran. The empty-map semantics are documented as the C1 design. (3) The GUI session has its own post-geometry path, which tessellate_snapshot runs and then upgrade_indeterminate_verdicts. The real residue is narrower: the kernel-backed GUI session's check-time DFM/GD&T cannot see handles, and the sequence lives in rustdoc plus cmd_check's inline ordering.

findings.title: language-pipeline/eval-resolve-order-eval-lib-compiler-annotations-compute-contract-eval-g.9
findings.statement:
Nine geometry-kind enums in types.rs each carry a hand-maintained private `const ALL: [Self; N]` and a `pub const VARIANT_COUNT = Self::ALL.len()`. The enums are PrimitiveKind, BooleanOp, ModifyKind, TransformKind, PatternKind, SweepKind, CurveKind, ProfileKind and SurfaceKind. Each also carries a copy of the same ~10-line 'Maintenance contract' doc paragraph, which says ALL is 'the single source of truth' and 'cannot independently drift'.

Nothing ties ALL to the enum. Adding a variant compiles with ALL and VARIANT_COUNT unchanged; only the exhaustive Display match forces an edit. The downstream registry-completeness locks (`geometry_modify` CASES assert, reify-eval `compile_geometry_op_registry_completeness`, `compile_geometry_op_characterization`) compare against the stale count and pass. So the tripwire fails in exactly the case it exists for.

reify-compiler already depends on strum, and reify-core already derives `strum::EnumCount` for TypeDiscriminants.
findings.bug_history_link: re-observed from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: grep -c on types.rs for 'const ALL: [Self;' and 'Maintenance contract'; PrimitiveKind block 1500-1560; geometry_ops/tests.rs 28190-28210; strum in Cargo.toml — 9 hand-maintained ALL arrays and 9 duplicated 'Maintenance contract' paragraphs reproduced. The ALL arrays do not tie to the enum, since an added variant still compiles with ALL and VARIANT_COUNT unchanged. The registry completeness lock compares a separate hand-written ALL_PRIMITIVE against VARIANT_COUNT, so both stay stale together. strum is available in reify-compiler. Weakened: the scenario that a new kind can ship without a registry row or characterization case is not shown. I did not check whether the compile/dispatch code matches exhaustively on the kind enums, in which case the compiler would force the row.

findings.title: cg-ck.3
findings.statement: Engine::check runs eval() and then three check-time passes: dispatch_constraints' RepresentationWithin interception, measure_gdt_conformance and measure_dfm_rules. Their verdicts are read from Engine fields that eval() never writes or clears. achieved_repr_tol is written only by tessellate_realizations and cleared only on the Tessellate* surfaces. realization_handles is written by build and cleared only on the Build/BuildSnapshot surfaces (engine_build.rs reset match: the 'build<->tessellate asymmetry'). capture_repr_tol is set by a separate setter. check()'s own doc states the ordering contract: callers must call set_capture_repr_tol(true) then tessellate_realizations before check(). measure_dfm_rules is a no-op unless a prior build() stamped realization_handles. A check() after an edit without a fresh build injects handles from the previous build, keyed by RealizationNodeId, into the GD&T and DFM measurements.
findings.bug_history_link: re-observed from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: [recovered from the anchor-shape drop; re-verified in phase 4] Opened engine_constraints.rs (Engine::check at 2352 with its doc; measure_dfm_rules at 1793; measure_gdt_conformance at 2043; dispatch_constraints capture_repr_tol branch at ~912). Opened engine_build.rs reset_per_build_state (3267-3370). Grepped crates/reify-eval/src and crates/reify-cli/src for writes and clears of realization_handles and achieved_repr_tol. Read the CLI check arm in reify-cli/src/main.rs (~900-1001). — The structure reproduces. check() calls eval() and then three passes. measure_dfm_rules and measure_gdt_conformance read self.realization_handles, which only build() inserts into (engine_build.rs:9953) and only the Build and BuildSnapshot surfaces clear. dispatch_constraints reads achieved_repr_tol and capture_repr_tol. The only non-test writers are geometry_ops.rs:13219 on the tessellate path and the set_capture_repr_tol setter. Nothing in eval() or the edit path writes or clears any of them, so a check() after an edit can see handles from the previous build. check()'s own doc states the ordering contract, and the CLI hand-sequences realize_for_check, tessellate_realizations and then check. Mitigations exist but do not cover the claim. The reset match is exhaustively destructured and type-enforced, and unit tests pin the build/tessellate asymmetry. Those tests cover which surface clears which field, not check()'s hidden dependence on call order. Task #5973 is already named as owner for pushing the post-realization re-check into check(), which acknowledges the seam. The statement's 'only end-to-end tests would catch it' is slightly overstated, since the reset asymmetry has unit tests. That does not change the claim's weight.

findings.title: language-pipeline/syntax-ts-parser-eval-engine-edit-compiler-type-resolution-compiler-geom.5
findings.statement: Type-expression resolution varies on two independent axes: substitution or not, and full Type vs DimensionVector result. Each combination has its own hand-written function: resolve_type_alias_expr, resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst, resolve_type_alias_expr_to_dimension and resolve_type_alias_expr_to_dim_with_subst, plus the builtin pair resolve_parameterized_builtin_type and resolve_parameterized_builtin_type_with_subst. The 12-name parameterized-builtin table is therefore written four times: is_parameterized_builtin_name, two independent 12-arm `match name` blocks, and the drift-guard test list. The two builtin matchers have diverged. The base resolver's Scalar, Vector3 and Point3 arms classify dimension-param slots (classify_dim_slot, about 30 lines each, emitting DimParamKind). The subst variant's arms go straight to the dimension resolver. The drift test pins only the predicate's name set, so an arm added to or changed in one matcher is not caught in the other.
findings.bug_history_link: re-observed from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: At a030ee7528 I located the function spans in type_resolution.rs, ran difflib over the two builtin resolvers, listed the arm heads of both, and read is_parameterized_builtin_name and the canonical-set test. — The builtin pair gives ratio 0.53 and 57 lines in runs of 4 or more, as stated. Both matchers have the same 12 string arms. The base resolver (3805-4067) uses classify_dim_slot/DimSlotClass in the Scalar, Vector3 and Point3 arms (3 classify_dim_slot references); the subst variant (4111-4283) has none. The predicate and the test list are the other two copies. The test pins only the predicate's name set. I did not re-run the to_dimension pair ratio (0.82).

findings.title: cg-ck.2
findings.statement: Engine names its kernels by String, and the production constructor files its picked adapter under the sentinel string Engine::DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME ("__reify_eval_default_kernel"). Engine::with_registered_kernel is that constructor, used by reify-cli cmd_check/cmd_build and the GUI. The sentinel encodes a construction mode, not a kernel. Production code branches on it in engine_build.rs (`default_kernel_name == Engine::DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME` selects backward-compat fallback vs NoKernelChain) and in realization_content.rs::resolve_realization_kernel, where a canonical-name miss falls back to the sentinel. Because the sentinel resolves to nothing in the static registry, the engine cannot ask its own kernel's CapabilityDescriptor. Task 6169 therefore added Engine::repr_capable_kernel: Option<bool>, recorded by two constructors, plus a registry fallback with a benefit-of-the-doubt rule. Explaining why the lookup cannot work takes 64 doc lines on has_repr_capable_kernel and unmeasured_reason.
findings.bug_history_link: re-observed from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: [recovered from the anchor-shape drop; re-verified in phase 4] Opened engine_admin.rs (DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME def at 210, insert at 232, record writes at 993 and 1128), engine_build.rs:8627, realization_content.rs:335-360, engine_constraints.rs:834-1030, lib.rs:1138-1153. Ran git grep for DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME and 'repr_capable_kernel =', and an awk count of /// runs in engine_constraints.rs. Checked that GeometryKernel (reify-ir/src/geometry.rs:4542) is the behavioural trait and that with_registered_kernel is used by the GUI main.rs:875. — The structural claim holds. The sentinel is a construction-mode marker. with_registered_kernel files its pick under it through with_prelude. The descriptor is unreachable afterwards. repr_capable_kernel is recorded as the workaround. The production-sentinel count reproduces, as does the number of writes. Three details are off. (a) realization_content.rs does not fall back to the sentinel on a canonical-name miss. It falls back to self.default_kernel_name, and the sentinel is only the unwrap_or default when that is None. (b) Only the with_registered_kernel write (engine_admin.rs:993) compensates for the unreachable descriptor. The with_registered_kernels write at 1128 keys by real registry names. Its own comment says a registry scan would also answer correctly there, and it records the value for uniformity. So '2 compensating writes' overstates the count. (c) The 64-doc-lines figure is exactly has_repr_capable_kernel's own docs (lines 941-1004). unmeasured_reason's 'Why capability' section (857-905, about 49 lines) is about a different rationale, that manifold always registers so default_kernel_name.is_none() is never true. It is not about the sentinel workaround. The measurement's rule is ambiguous and the statement merges two unrelated rationales into one workaround cost. The next_change scenario is plausible, and the failure mode is real and documented.

findings.title: language-pipeline.8
findings.statement: Comments in geometry.rs's production region (59% comment lines) record task-progress facts that later commits have made false, and the worst of them invert the point of truth. (1) GEOMETRY_OP_DESCRIPTORS' doc says it covers 'all 49 GeometryOp variants' (there are 55 rows and 55 variants). It also says its operation/parent_role columns are an 'unverified copy until L2 rewires geometry_op_to_operation and parent_handles_for_op … cross-check against the source functions when modifying either'. L2 has landed (7e0f2e0e5b, 4cdda71204): both functions now read this table. (2) ParentRole's doc still says 'see parent_handles_for_op for the authoritative source'. (3) FeatureId::content_hash_bytes is `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a comment that its only caller is the golden test; value.rs:2074 calls it in production. (4) TopologyAttributeTable::lookup_result_face says its production caller (#4263) 'has not landed yet'; reify-kernel-manifold kernel.rs:1211 calls it. (5) A `G-allow` marker on capability_kind cites task #3623 as done. Fix history on the file confirms the cost: 19 of 87 non-merge commits since 2026-07-06 are prose maintenance.
findings.bug_history_link: re-observed from review-all-reify-20261010
findings.verdict_notes: Read geometry.rs 1276-1372 (descriptor table doc and ParentRole doc), 2413 (G-allow), 5392-5406 (content_hash_bytes allow(dead_code)), 5922-5935 (lookup_result_face); read engine_build.rs:1891-1915 and 2184-2195; read value.rs:2074; git grep lookup_result_face callers; measured the comment share; counted prose-maintenance commits. — All 5 falsified comments reproduce. The doc says 'all 49 variants' and 'unverified copy until L2', but parent_handles_for_op and geometry_op_to_operation now read GEOMETRY_OP_DESCRIPTORS via descriptor_for (engine_build.rs:18, 1910, 2023, 2190), so the table is authoritative. ParentRole's doc still calls parent_handles_for_op 'the authoritative source'. FeatureId::content_hash_bytes (geometry.rs:5402, allow(dead_code), 'only caller is golden test') is called in production at value.rs:2074. lookup_result_face 'has not landed yet' is contradicted by reify-kernel-manifold kernel.rs:1211. The G-allow at geometry.rs:2413 cites '#3623 (done)'. Comment share of geometry.rs lines 1-6402 is 3636/6171 = 0.589. Prose-maintenance commits since 2026-07-06 reproduce at 17 of 87 under my regex, against the finding's 19, so roughly consistent.

chains.name: Tree vocabulary restated per consumer (CST → AST → compiler → LSP)
chains.description: One root cause seen from three sides. The grammar's child-kind sets (node-types.json, regenerated every build, read by no crate — verified: only the generate/freshness scripts reference it) and the AST's child enumeration (reify-ast has walk_members but no Expr::for_each_child — verified) are restated as hand-written string matches and ExprKind/MemberDecl matches in ts_parser.rs (seven body loops, `_ => None` defaults), in the compiler (S9 γ's member-support table; entity.rs/dot_chain_lint/shadow_lint child enumerations), and in reify-lsp (references.rs holds a third in-file copy; for_each_child_scope ends in `_ => {}`). Because names are bare Strings, the LSP adds a fourth restatement by rescanning source text (name_token_span, 11 callers). Each new kind, field or arm therefore lands as a fix commit per consumer: #5392→#6286→#7809/#8080/#8081/#8275 on the parser side (mined theme 'CST ERROR/MISSING swallowed'), #7999/#8042/#8071/#8195/#8203 on the compiler side ('silent-drop inside guarded blocks'), the index_domain/relate_relations/derivation walks and #7541 on the LSP side ('walkers miss newer variants'). fk-7173c189d7ea and S9 γ #8732 are the same commonMembers set dropped at two stages; fk-8d86383441a3 and fk-406a3917737c are the same missing child enumeration; fk-3553b78476b5/.2 are the missing module-level backstop that makes every per-arm refusal redundant rather than load-bearing.
chains.proposal: Derive the vocabulary once, downward. (1) reify-syntax: add `supertypes` to grammar.js so node-types.json carries subtype lists; one node-types.json contract test asserting each container's child kinds equal the lowering tables' handled set plus a reasoned exclusion list (absorbs #7676's grammar.js re-lexer); one `lower_member_list(container, &MemberListSpec)` shared by the seven body loops; one module-level `fault_backstop` at parse_with_prelude_enums so `root.has_error() ⇒ errors non-empty` holds by construction. (2) reify-ast: wildcard-free `Expr::for_each_child`, `MemberDecl::for_each_direct_expr` and `MemberDecl::child_scopes` built on MemberRecursionSet, consumed by reify-lsp and reify-compiler (entity.rs, dot_chain_lint, shadow_lint delete their copies); `SpannedIdent` for every declared and referenced name, populated at the single lowering site. S9 γ's member-support table and the parser's MemberListSpec share one kind vocabulary.
chains.routing: new stream (reify-syntax lowering contract: fk-3553b78476b5–.6; no review-all stream owns reify-syntax) + amend S9 (γ #8732 reads the shared kind vocabulary) + amend S27 (η #8772/#7860 become clients of the reify-ast primitives; fk-c008cdb5b456's SpannedIdent lands in reify-syntax lowering, consumed by χ #8756's decl_oracle). Why: the fix class recurs at every layer because the SPOT is upstream of all three, and only a stream that owns reify-syntax can place it.

chains.name: Type arguments and overload choice discarded at the compiler → eval boundary
chains.description: The compiler computes a sigma (type-param binding) and an overload choice as transient locals and records neither on the IR (verified: CompiledExprKind::UserFunctionCall carries only function_name and args; reify-expr::find_matching_compiled_function re-selects at eval; entities_phase::check_expr_fn_calls re-unifies). Generic structure monomorphization lives only inside the auto: resolver with a hand-picked field subset, so explicit instantiation never monomorphizes and TypeParam cells reach graph hydration. Downstream compensations: the eval-side tie-break doc and three parity fixes (esc-4093-152, #5685, #5686, pending #5992/#8586); the debug-only assert_value_cell_types_representable in engine_eval; the LSP's eval_guard::skip_reason containment wired at three sites (verified: analysis.rs:149, diagnostics.rs:271 and :902; task #6851), which fk-4034ccf5b655 shows is one of three copies of the compile+guard+check pipeline. Upstream of the binding, the arity decision itself has about ten homes with four policies (findings .1, .5, .6 are the same missing bind_type_args seen at three sites) and alias bodies are resolved by a second TypeExpr resolver (.4). The mined themes 'type args silently dropped' (16 tasks) and 'un-annotated types silently default' (10) are this chain's symptom census.
chains.proposal: One binding, recorded on the IR, with the concrete-template invariant enforced at two points. `bind_type_args(TypeArity, args) -> Result<Sigma, Diagnostic>` in a lower type_args module (absorbs #7337, #8229, #8098, probes a/c; reads S8-ο's PARAMETERIZED_BUILTIN_TYPES for builtin arity); `instantiate_template(&TopologyTemplate, Sigma)` in compile_builder/monomorph.rs with an exhaustive destructure, ValueCellId re-keying and `template_is_concrete` as the postcondition, called by both the auto phase and a new explicit-instantiation pass; graph hydration checks the same predicate always-on (closing #7225's option (a) and making the engine debug_assert and the LSP eval_guard redundant); `UserFunctionCall { callee: FnRef, type_args }` produced once by `bind_user_call`, so check_expr_fn_calls reads it and reify-expr dispatches on it (find_matching_compiled_function and #5992's parity test die; #8897's intrinsic stamp becomes a projection). The alias-body resolver collapses onto S7 μ's ResolutionCtx with a TypeParamEnv field.
chains.routing: new stream (generic instantiation and call binding: fk-4bd738a79576–.6), with amendments to S8 ο #8903 (arity column feeds bind_type_args), S7 μ #8643 (TypeParamEnv on ResolutionCtx), S8 ζ #8897 (stamp derived from callee), and S27 β #8761 (the containment predicate becomes the hydration-side check). Why: #6853/#7225/#5992 are site fixes on three different crates; no review-all stream owns type substitution, and the eval and LSP compensations only come out once the compiler records the binding.

chains.name: A realized step's facets kept in parallel bare-id containers from the kernel to the cache
chains.description: The fact 'this realized body has handle H on kernel K, repr R, egress body E, swept kind S, attribute entries A' is split across containers at every layer. In the OCCT crate the repr is decoded from a C++ type-name string with `_ => Solid` (fk-d09e31d2ef9d) and kept in a second map beside the shape map, so three consumers each handle 'repr absent' differently (fk-2281cf9afc51; verified unwrap_or(Solid) at lib.rs 1203/1318). In reify-eval the executor keeps realization_step_ids/realization_step_reprs in lockstep and named_steps/named_step_reprs as sibling maps, and seeding writes only the handle half (fk-9d5be5dd1b72), SweptKindTable is keyed by bare GeometryHandleId although #4351 re-keyed its sibling by KernelHandle (fk-da0908f1437e), and the realization cache stores a bare terminal handle, so the hit path hand-rebuilds the repr, a cross-build VolumeMeshSources map was added by #6308 for the egress body, and swept-kind/attribute facets are simply absent on a hit (fk-a1dbdb4e699e; verified evict_family never touches volume_mesh_sources). Value::GeometryHandle carries a bare Option<GeometryHandleId> (#6366), so every value-started egress re-derives the owner. Which fields of an op are parents is a fifth restatement (fk-abfd068e9631). The mined 'geometry handle and kernel ownership' and 'kernel result-representation stamping' themes (14 + 7 fixes) are this chain; the S11 §1 probes (translate re-stamps Compound as Solid) are the string-decode end surfacing at the eval end.
chains.proposal: One typed realized-step value carried end to end. OCCT: `shape_kind` FFI returns a cxx shared enum (exhaustive on both sides, no Solid default), and ShapeStore (S11 ε) stores `Entry { shape, repr }` so 'repr absent' is unrepresentable. Eval: `RealizedStep { handle: KernelHandle, repr }` (S2 ε's RealizedTerminal) as the element of the executor's step list and the value of named_steps and module_named_steps; SweptKindTable keyed by KernelHandle; `CachedRealization { terminal, repr, egress_body, swept_kind, attribute_entries }` as the cache value with one `apply_realized` writer shared by hit and miss, so INV-BUILD-3 holds by construction and volume_mesh_sources is deleted rather than moved; `GeometryOp::parents()/parents_mut()` as the single exhaustive home for parent fields.
chains.routing: amend S2 (ε #9157 widened from the oracle to named_steps/module_named_steps; δ #9158's CacheHit widened to CachedRealization; β₁ #9154 converts the OR-matches to parents() in its move) + amend S11 (ζ #8669 rests on the enum classifier; ε #8682 stores one Entry) + amend S1 (λ #9050 drops volume_mesh_sources instead of relocating it; ε #9043 re-keys SweptKindTable in its move). Why: every leaf already touches these exact functions as verbatim moves; the typed value is a one-line change to each leaf's contract, and splitting it across three streams is only legitimate because the value type lives in reify-ir below all three.

chains.name: 'Which constraint reaches which auto, over which domain' derived separately by eval walks and solver miners
chains.description: The compiler mints instance-path-keyed Auto decls with no default_expr, so reify-eval bridges two id namespaces by string normalisation inside each read walk; six walks then answer 'does C reach auto A' with six edge sets (fk-a5a65ab8428c), CellReadIndex builds forward and reverse separately with the bridge restated at three insert sites (fk-a5237570b374), and within reify-constraints two functions both named collect_value_refs traverse with different rules (fk-227058959fa6, still open). Because the eval problem builders never populate AutoParam.bounds (verified None at engine_eval.rs:1953 and engine_edit.rs:1708/4034) the solver grew a private constraint-derived interval miner re-run 3+K times per resolution, cpsat's Int arm reads only the empty field so engine Int autos are never enumerable (#6755), and strictness is compensated by two clamp-box policies because the acceptance predicate is a hand-rolled residual inclusive at strict bounds (fk-622678f17117). The engine then strips `__connector_`-prefixed autos by string prefix to dodge the solver's ConstraintNonUnique verdict (verified engine_eval.rs ~1688-1731), and detect_underdetermined is a third determinedness producer. The #5467 series (four fixes plus three escalations), #6307/#7069/#6649 false W_UNDERDETERMINED, #7883/#6465/#5618/#5711 bound fixes are all this chain.
chains.proposal: Two typed carriers computed once. (a) `AutoReach` built from S3's DependencyGraph (CellReadIndex folds onto a `template_reads()` projection keyed by InstancePath::structure_scope with alias edges, so reverse == transpose by construction) and queried by the problem builder, detect_underdetermined, compute_clusters and constraints_reaching_auto; invariant: W_UNDERDETERMINED fires iff the builder admitted no constraint for the auto. (b) `ParamDomain { Endpoint::{Open,Closed} with BoundSource, integrality, finite }` in a reify-constraints `domain` module, produced once per component by `derive_domains` (today's miner, later #6655's HC4) replacing AutoParam.bounds; every reader is a projection (seed_box, clamp_box, int_range, default_bounded_sides). Acceptance calls the checker's Kleene predicate (`leaf_verdicts`), so strict bounds and NaN are rejected uniformly. The connector-prefix strip becomes a typed 'determined elsewhere' mark the builder sets.
chains.routing: amend S3 (δ #8691 gains template_reads/alias edges; ι #8704 canonical spelling) + amend S4 (κ #8868 and ν #8860 become AutoReach queries rather than pure moves; ζ #8867) + amend S14 (ξ #8653 introduces the domain module; cpsat reads it) with edges to solver-driver-parity β #6690, #6655, #5470, #6692, #6653, #9012; fk-227058959fa6 attaches to the same S14 leaf. Why: four streams already own the moves; what is missing is the shared carrier each move should target, and that is an amendment to leaves not yet started, not a new stream.

chains.name: Solve outcome flattened to text and re-interpreted per eval path, with parity twins paying each fix twice
chains.description: The solver flattens typed causes (ObjectiveAbstention, Determinedness) to `NoProgress { reason: String }` and `Infeasible` at the crate boundary (verified solver.rs 3129/3226/3280); reify-eval re-wraps them as the literal "infeasible" or `format!("no progress: {reason}")` in record_failed_autos (fk-025e984ea962) and interprets SolveResult at six arms that have drifted — record_failed_autos only on the cold arms, pinned-connector write on four of six, the ranked→plain downgrade copied three times (fk-3f8966182829; verified). Two of those arms exist only because eval_cached is a 1,900-line parity twin whose sole production caller (reify-lsp, unchanged content, no solver, no kernel) reduces it to replaying the last cold eval (fk-2bec945fda6e), and the MCP set_parameter path compensates for edit_param not persisting the user pin with a second call that invalidates what edit_param just committed and dirties a map only eval_cached reads (fk-95335511ba08; verified mcp_context.rs ~603). #5240/#5238/#2259/#2266/#8028/#7038 (eval vs eval_cached), #6707's five byte-identical warning sites and P3's 'solve failed: infeasible' are this chain.

chains.name: Compute outcome contract unenforced, supports realized per trampoline, results echo options
chains.description: reify-compute-contract documents 'Completed.diagnostics are non-fatal' and nothing enforces it (verified dispatch.rs:75; modal_ops.rs: 49 Completed constructions, 0 Failed), so every modal-family error returns Completed with fabricated zeros, run_compute_dispatch caches that value, and the transient trampoline grew modal_result_missing_outcome (#4131) to re-detect upstream failure from the value's shape (.2). Support realization — which DOFs of which nodes a declared support constrains — has five homes with different vocabularies (box faces in modal, "root" string in elastic dims, kind-blind union on the realized path, hard-coded pin-pin in buckling that discards the supports argument, and the solver crate's own SupportKind policy never built with Pinned), so modal silently constrains nothing for "root" or an unknown kind while echoing the raw options list as applied (.1, .3). Result builders choose Undef/0.0/[] by hand per builder (.4) and multi-case results are Value::Map{"cases"} that the GUI key-sniffs (.5). chains.routing: amend S5 (the completion-hook check on #8674/#8679's ComputeDispatchRegistry descriptor) + amend S15 (γ #8683 rejects unknown kinds; ζ #8693 builds typed parts; C5 adds the two multi-case structures; PVAC #7100 drops the degenerate-builder dispositions) + amend S16 (ξ #9120 and μ #9119 become calls into the shared realization module; ο #9121 hosts it; #7081's buckling port becomes a call).
